Codex completed-turn watchdog recovery uses a redacted rollout snapshot: the last eight response_item summaries plus the latest event_msg task_started/task_complete marker. Recovery requires an active run, stale Codex child session, no pane safety block, a fully parseable transcript, and task_complete older than the run's base idle timeout. Fresh completion suppresses intervention during the grace window; completed-turn continuation precedes reasoning recovery and counts toward the bounded idle-reprompt budget. IdleCheckHandler owns scan/order policy, while WatchdogRecoveryCoordinator owns completed-turn recovery state and execution.

Security rule: permission and plan-approval timeouts must fail closed. Timeout must clear pending approval, report a distinct timeout outcome, and interrupt or cancel the provider flow rather than implicitly approving work. Rule YAML and update payloads cross a shared boundary at split_rule_definition_data in src/gobby/workflows/definitions.py. Runner degradation invariant after #16609 and #18371: GobbyRunner initializes degraded_services as a set before runner_init phases. The stderr resource monitor uses stderr_capture_over_limit and leaves the live capture file intact because safe rotation requires coordinated descriptor reopening (#12010/#13910). Features absent by configuration are not recorded as degraded.

Transcript index sidecars include session_id in the persisted payload and load validation, so callers that know the session should pass session_id to load_index_sidecar/get_or_build_index to prevent cross-session cache reuse.

Take proper care with every task. Don't rush or try to burn through tasks. Rely on the Gobby daemon to manage context (compaction, session persistence). Quality over speed.

Each call recomputes `include_merge_stage = opts.isolation in {worktree, clone} and not opts.no_merge` (src/gobby/build/task_lifecycle.py:154) and re-runs cascade_build_state_to_subtree, so a later tick that omits the flag cascades merge stages across a full-lifecycle subtree.

FIXED 2026-07-27 (task #19056, commit 75fb9f7d9) — derive_child_manifest_specs (src/gobby/storage/tasks/_stage_manifest.py) now gates the merge append on at least one derived work stage (`if stage_names and ("merge" in by_name or include_merge_stage)`). Before the fix, development/epic_qa/pr were each appended only if present in the parent manifest but merge was appended unconditionally, so an expansion-only parent gave every child a merge-only manifest at position 0 — which the dispatcher correctly read as a ready first stage and dispatched a merge-orchestrator against never-worked tasks (observed on epic #19018). The same commit stopped cascade_build_state_to_subtree (src/gobby/storage/tasks/_build_cascade.py) treating an empty derivation as a per-task failure: an expansion-only build has no per-child lifecycle, so it now skips manifest initialization and still propagates allow_automation/unattended/isolation. Omitting `--no-merge` on an expansion-only build is therefore no longer harmful, but it is still required to keep merge off a full-lifecycle subtree.

Recovery if a build does dispatch unwanted work: `gobby build stop <ref>` halts automation and cancels spawned agents. Do not hand-delete task_stage_states merge rows — merge is the terminal stage, is inert once allow_automation is false, and is what you want present if the build later resumes.

In gobby-cli, the unified Obsidian vault contract for gwiki/gcode uses `code/` for gcode-generated codewiki pages, `knowledge/` for synthesized knowledge pages, and `_meta/` for shared metadata. gcode codewiki emits shared frontmatter keys such as `source`, `provenance`, `generated_by: gcode-codewiki`, `trust`, and `freshness`. Do not add or preserve legacy `wiki/**` compatibility paths when changing gwiki or codewiki.

Web session activity filters are persisted per effective project under `gobby-sessions-filters:<project-id>` (with `:all` for no project), preventing task-reference filters from leaking across projects.

Gobby codewiki truth_digest.json is generated deterministically without AI from build_system_model().services, stable ServiceKind::kind_slug() values, curated infrastructure descriptors, and structural_repo_summary counts. AI routing affects prose pages, not truth-digest infrastructure authority.

For ordinary Gobby memory VectorStore rebuilds, retain a compatible existing Qdrant collection: upsert regenerated vectors and delete stale point IDs only after successful upserts. Delete/recreate is reserved for embedding-dimension mismatch and is lifecycle-locked. Embedding-provider switches use the separate alias-backed staged-collection workflow.

Managed native-binary version parsing is centralized in src/gobby/install/version_probe.py. probe_native_bin_version extracts the numeric semantic version from decorated `--version` output (for example `ghook 0.4.5 (build abc)` -> `0.4.5`), and distribution._probe_helper_version delegates to it while passing distribution.subprocess.run to preserve the module's test seam.

Pipeline execution discovery is now fully exposed: list_pipeline_executions and search_pipeline_executions MCP tools on gobby-workflows server, CLI subcommands (gobby pipelines executions, gobby pipelines search), HTTP endpoint (GET /api/pipelines/executions/search). Storage layer search_executions() uses LEFT JOIN step_executions with LIKE-based text search across pipeline names and step errors/outputs. The previous API gap (no list/search without knowing execution ID) is closed.

Merge tooling bug fix #14888: gobby-merge verify_in_worktree(final=true) must enforce a clean git worktree after the verification command succeeds. Previously final verification ignored the final flag and allowed merge campaigns to record success with staged/dirty files. Commit 70f841d7e adds a post-command `git status --porcelain` check and returns dirty file details on failure while leaving non-final verification permissive.

Qwen typed JSON transcripts may report usage as tokens:{input, output, cached, thoughts, tool, total}. In gobby.sessions.token_usage.typed_json_token_usage, input includes cached tokens and maps to input_tokens=max(0,input-cached); cached maps to cache_read_tokens; output+thoughts maps to output_tokens; tool is excluded because it is a subset of input.

Web chat routing exposes addSystemMessage through ChatState so synchronous routing failures can surface visible local feedback. useChatPageSessionRouting validates a web-chat target against conversations.sessions before parking the current chat or dismissing the mobile panel; missing targets append a local system message and leave UI/session state unchanged.

For Gobby Droid/Factory transcript ingest, local transcripts are raw JSONL with a `session_start` record followed by `message` records containing `message.role` and typed `message.content` blocks. The Droid adapter must require `session_start` before claiming generic message rows, use `record.get("title")` for the generated session title, skip `visibility: "llm_only"` and `context-*` records, render `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks, and use `GWIKI_DROID_ARCHIVE_FIXTURE` for env-gated real-fixture validation.

LLMProvider base abstraction and bridge adapters were removed. Text capability routing now exposes native `ClaudeTextGenerateAdapter` and `LocalTextGenerateAdapter`; vision routing exposes `ClaudeVisionExtractAdapter` and `LocalVisionExtractAdapter`. Runtime code should use feature-routed AI capability adapters plus shared primitives like `LLMTextResult` and `LLMProviderCancellation`, not an `LLMProvider` ABC or generic LLMProvider bridge adapters.

Gobby build child-merge recovery: if a child task is stuck in merge because its source worktree metadata exists but the parent integration worktree DB row is missing, the intended repair is `gobby build <child-ref> --target-branch <target>`. The code now ensures/adopts the nearest parent integration workspace for child resume and workspace merge recovery instead of requiring a full epic rebuild.

FastAPI test patterns learned during coverage push:

1. isinstance with lazy imports: When route handlers do `from gobby.storage.database import LocalDatabase; isinstance(db, LocalDatabase)`, MagicMock fails. Fix: autouse fixture patching `gobby.storage.database.LocalDatabase` with `MagicMock` class so isinstance(MagicMock(), MagicMock) returns True.

2. Test directory naming conflicts: Never name a test directory after a Python package (e.g., tests/servers/routes/mcp/ clashes with the `mcp` package). Use `mcp_endpoints/` instead.

3. FastAPI dependency_overrides: Routes using Depends(get_server) need `app.dependency_overrides[get_server] = override_fn` instead of `create_X_router(mock_server)` pattern.

4. Exception re-wrapping: If a route catches HTTPException(503) inside a generic `except Exception`, it re-raises as 500. Check the actual handler logic when writing test assertions.

5. Installer backup-before-read order: copy2 (backup) runs before open (read), so making a file unreadable causes 'Failed to create backup' not 'Failed to read'.
Daemon restarts are allowed when needed. Before restarting, broadcast the expected MCP/tool interruption and recovery notice to all active agents and sessions, not only the current build selector.

Interactive and delegated planning-review rejection uses mark_task_review_rejected(task_id, rejection_notes, round_number=None). It returns the planning-review task to open and appends the round-scoped Adversary Findings heading automatically when round_number is supplied; rejection_notes must contain only finding bodies. Use this review-rejected/open round-trip contract rather than introducing a changes_requested status.

ACP auth in Gobby follows ACP 1.0 initialize authMethods plus agentCapabilities.auth.logout. Store advertised auth methods on the ACP client/session, call authenticate with the selected methodId, and call logout only when auth.logout is advertised. This remains separate from Gobby Plan/Act/YOLO chat_mode; auth UI belongs in existing session/chat controls, not a new Activity Panel.

Claude watchdog transcripts use assistant, user, and system records. A valid system subtype=turn_duration record with nonnegative integer durationMs/messageCount and a valid timestamp can mark completion; subsequent model output makes that completion non-conclusive. User tool_result records are diagnostic and do not start a turn. Assistant isApiErrorMessage=true maps to diagnostic provider_error_kind=api_error and never conclusive capacity. Keep raw content and error values out of WatchdogTranscriptSnapshot.

Gobby build config loading and profile resolution live in src/gobby/config/build.py. load_build_config merges BuildConfig defaults, ~/.gobby/build.yaml, <project_root>/.gobby/build.yaml, then flag overrides, normalizing clones_dir to Path and merging profiles by profile name. resolve_profile supports quick, review, full, full-yolo, and auto mappings: plan_file -> review, leaf/default -> quick, epic with plan -> full, epic without plan -> ValueError.

Task #18727 (commit 80f12cd87) extended review-learning taxonomy. SourceKind now includes plan_review and task_validation; SOURCE_KIND_DOMAIN is the total fail-closed source-to-domain map and CODE_DOMAIN_EXCLUDED_TAGS centralizes plan exclusion. Every newly normalized lesson receives lesson-domain:<code|plan>; check_key/category findings get explicit enumeration tags. Reserved plan-review and epic-qa pattern namespaces validate class-scoped pattern_id components against explicit kebab-case check_key (and plan category), while ReviewLearningService preserves existing record signatures and honors explicit class-scoped finding_fingerprint values so multi-class lessons have independent occurrence streams.

In /Users/josh/Projects/gobby, adding a new public SessionManager method through storage mixins also requires updating tests/storage/test_sessions_import.py EXPECTED_PUBLIC_METHOD_SIGNATURES; that test asserts the exact public SessionManager method surface.

Gobby Homebrew distribution mode is detected with `GOBBY_DISTRIBUTION=homebrew`. In that mode `gobby install` verifies `gcode`, `ghook`, and `gwiki` against `src/gobby/install/version_pins.py`, skips global npm installs and managed helper downloads. Helper resolution and Homebrew verification treat executable `~/.gobby/bin/<helper>` binaries that satisfy the managed pin as authoritative before falling back to Homebrew/PATH helpers.

Gobby's durable identity boundary is user -> machine -> session. The machines registry owns optional owner_user_id; sessions, tasks, agents, and memories should not gain scattered user_id columns. Session filtering uses machine_id. Placeholder IDs such as unknown, unknown-machine, none, and null are not registered; missing client machine_id instead uses a unique legacy-missing:<uuid> session-row sentinel, which is also excluded from machine-registry upserts.

All read-modify-write operations on a session_variables row must use transaction_immediate(SessionVariableMutation(session_id=...)) so PostgreSQL advisory locking serializes compact-continuation helpers with SessionVariableManager writers. This includes first-write INSERT paths, which otherwise can race into a unique violation.

`gobby build restart --no-resume` treats stage cap escalations as build-owned reset state. `_is_build_owned_escalation` includes reasons ending in `_max_work_attempts`, `_max_review_rounds`, `_work_failed:max`, and `_review_failed:max`, so paused manifest resets clear cap escalations like `development_max_work_attempts`.

Dispatcher agent-slot caps are global across projects. In src/gobby/dispatch/dispatcher.py, both the early candidate-loop check and the final SpawnAgentAction admission check call count_active_agents(db) without project_id; final admission uses AgentCapAdmission(project_id=None), which maps to the global agent_cap_admission:* advisory-lock key. Project-scoped count_active_agents remains available for observability/fairness reporting. Regression test test_concurrent_project_heartbeats_share_global_agent_cap in tests/dispatch/test_dispatcher.py runs heartbeats for two projects and proves global pending/running runs stay at the configured cap. Implemented by #15958 in commit 69cfc34e183caabefb72fca762ec5dc3a5c90f18.

Gobby web voice capture diagnostics use local browser console events prefixed `[gobby:voice]`. `useVoiceCapture.ts` logs VAD readiness and speech lifecycle (`vad_waiting`, `vad_start`, `vad_ready`, `vad_speech_start`, `vad_speech_end`, `vad_misfire`, `vad_error`), PTT lifecycle, and voice audio send attempts/results with request IDs, sample rate, payload size, WebSocket state, and only a short conversation prefix. PTT capture normalizes high-rate audio to 16 kHz before WAV encoding and blocks payloads over `VOICE_AUDIO_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES`.

Expansion runs have no restart recovery worker. Task #16358 added LocalExpansionRunManager.cleanup_stale_runs, which atomically fails running/applying rows older than 30 minutes. Daemon startup invokes it through DatabaseExecutor, and start_expansion_run_impl invokes a parent-task-scoped sweep before active-run reuse so a row that becomes stale after startup cannot permanently block re-expansion.

FalkorDB entity-memory linkage: Entities in FalkorDB get a common _Entity label (via SET after MERGE to avoid mismatch). When memories are created, entities are linked to (:Memory {memory_id}) nodes via MENTIONED_IN relationships. This enables graph-augmented search: vector search finds entities, MENTIONED_IN links resolve to memory IDs, and graph traversal finds related memories. Backfill via rebuild_knowledge_graph MCP tool passes memory_id to add_to_graph().

For Path B plan-keystroke capture, run the CLI's native interactive TUI rather than a Gobby-managed ACP or spawned-agent session, because managed ACP flows do not render the native approval menu. Capture in a disposable persistent tmux or in-process pty, use a genuine planning/action task, and validate only with the safe reject option before mapping approvals. Keystroke mappings must be empirically verified per CLI and menu shape; Claude’s full plan menu and bare confirmation menu require pane-aware resolution.

Plan-review approval keeps the reviewer round_result canonical and materializes a separate server-derived approval_result.quality_ledger. ReviewCheckpointService owns ledger derivation/finalization for normal, checkpoint reconciliation, restart recovery, and interactive-intent paths. Stage approval derives the ledger inside the outer transaction before stage mutation, then persists that exact ledger after stage mutation; this ordering preserves failure atomicity without violating DB lock acquisition order. Replay compares the raw approval payload after removing quality_ledger and separately verifies the delivered ledger against evidence.quality_ledger.

In Gobby Teams communications, `TeamsAdapter.verify_webhook` binds Bot Framework JWTs to the activity body by requiring decoded `serviceUrl` to be a HTTPS string equal to the activity `serviceUrl`. Mismatched replayed tokens are rejected before parsing stores ConversationReferences, preventing proactive sends to forged service URLs. Commit bf32ac121 for task #16011.

For GitHub-originated linked tasks, GitHub lifecycle reconciliation uses LocalTaskManager.reconcile_task_state: a remote close sets closed_at and closed_reason="github_sync", while a remote reopen clears close metadata. Outbound GitHub synchronization derives closed state with tasks.state_semantics.is_task_closed and must remain linked-task-only; unlinked local-native tasks must not create GitHub issues. Preserve existing label-mapping helpers when importing or pushing labels.

In Gobby communications, BaseChannelAdapter.initialize receives a synchronous secret_resolver callback. CommunicationsManager._init_adapter must resolve `$secret:` channel config refs with asyncio.to_thread before calling initialize, then serve both full `$secret:NAME` and bare `NAME` keys from an in-memory map; adapters such as Telegram may pass bare names after stripping the prefix.

During gobby build dogfood #15385/#15447, AgentLifecycleMonitor.refresh_active_run_dispatch_mutexes was changed to restore a dispatcher-held heartbeat mutex when an active task-bound agent run has no task_dispatch_mutex row. This prevents duplicate dispatch windows after a same-task helper clears a mutex while another active orchestrator/agent is still running.

Spawned tmux agents must persist child_session_id, pid, and tmux_session_name immediately after live-pane verification and before waiting for SessionStart registration. Otherwise registration timeouts can kill the pane while DB/MCP surfaces still report no terminal. Claude sandbox settings should omit optional proxy port keys when no proxy is configured; serializing httpProxyPort/socksProxyPort as JSON null triggers Claude /doctor settings warnings.

Force-graph ref-isolation pattern (2D reference implementation: web/src/components/activity/wiki/WikiForceGraph.tsx, #17764): react-force-graph re-applies props on parent re-render and destroys custom canvas objects, so graph components sit behind a memo wall whose equality checks only (dataRevision, theme, width, height, reducedMotion). Everything else crosses the wall through parent-owned MutableRefObjects: interaction state (hoverId, lowercased search) in an interactionRef read by nodeCanvasObject/linkColor accessors every frame, and callbacks in a handlersRef whose identity never changes. autoPauseRedraw={false} keeps force-graph's internal rAF repainting the accessors, so pointer-move causes zero React state updates (hover writes go through useRafCoalescedHandler). dataRevision is a composite string of requestKey + toggle bits + theme; token colors are baked into the scene once per build via resolveCssVar (pure builder in WikiGraphScene.ts takes an injectable resolver for tests). Gotchas: force-graph mutates link source/target from id strings into node objects at runtime (type endpoint extraction as unknown); the 2D package exposes no renderer()/pixelRatio API unlike the 3D exemplar; eslint react-hooks/immutability forbids render-time writes even to module-level '.current' objects in test mocks — capture props inside a useEffect. Backend graph include enum is {all, knowledge, code} (_GRAPH_INCLUDE_VALUES in src/gobby/servers/routes/wiki.py) — 'wiki' is not a value and 400s.

Project registration concurrency pattern: LocalProjectManager.ensure_exists uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING and returns the stored Project, which is appropriate when callers only need existence. Routes that must distinguish a newly created row from a concurrent duplicate should use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id; a returned row means success, while no row means fetch and return the existing project.

Task #19238 (commit 56cf79bfa) made close_task converge honestly for escalated tasks. increment_validation_failure now diagnoses zero-row updates as closed (closed error), already escalated (TaskAlreadyEscalatedError), or true staleness. MCP validation maps the already-escalated race to validation_failed. An escalated task skips only gate 10 when given non-whitespace override_justification; the close persists validation_override_reason, clears escalation through the existing storage exit ramp, and resets the failure count. Without justification it returns actionable task_escalated and does not invoke the reviewer. Close commit locking now compares a named fingerprint of gate-relevant task, child, claim-window, and attribution state while excluding benign updated_at/path-cache churn; commit and dirtiness checks use a fresh attribution snapshot.

Default-agent prompt-facing role, goal, personality, and instructions are injected from the first UserPromptSubmit/before_agent hook, not during SessionStart. SessionStart activates agent variables/rules/skills. Full startup/context-loss starts set _agent_context_injected=false and _agent_context_rehydrate_pending=true so the next prompt rehydrates once, then clears the pending marker. Daemon restart/reregister_active_sessions must not reset prompt injection flags; stale _agent_context_injected=false on sessions with prior message_count/turn_count is repaired to true without emitting another preamble. Persona switches still use _agent_identity_reinject=true for a one-time reinject. Implemented in commit 3dfba4be7 for task #17468.

Gobby agent messaging uses target-based `send_message(from_session, target, content, target_id=...)`, supporting session, agent, project, build, and all targets. `send_command` remains for ancestor-descendant control; peers use messages. Use `list_messages` or `get_inter_session_messages` for inspection, while `deliver_pending_messages` fetches undelivered messages and marks them delivered.

Task-scoped build controls remain publicly available from gobby.build. controls.py contains workflow orchestrators; control_runtime.py owns target resolution, cancellation, cleanup, and stage resets; restart_controls.py owns restart validation and recovery; results.py owns result serialization and history. Stop/resume toggle allow_automation while preserving unattended.

Gobby web MemoryTab search architecture after task #16818: non-empty queries call useMemory.searchMemories and render the server's searchResults, allowing hits outside the capped 100-row list. MemoryTab still applies type, recent-only, and visibility filters locally to those server results, and selected-memory lookup uses the displayed result set so server-only hits open in the detail panel.

Task #17245 decomposed `web/src/components/activity/SessionsTab.tsx` from 970 lines to 571 lines. Running-agent polling and entry derivation now live in `SessionsTab.entries.ts`; the toolbar and session list row rendering live in `SessionsTabList.tsx`; the watched-session detail pane and resize handle live in `SessionsTabDetail.tsx`; and context-menu/modal rendering lives in `SessionsTabMenu.tsx`. `FilterEmptyState` and its source-inspected empty-state strings intentionally remain in `SessionsTab.tsx`; `typographyLadder.test.ts` now reads the extracted sessions surface files when checking shared activity typography classes.

Gobby web useSessionDetail maintains a bounded tail-first transcript window, merges refreshed/live tail messages by message ID, and preserves older-page state during tail updates. Tail refreshes and page responses must be rejected when session identity, detail-load version, or tail-window version makes them stale; append live tail rows only when the loaded window is tail-contiguous and the viewer is at bottom.

Pipeline, cron, and system sessions are implementation details and must be excluded from user-facing session lists. Provider-native ACP session/list history is not materialized as canonical Gobby sessions; lifecycle controls remain for ACP sessions genuinely created through Gobby.

In gobby-cli, `crates/gwiki/src/commands/ask.rs` is a 1,388-line command module whose natural decomposition boundaries are: thin `execute` entrypoint; search-to-AskOutput assembly and dedup helpers; unified graph enrichment; AI synthesis/prompting; answer narration stripping; citation grounding; text/JSON rendering; and ask-specific tests. Nearby `crates/gwiki/src/commands/refresh/mod.rs` uses the local pattern of a command root with private submodules plus `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`.

Current web pipeline definition editing lives under web/src/components/activity/pipelines. PipelineEditor is mounted by PipelinesDefsDetail, while PipelinesTab owns the detail/editor view mode. Component regression tests belong in activity/pipelines/__tests__, with PipelinesTab integration coverage in PipelinesDefs.test.tsx.

In web TasksTab, selected-task WebSocket events already refresh detail explicitly in handleTaskEvent. The selection-driven detail effect should depend only on selectedTaskId and read cached task data through tasksRef; depending on the full tasks array causes unrelated task events/refetches to replace the detail editor and lose local draft/focus.

In gobby-cli/dev-parity-plus, task #635 kept gwiki `benchmark`, `graph`, `graph-context`, `librarian`, `review-report`, and `citation-quality` as public CLI subcommands and documented them in `docs/guides/gwiki-user-guide.md` instead of hiding them with clap `hide=true`. The guide now describes purpose, options, output contracts, hard PostgreSQL requirements, and degraded optional backend behavior for those commands.

The web UI's dark mode color hierarchy: --bg-primary (#0a0a0a) for main content areas, --bg-secondary (#141414) for secondary surfaces, --bg-tertiary (#1a1a1a) for chrome/elevated UI (sidebars, status bars, headers, and the ConversationPicker header/body).

Terminal UI session identity is socket-provenance-specific because daemon tmux identity fields can collide across the default and gobby sockets. In `web/src/components/activity/terminal/terminalSessions.ts`, default-socket rows join only by `gobby_session_id` to a `GobbySession` whose `agent_run_id` is null; gobby-socket rows join only by non-null `agent_run_id`. Raw `agent_managed`, default-row `agent_run_id`, and gobby-row `gobby_session_id` are untrusted. Focus resolution must scan the trusted joined result by matched Gobby session ID. Implemented by task #18542 in commit a62b2b945.

Daemon telemetry startup remains two-phase: bootstrap file logging is configured early so startup logs are available without creating OpenTelemetry providers; after ConfigStore and SecretStore load, phase-two telemetry initializes tracer, meter, and logger providers from runtime configuration and resolved secrets. Logging configuration is owned by top-level gobby.config.logging.LoggingSettings, while TelemetrySettings owns tracing, metrics, exporters, and LLM instrumentation; both phases use the resolved common logging-directory contract.

Claude Code PreToolUse blocks are represented through hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision="deny" while top-level continue remains true. In ClaudeCodeAdapter.translate_from_hook_response, a denied unified HookResponse must override any conflicting permission_decision="allow" before updatedInput is considered, or Claude may execute the blocked tool.

Gobby UI enablement is controlled by ui.enabled. In source checkouts, ui.mode=auto uses Vite development routing while the daemon remains the stable API/WebSocket origin on port 60887; installed layouts serve the built UI from the daemon. For network access, bind the daemon appropriately (current bind host: 0.0.0.0).

Web-chat plan approval supports two mechanisms: native tool-plan providers park an explicit plan-exit tool pending approval, while managed text-plan providers broadcast a pending plan after streaming and continue with a normal turn after approval. Approval can select normal or bypass execution; requested changes cancel while preserving feedback; timeouts clear pending state, interrupt the provider turn, and resolve as cancellation.

Gobby rule model constraint: RuleDefinitionBody allows AT MOST ONE 'block' effect per rule (pydantic validator rejects multiple). To block several command patterns in one concern, author separate named rules in the same YAML file (e.g. worker-safety/no-data-exfiltration.yaml holds no-curl-upload, no-wget-upload, no-remote-copy, no-secret-read). Also: block effects support command_not_pattern as an exemption regex alongside command_pattern, and rule `group` is derived from the rules/<dir> directory name during sync_bundled_rules.

Task #19092 / commit ca27e9898 hardens the asynchronous memory-recall gate announcement. Both bundled block reasons now tell the agent that get_recall_memories for the pending request is the only permitted call and must be issued alone, outside a parallel batch, because sibling calls are evaluated before retrieval lands. The bundled manifest was regenerated with write_bundled_content_manifest, and focused rule tests pin both directives.

HubConfig.auth_secret_name is the canonical hub credential selector. GitHub-topic hubs resolve auth_token_env; other hub types resolve auth_key_name through resolve_hub_api_keys. HubManager uses auth_secret_name consistently for loading, provider construction, status, and warnings.

For epic #15741 language-skill tasks, reference file count is intentionally flexible. Do not force exactly six reference files; choose the count by language needs and skill quality, such as four, seven, ten, etc.

Gobby's HTTP memory update path is src/gobby/servers/routes/memory.py MemoryUpdateRequest and route -> MemoryManagerFacadeMethods.update_memory -> MemoryLifecycleService.update_memory -> MemoryCrudMixin.update_memory. Mutable API fields must be forwarded through every layer; focused coverage pairs a route mock argument assertion with a manager/storage round-trip test.

WorkflowHookHandler serializes per-session rule evaluation with a threading.Lock registry acquired from async code. This is intentional because evaluate() can enter _evaluate_rules through sync bridge paths and different event loops; a shared asyncio.Lock would be unsafe under cross-loop contention. SESSION_END cleanup is ref-counted so queued same-session hook events keep using the same lock until all waiters drain.

HTTP auth exemptions in src/gobby/servers/middleware/auth.py use exact _PUBLIC_PATHS for session ingestion: /api/sessions/register, /find_current, /statusline, and /update_status. Other /api/sessions routes, all /api/mcp routes, and admin status/metrics/config remain protected; MCP server route construction already calls MCPServerConfig.validate(), which rejects unsupported transports and stdio without command.

Bundled agent sync poisoning (#17627): if an agent definition row is created via MCP create_agent_definition (tags ["user"]) BEFORE its bundled template ships with the same name, sync_bundled_agents skips it forever (_is_sync_managed_bundled_agent requires the 'gobby' tag), so template updates never reach the DB and generated <agent>-steps rows regenerate from the stale DB row at spawn time. Fixed in #17627: sync now fails loud (result['errors'] + result['shadowed'] + logger.error) when an unmanaged row shadows a bundled agent name; repair is deleting the unmanaged row and re-running sync (daemon restart). The wiki-researcher row was the first instance — created 2026-07-05 14:33 UTC during #17511 dev, template committed 15:35 UTC, allowance commit 51b21646b never synced.

PostgreSQL migrations are discovered from src/gobby/storage/migrations using unique sequential numeric SQL filenames matching ^(\d+)_...\.sql$. Baseline version 305 is a permanent high-water mark: versions at or below it are reserved, and future migrations must use unique numbers above 305 while remaining synchronized with the baseline schema and migration inventories.

Use the daemon-configured `TmuxSessionManager` helpers for Gobby-managed agent terminals; do not use a default tmux client or assume the default socket. Verify spawned sessions through that manager by requiring a live pane with `pane_dead=false` and a present `pane_pid`.

MCP call_tool wrapper contract: canonicalize_call_tool_wrapper strips nested server_name/tool_name/project_id wrapper route fields when nested route fields are present, while preserving nested session_id as target tool payload. MCP route stale-wrapper handling treats a call as stdio-wrapper context only when MCP_WRAPPER_FINGERPRINT_HEADER is present; X-Gobby-Caller-Project-Id alone is not enough.

Gobby router forms are `/gobby <skill> [args]`, `/gobby skill <skill> [args]`, and legacy `/gobby:<skill> [args]`; bare `/gobby` and `/gobby help` show dynamic help. In Codex-facing examples, use `$gobby <skill> ...`.

Gobby's legal last-hop truncation views keep truncation and expose honest provenance: SymbolSummarizer reports rendered/consumed/total characters plus file:line range inside the fenced source block; session-start wiki overview points to wiki _index.md; MCP importer documentation reports shown/total characters plus the originating GitHub URL or search query.

Worktree sync product direction: sync_worktree should let callers explicitly choose the source branch/ref, including local branches such as 0.5.0, remote-tracking refs such as origin/0.5.0, or another branch. Default for Gobby local-first workflows should prefer the worktree's stored local base_branch, not origin/<base_branch>. This applies to MCP/CLI/API sync surfaces.

GitHubIssueImporter input contract after task #18920: imported issue numbers must be plain positive integers within PostgreSQL INTEGER range; invalid numbers are skipped with github_issue_number/github_repo warning context. Labels accept GitHub's list of strings or mappings with string `name`, trim non-empty names, and discard malformed entries. Missing or malformed creation timestamps fall back to current UTC so one bad issue cannot abort the batch.
User preference: after finishing a Gobby task, call gobby-sessions:compact_self before continuing when feasible. This reinforces the existing context-handoff convention for terminal sessions.

# Review Lesson: Loop-hosting thread readiness must be signaled from inside the running loop

## Lesson
- principle: When a background thread hosts an asyncio event loop and consumers gate submissions on loop.is_running(), the readiness event must be set by a callback scheduled on the loop (loop.call_soon), not between loop creation and run_forever(); otherwise there is a window where the constructor has returned but the loop is not yet running.
- root_cause: Readiness was signaled at thread-setup time instead of loop-run time, creating a construct-then-submit race for immediate first use.
- prevention: Signal readiness via loop.call_soon(ready.set) immediately before run_forever(), and regression-test by gating run_forever entry and asserting a submission immediately after construction succeeds.

## Diagnostic
- title: Loop-hosting thread readiness must be signaled from inside the running loop
- message: WorkflowEvaluationRuntime._run_loop set its readiness threading.Event after storing the loop but before loop.run_forever() started, so __init__ could return while loop.is_running() was still False and run() spuriously rejected work with 'Workflow evaluation runtime is not running'.

Gobby runs multiple concurrent agent sessions against the SAME working tree and git index. A bare `git commit` (or `git add -A`) will sweep another session's staged files into YOUR commit — observed 2026-06-09 when a docs/reviews scaffold commit (#15765) accidentally bundled another session's in-flight bundled-C-skill files (#15748). Mitigation: always commit with an explicit pathspec (`git commit <paths> -m ...`) and stage only your own files; never bare-commit the whole index. If you hit a `.git/index.lock` error, another session's git process is mid-commit — diagnose via `ps` for git processes + lock mtime and wait for it to clear; do NOT force-remove the lock (risks corrupting the other session's commit). Recovery if you already bundled foreign files: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` then `git commit <your-paths>` (pathspec commit leaves the other files staged for their owner).

For a small render-only delta, prefer a deterministic in-place adjustment over a full AI regeneration. Full-vault generation can converge across nightly runs because completed pages and interim metadata persist. Keep `_meta/codewiki.json` and `.obsidian/*` out of git staging.

gobby-cli source-edit workflow under Gobby hooks: PreToolUse hooks block the Read/Edit/Write tools on indexed .rs source (even bounded reads, and even scratchpad copies that keep the .rs extension), plus grep/rg, broad head/cat on project source, bare python (require-uv), and cat of JSON. The standard Edit/Write tools need a prior Read the hook denies, so they're unusable directly on .rs. WHY: the repo enforces 'prefer gcode for source reads' + required-skill/task gates. HOW: (1) read working-tree source via `git show HEAD:<path>` or gcode (outline/symbol/grep); small `head -n` is ok, broad head/cat on .rs is flagged. (2) To EDIT: cp the .rs into the scratchpad as a .txt (the hook keys on the .rs extension, so .txt copies Read/Edit freely), edit the .txt with the Edit tool, then cp it back over the .rs; verify with git diff + cargo build/clippy/nextest. (3) Move a large inline #[cfg(test)] module with `git show ...|sed -n 'a,bp'|sed 's/^    //'`. (4) Load gate skills up front via get_skill: code-index, task-creation, rust, development-discipline, json, task-transitions. (5) Create/claim a gobby-task before editing; finish with commit + close_task(commit_sha). Foreground `sleep` is blocked — wait via background Bash or Monitor.

Chat UI off-by-one bug after interrupt: When a user sends a new message while the previous response is streaming, the Claude SDK's response buffer isn't fully drained after interrupt(). The next receive_response() call returns stale events from the interrupted query, and _stream_chat_response tags them with the NEW request_id — so the frontend renders the old response as if it belongs to the new message. useDetailDraft (web/src/components/activity/fields/useDetailDraft.ts) marks the draft clean only AFTER its onSave callback resolves. Any navigation triggered inside onSave (e.g. a WikiTabActions helper that navigates on success) runs while the registered dirty guard still reports dirty, so guardedRun pops a spurious 'discard unsaved changes' confirm. Pattern: onSave only persists and stashes the result path in a ref; the caller awaits save() and navigates after it returns true (draft is marked clean synchronously inside save() before it returns). WikiPageEditor.runSave/onSaved is the reference implementation.

Gwiki human-facing timestamps use the shared precision-aware parser in crates/gwiki/src/support/time.rs. ParsedTimestamp distinguishes Instant, DateOnly, DatePrefix (date plus original text), and Unparseable. Instant rendering accepts an injected FixedOffset, emits local `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ±HH:MM`, and retains computed `unix-ms:<epoch>` in parentheses. DateOnly retains calendar precision; DatePrefix and Unparseable render their original text verbatim. Citation rendering is exposed as render_citations; citation, log.rs, and collect.rs log bodies use the shared formatter, while recap.rs alone converts DateOnly/DatePrefix to midnight UTC for ordering. Implemented for task #18578 at commits 9d1b579a6 and 7af59c95c.

Josh's rule for plan deferrals and task hygiene (stated 2026-07-29, after deleting #19207/#19208/#19209): do NOT create deferral or follow-up tasks for a plan that has not finalized — it is wasteful, since the plan can still change or be abandoned. He also does not want unrelated loose tasks floating outside an epic when the work is epic-based; tasks should hang off the epic they belong to. Practical effect on /gobby plan: a `kind: deferred` section's task_ref should not drive task creation during drafting, enhancement, or adversarial review. Deferral anchors belong at finalization/expansion, under the epic. Note the plan validator does not verify task existence — `uv run gobby plans validate` passes with dangling task_ref values — so an unfinalized plan carrying deferral refs will not fail validation.

Support VLM multimodal workloads needed by UI-TARS where backend/model capabilities allow them, and integrate UI-TARS as a Gobby-bundled external MCP server managed like Context7 and Brave Search. vLLM is the serving product; VLM is a vision-language model class.

Codewiki compare mode (`gcode codewiki --compare-to GIT_REF[:META_PATH]`) is a read-only metadata consumer. It resolves the Git ref and repository-relative baseline path separately; omitted META_PATH defaults to `<out-relative>/_meta/codewiki.json`, while current metadata always comes from local `--out`. It compares only each doc's commit, commit_dirty, and source_hashes. Output uses top-level base/current commit metadata plus path-sorted added/removed/changed arrays; unstamped values serialize as null. Invalid explicit paths, bad refs, absent baseline metadata, malformed baseline metadata, and malformed current metadata have distinct errors. Implemented by task #18789 / commit 0dd39d15e.

Store runtime configuration in Gobby's DB-backed config store. `~/.gobby/config.yaml` is an export, legacy, or explicit-load path; avoid ad hoc environment variables as persistent configuration conventions. Add real config-store-backed settings and update the variables/config surface when introducing settings.

Daemon cron initialization invariant after #16770 / commit 84d8be5f5: CronJobStorage and CronExecutor are required dependencies for cron registration; their constructor failures stop that chain after logging the exact subsystem with traceback. SystemAutomationLoop initialization may fail independently while CronScheduler still initializes. CronScheduler or unexpected handler-registration failure clears runner.system_automation_loop so lifecycle startup cannot run automation against an unavailable scheduler/executor chain.

Transcript provider parsers may emit provider-shaped records, but rendering, windowing, indexing, stats, lifecycle processing, and title heuristics must consume records after normalize_transcript_records(...). The normalizer suppresses successful no-output Grok hook_execution and renders visible or failed Grok hooks as system text. Parsers intentionally suppress Codex tool_search_call/tool_search_output and protocol metadata, but Droid todo_state snapshots are now emitted as synthetic completed TodoWrite tool-use/tool-result pairs; normalization collapses only consecutive synthetic pairs with the same id. True unknown provider blocks should be fail-soft preserved as ParsedMessage records.

As of commit a5380ad60 (task #16285), export_config_to_yaml writes owner-only YAML through a same-directory temporary file, flushes and fsyncs the completed file, atomically replaces the destination, then fsyncs the parent directory. Serialization or pre-replace failures remove the temp file and preserve the previous export byte-for-byte.

The gobby root CLI supports eager --hello and --goodbye flags in src/gobby/cli/__init__.py; they print 'Hello from Gobby!' and 'Goodbye from Gobby!' before config loading or subcommand dispatch. Focused coverage lives in tests/cli/test_cli.py under TestCLICommands.

Gwiki URL cache freshness is modeled separately from immutable capture identity: SourceRecord.fetched_at remains the original capture timestamp, while last_verified_at advances after successful unchanged URL ingest/refresh and fetch_provenance promotes from Stub to Fetched. URL batch cache lookup lives in ingest/url/cache.rs, uses one manifest snapshot, canonical location, checked unix-ms TTL math, and raw/asset existence; zero TTL always refetches. Only real HTML/non-HTML URL snapshot ingest originates Fetched; manifest dedup and refresh may promote it, while collect/manual/local constructors remain Stub. Pre-field manifest records deserialize as Stub with last_verified_at normalized to fetched_at.

Task #18713 implemented context-aware progressive MCP discovery in commit e0eed4dda. Contract: call leased known tools directly; for a known unleased tool call get_tool_schema then call_tool; for an unknown tool name use list_tools then get_tool_schema then call_tool; use list_mcp_servers only for unknown server or registry inspection; gobby-skills get_skill/list_skills/search_skills are schema-gate exempt and callable directly. Context clear/compact/resume resets only schema leases while PostgreSQL inventory/session variables persist across daemon reconstruction. Invalid arguments always include the current schema and retain the lease. Validation: 115 runtime/rule tests, 173 guidance/skill/compact tests, 356 adapter/hook/manifest tests, Ruff format/check, mypy on 11 source files, and test-quality audit of 551 tests all passed.

Compact-session ghost reconciliation uses creation ordering. A ghost caused by compact ingress can only be newer than the canonical session row, so same-machine exact-terminal rows with `(created_at, id)` older than or equal to the canonical row are historical and must not block compact reactivation. Newer empty unreferenced rows may be deleted as ghosts; newer populated or retained duplicates remain structured conflicts without mutation. Implemented for task #19166 in commit 2e057ccb8e13.

Voice-stack dependency compatibility (2026-07): TorchAudio 2.11's official release declares compatibility with PyTorch 2.11 and future PyTorch versions. Gobby therefore pins torch==2.13.0 with torchaudio==2.11.0 in [tool.uv].override-dependencies. PyTorch 2.13.0 fixes GHSA-rrmf-rvhw-rf47, so pyproject.toml has no audit ignore for that advisory. The pair was validated by a real import reporting torch 2.13.0 / torchaudio 2.11.0, exception-free `uv audit --frozen`, 37 focused Chatterbox voice tests, and package build. The existing setuptools>=83.0.0 override remains because exercised voice paths do not use removed pkg_resources APIs.

Git >=2.38.0 is a required Gobby dependency. `gobby install` fails when Git is unavailable, and `gobby status` reports missing or insufficient Git as a required-dependency health issue. A workspace itself need not be a Git repository; the Personal workspace may remain non-repository.

Gobby workflows are event-driven behavioral rules, not step-based state machines. The legacy WorkflowEngine was removed; RuleEngine is the sole enforcement mechanism and loads standalone workflow definitions from PostgreSQL-backed storage. Rule effects are validated through RuleEffect and may extend beyond the original block, set_variable, inject_context, mcp_call, and observe set.

Josh strongly prefers preserving complete raw system and cron output. Use structured outputs, summaries, pagination, references, and drill-down access instead of arbitrary truncation; any hard byte cap should exist only as a safety boundary with explicit overflow storage and retrieval.

Activity-panel toolbars use the shared layout tokens `--activity-panel-bar-height` (2.75rem) and `--status-bar-control-height` (1.75rem), plus surviving activity-panel layout hook classes. Use the canonical React `ui/Button` surface rather than new `.btn` CSS usage. Task stage filters are explicit: no selected stages emits no `stage` params; selected stages emit their names. Review-rejected filtering remains a frontend-derived filter for ready current stages with `review_round_count > 0`.

MCP call_tool argument validation in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/argument_validation.py intentionally enforces only top-level JSON Schema types. It supports string, number, integer, boolean, object, array, null, list-valued type, and recursive anyOf; booleans are excluded from numeric types and integral floats satisfy integer. Unsupported or untyped branches stay permissive, and enums, bounds, patterns, nested properties, and array items remain downstream concerns.

Task #15700 cleanup: ProviderModelCatalog no longer accepts a DaemonConfig/config constructor argument; runtime and tests should instantiate it with ProviderModelCatalog(cache_path=...) or ProviderModelCatalog(). The web plan-pending surface variant is now a persisted UI setting named planPendingVariant with allowed values 'info' and 'amber', defaulting to 'info', and render code should resolve colors via getPlanPendingColors(variant) rather than a module-level active variant constant.

Gobby build coordinator policy: bugs discovered while coordinating `gobby build` should get regression coverage at the E2E or build-level integration layer that exercises the autonomous build path, in addition to focused unit tests where useful.

In gobby-cli nextest test-group filters for structural serial DB modules must match both nested and root module paths: use `(test(::serial_db::) | test(serial_db::))`. Top-level integration tests like `gobby-wiki::cli_search serial_db::...` do not match `test(::serial_db::)` alone.

Expansion prompt file context in `src/gobby/tasks/expansion/_compile.py::_build_file_context` treats task title, description, and validation criteria as untrusted path input. Accepted candidates must contain no `..` components, resolve under the canonical repository root (including symlink resolution), and be read through the already-validated resolved path.

Transcript rendering treats late tool-result owner emissions as updates to an existing RenderedMessage object. Full and window materializers should deduplicate those repeated object references by object identity, because distinct messages expanded from one raw transcript record can legitimately share the same rendered ID (for example Claude image and document blocks).

Web UI code splitting pattern: All non-default page components in App.tsx are lazy-loaded with React.lazy() and wrapped in Suspense inside the AppErrorBoundary. Vendor deps are split via manualChunks in vite.config.ts: codemirror, xterm, syntax-highlighter, markdown, d3. MemoryGraph (2D) and KnowledgeGraph (3D) are both lazy-loaded in MemoryPage.tsx. The lazy import pattern is: const Page = lazy(() => import('./components/Page').then(m => ({ default: m.Page }))). ChatPage stays eagerly loaded as the default tab.

Task #17267 decomposed `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_expansion.py` into a 17-line compatibility facade. MCP tool registration now lives in `_expansion_registry.py`; run/background orchestration, `ExpansionRunResult`, and `start_expansion_run_impl` live in `_expansion_runtime.py`. Keep `_background_run_tasks` and `_execute_run_background` re-exported from `_expansion.py`; `_expansion_registry` deliberately resolves `_execute_run_background` through the facade at call time so existing tests/callers patching `gobby.mcp_proxy.tools.tasks._expansion._execute_run_background` still affect resume behavior.

User preference for build-coordinator sessions: when coordinator cleanup or bug-fix work is broad, spawn subagents to parallelize investigation and implementation when useful, then have the coordinator verify and integrate the results before closing tasks.

Gobby daemon shutdown handling for uvicorn has layered shutdown noise control. `shutdown_daemon_services()` drains uvicorn HTTP connections before setting `server.should_exit`; as of task #15300 commit 7afa6149001b3d7dd13143db29dda3afca99aba9, it also cancels remaining live `server.server_state.tasks` with the `Gobby shutdown drain` message and waits briefly so daemon stop is bounded before uvicorn's own graceful timeout. `UvicornShutdownLogFilter` suppresses those Gobby drain cancellation records only while shutdown is active, while preserving the older graceful-timeout downgrade fallback from task #15289 commit f6a41cacb.

Transcript processing must decide short-session LLM skipping from the session turn_count refreshed after _process_session_transcript persists parsed transcript stats. digest_markdown remains the synthesis input and missing-transcript availability check; its heading count is not authoritative session state. This behavior lives in TranscriptProcessingMixin in src/gobby/sessions/transcript_processing.py.

Since task #18818 / commit 24ef776e2, oversized inline handoff summaries use deterministic section-aware budgeting. `split_markdown_sections` is fence-aware for ```/~~~ and preserves a preamble plus casefolded `##` sections; `allocate_section_budget` guarantees the first `Next Steps` and `Current State` occurrences before optional sections, treats later duplicates as unknown-priority sections, and emits trim/drop titles. `_bound_handoff_summary` falls back byte-for-byte to the prior head cut when neither mandatory title is recognized, and otherwise reserves a bounded breadcrumb whose omission list truncates titles to 40 chars and caps at 10 entries.

Daemon-selected recalls use a mandatory single-call retrieval contract. The dispatcher records ranked references in `memory_recall_deliveries`; `gobby-memory.get_recall_memories(recall_request_id)` resolves the ambient session, enforces oldest-pending order, returns selected bodies unchanged with rank/search metadata, reports missing IDs, and completes the request after retrieval. While valid recall is pending, every other tool and `turn_end` are blocked; `get_recall_memories` is the only permitted call and must be issued alone, outside a parallel batch.

Task ownership is represented by claimed_by_session_id with a real sessions foreign key and task_stage_states for lifecycle/projection. Do not rely on the removed tasks.assignee field; active sessions without claimed tasks do not appear as task owners merely because they are linked elsewhere.

gwiki librarian boundary after #18433 (commit 447ed0828): `librarian.rs` owns the public Options/report/artifact/SemanticProbe models, `run`, `render_text`, runtime probing/orchestration, deterministic hygiene classification, and lifecycle promotion. `librarian/semantic.rs` owns semantic availability/failure reporting, near-duplicate discovery and exclusions (reviewed distinct pairs, redirects, session/source digests, folder contexts), semantic queries, and unresolved-link clustering. `librarian/proposals.rs` owns suggested task/diff construction plus librarian artifact paths and JSON/text persistence. `librarian/tests.rs` owns the full behavior suite and semantic test backends. Keep internal callers pointed at the owning modules; do not add forwarding wrappers or compatibility re-exports.

Native helper policy: Gobby resolves executable managed helpers in ~/.gobby/bin before PATH, including GOBBY_DISTRIBUTION=homebrew. Managed install/status/updater logic for gcode, ghook, and gwiki must first probe the real local binary version and skip downloads or downgrades when installed_version >= MANAGED_BIN_VERSION_PINS[name]. GitHub releases are only a source for missing or stale helpers, not something the daemon should query before accepting an already-pinned local binary.

`task_artifacts` rows are created lazily. To serialize merge-style updates safely in PostgreSQL, first `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, then `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` inside the same transaction so first-write races also lock a real row. Counter increments such as `expansion_attempts` should use a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET counter = table.counter + 1 RETURNING counter` statement.

LM Studio and Ollama chat-completions generation endpoints use endpoint:<name>[/<model>] selectors and execute through endpoint-specific Codex OSS app-server backends. They are web-chat available only when live discovery finds eligible chat models, the protocol is supported by Codex OSS, and Codex CLI is installed. Start the OSS app-server with global flags before the subcommand: codex --oss --local-provider <ollama|lmstudio> app-server. Generic OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints remain catalog-only for web chat.

In gobby-cli, CodeWiki purge is intentionally file-only (`gcode codewiki --purge --out <DIR> --force`) and must not clear code index, code-symbol Qdrant collections, or Falkor code graph; those remain owned by `gcode invalidate`, `gcode vector clear`, and `gcode graph clear`. Gwiki purge owns scoped generated wiki state across `gwiki_*` Postgres rows plus scoped Qdrant/Falkor wiki projections.

Gobby PostgreSQL migrations are flattened through baseline version 305. `postgres_baseline_schema.sql` is the current complete fresh-install schema and seed snapshot, and fresh installs record version 305. Future schema changes must use uniquely numbered SQL migration files above 305 while keeping the baseline synchronized, because fresh installs replay on-disk migrations atop it. Existing hubs below 305 follow the corrupt-partial backup/recreate path.

Gobby daemon resolves config_store $secret: references ONLY at daemon startup (runner_init/storage.py passes secret_resolver=secret_store.get to load_config). A secret added or changed after the daemon starts is invisible to the running process until restart. Symptom seen 2026-06-11: POST /api/embeddings returned LM Studio's 'An LM Studio API token is required' while gcode embeddings doctor showed api_key_present=true in config_store — the daemon process simply predated the secret. Before filing a daemon auth/config bug, compare the daemon start time (ps -eo pid,lstart,command | grep gobby.runner) against when the config/secret was written.

Gobby lifecycle manifest semantics changed in task #14248: generic task creation through storage/MCP/HTTP is metadata-only and does not seed task_stage_states. Lifecycle rows are now created by explicit entry points such as LocalTaskManager.initialize_task_manifest, gobby-tasks-ops initialize_task_manifest, and build/expansion/review-anchor flows. Expansion and epic build descendants derive child manifests from the parent resolved manifest, copying matching caps and limiting child scopes to development, optional holistic_qa for epics, and inherited pr/merge. Historical manifest cleanup is scoped through LifecycleRepair / `gobby tasks repair-lifecycle` and dry-runs by default.

CodeWiki persistence and nightly-boundary invariants (#18190/#18483/#18486; commits c7681dfb5, 95a71920f, a4fcd798f, 5e44a7b0e): generated pages whose links depend on computed targets must invalidate over the complete emitted link set, and deterministic docs vulnerable to stale retained bodies must use a `content-sensitive:<sha256>` key. For content-sensitive docs, reuse is allowed only when the staged body is byte-equal to freshly rendered content; fresh metadata alone must never bless a stale body. `code/_ownership.md` hashes its actual rendered ownership content, so deleted sources and cluster renames rewrite stale file/module links before fail-closed publication validates targets. Separately, ordinary `--scope` intentionally preserves out-of-scope docs and returns before global/curated/ownership emitters; nightly configured scopes must pass `--complete-scope`, filtering input to configured roots while using a global prune/generation boundary so retained global pages cannot escape refresh. Production proof on 2026-07-18: cron run b0ccd499-3883-421b-accd-3d6aac46ef24 completed with 2,997 tracked docs, 44 changed docs (10 files, 6 modules), zero degraded file pages, ownership key `content-sensitive:8cde144c...`, no stale `usefulness.py` link, successful atomic publication, and successful post-publish indexing.

Task #14257 converted `src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_session_start.py` into a same-name package. `__init__.py` is the compatibility boundary exporting `SessionStartMixin`, `AgentActivationResult`, `SUMMARY_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_S`, and the package-level patch targets `Path`, `schedule_tmux_window_rename`, and `consume_and_schedule_compact_self_continuation`; implementation now lives in `types.py`, `transcripts.py`, `agents.py`, `handoff.py`, and `flow.py`.

Web chat SDK resume architecture: ChatSession.resume_session_id is passed to ClaudeAgentOptions.resume + continue_conversation=True. SDK session IDs come from two sources: (1) sessions.external_id — web chat updates this to SDK session ID after first ResultMessage (chat.py:1214), (2) agent_runs.sdk_session_id — autonomous agents store this via update_sdk_session_id(). The _handle_continue_in_chat handler in session_control.py resolves the SDK session ID, kills any running agent (terminal/autonomous) via registry.kill(close_terminal=True), then creates a ChatSession with resume. Falls back to history injection if no SDK session ID available. Frontend /resume command opens ResumeSessionModal which calls continueSessionInChat.

In gobby-cli, gwiki video behavior is split with `crates/gwiki/src/video.rs` as a small facade. Child modules live under `crates/gwiki/src/video/`: `types.rs` defines the video frame/audio/markdown/degradation data types; `sampling.rs` contains frame sampling and audio-reference helpers; `alignment.rs` aligns transcript segments to frame descriptions; `timestamps.rs` contains timestamp parsing/formatting and transcription range formatting; `markdown.rs` orchestrates video-derived markdown rendering/writing; `write.rs` contains atomic derived-markdown file writes and parent-dir sync; `tests.rs` holds the existing video behavior tests with explicit imports for private alignment coverage. The facade still exports the crate call-site APIs used by ingest: sample frame/markdown functions and public video data types.

Memory recall should use the current prompt and available session digest rather than replaying prior-turn synthesized context. Generic recalled-memory injection is rendered by `src/gobby/memory/context.py::build_memory_context()` as `<project-memory>` blocks with `memory_id` metadata; do not rely on retired workflow/MCP-specific injection renderers or similarity/search metadata.

Settings-overlay sections that edit useSettings-managed client preferences must consume the single shared useSettings instance provided through SettingsSectionContext, not instantiate useSettings independently. This preserves one source of truth for settings used elsewhere in the app. API settings are authoritative after initial load, except explicit per-field edits made before the GET resolves override the corresponding remote field; persistence waits for initialization and records pending user changes.

Bundled workflow definitions should be source-controlled YAML under src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/. Synced YAML records have source='template' and are not runnable by default; create an installed copy from the YAML content to run a pipeline. Template writes converge through template_writer.py::_write_yaml, while user/project-authored definitions must be preserved by refresh and reinstall flows.

Codex app-server supports ephemeral threads through `CodexAppServerClient.start_thread(..., ephemeral=True)` and maps the returned `thread.ephemeral` field into `CodexThread`. Gobby's daemon one-shot Codex text generation does not use this app-server path; it uses `CodexCLITextGenerateAdapter` with `codex exec --ephemeral`. App-server threads remain for web-chat/session integration and model discovery.

Circular-import gotcha for token/usage helpers: `src/gobby/sessions/transcripts/__init__.py` eagerly imports every parser (claude, codex, droid, gemini, grok, qwen), and `gemini.py` imports the shared helper `gobby.sessions.token_usage`. So any leaf/helper module that needs `TokenUsage` from `gobby.sessions.transcripts.base` and is imported by both a parser and a non-transcript layer (e.g. the hooks layer `hooks/event_handlers/_misc.py`) will hit `ImportError: cannot import name ... from partially initialized module`. Fix: import `TokenUsage` LAZILY (function-local, with a `TYPE_CHECKING` import for the annotation under `from __future__ import annotations`) inside the helper rather than at module top. This both breaks the cycle and keeps the hook layer from transitively loading all transcript parsers at import time. Established in gobby-#15578 (commit 1e4aeb4ba) for `gobby.sessions.token_usage.gemini_token_usage`.

Task #17241 decomposed `src/gobby/servers/websocket/handlers/session_observe.py` while preserving it as the public import and monkeypatch facade. Shared coercion, fallback-context, live-variable, and metadata payload helpers live in `session_observe_support.py`; continue/resume handling and `check_resume_blocked` live in `session_observe_continue.py`; attach, detach, and `send_to_cli_session` proxy handling live in `session_observe_proxy.py`. The moved implementations intentionally consult facade aliases for `check_resume_blocked`, `kill_terminal_session`, `get_tmux_manager_for_context`, and `_resolve_agent_name_for_session` so existing tests/callers that patch `gobby.servers.websocket.handlers.session_observe` keep working.

Task #18736 (commit 69eb83caf) wires one ReviewLearningService instance from setup_internal_registries into the review-learning registry and both task RegistryContext instances. Leaf LLM validation recalls code-domain validation-miss lessons with limit 3 before prompt assembly. Successful empty recall preserves the legacy prompt bytes; recalled guidance enters the lessons_section slot as untrusted content. Recall failures, including project-scope resolution failures, remain non-fatal, log one warning, and serialize one lesson-recall-failed warning diagnostic while keeping the prompt identical to empty recall. Structured validator issues continue through the same validation pass and history persistence.

User-confirmed context-pressure contract: ordinary Plan mode receives no compact_self/context-pressure nudges on any provider or surface, including spawned plan-review agents. The reserved future exception is autonomous plan-to-PR execution through `gobby build` once that path is fully implemented; until then Plan mode always suppresses nudges and clears stale pressure-band/deduplication state so normal nudging resumes after exit.

Gobby RuleEngine manual compaction handling: manual-like PRE_COMPACT triggers (`manual`, `user`, `clear`, `compact`, `compress`, or a present `custom_instructions`) set `_compact_turn_end_bypass_pending`. The next stop/after_agent/stop_failure evaluation removes only semantic `turn_end` and clears the marker, preserving raw-event rules; `turn_start` clears stale markers.

MCP list_mcp_servers tool output is intentionally compacted in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server_list.py for stdio, GobbyDaemonTools, and hook _proxy/list_mcp_servers paths: connected servers are emitted as names in servers, while non-connected or disabled servers keep compact detail under issues. The HTTP /api/mcp/servers response remains rich object-shaped for UI and API clients.

Task storage concurrency convention: mutate labels and commits with guarded PostgreSQL JSONB operators in a single UPDATE, never by rewriting arrays derived from a prior read. Contested lifecycle transitions such as claim and escalate use conditional UPDATE predicates and inspect rowcount to report the losing transition.

Phase 6 frontend task refactor for #13866 moved LifecycleBoard stage registry construction, blocked filtering, category filtering, visible-stage calculation, swimlane grouping, and per-stage task selection into web/src/components/tasks/lifecycleBoardModel.ts. useTasks now keeps its public API/types intact while using internal helpers for task-list query params, pagination append behavior, and websocket task event application; the Phase 6 test contract still expects StageAdvanceAction to be imported in web/src/hooks/useTasks.ts from ../lib/stageActions.

Tags (and similar extensible config concepts) must be configuration, not code — introducing a new value must never require a Python source edit.

Why: Josh's framing (session #3368, 2026-04-22): 'shouldn't adding tags not require a code change? kind of defeats the purpose of having tags.' Tags are only useful if they're an extensible config surface; if every new value requires shipping Python, they're just hardcoded enums with extra steps.

How to apply: When a plan needs to introduce a new tag, label, category, or similar extensible vocabulary word, don't put the list in Python. Check first: (1) does the storage layer already accept free-form strings (Gobby's `labels` column does), (2) are there existing config surfaces that can emit the new value — LLM prompt templates, rule YAMLs with `mcp_call` effects that call `add_label` on `task_created`, agent calls to `add_label` with arbitrary strings. A one-time plumbing change to EXPOSE a config-driven mechanism (e.g. adding `labels: list[str]` to an LLM output schema so prompts can populate it) is acceptable because it makes the mechanism generic; per-value Python changes are not. This generalizes: before adding a whitelist, enum, or hardcoded set in Python for any extensible concept, check whether the existing storage + a config surface (prompt, rule, skill) already supports free-form strings.

At task-closure boundaries, follow the user's latest explicit instruction for compaction. Call gobby-sessions:compact_self after close_task when the active goal asks for it; if the user rejects it, let them compact manually. The durable intent is clean context between tasks.

Python imports of `gobby.ai.<submodule>` execute the eager `gobby.ai.__init__` first. Configuration modules loaded by `gobby.config.app` must keep import-time dependencies outside the `gobby.ai` package, while endpoint helpers used by agent reasoning should be imported inside the call boundary. The regression probe is `python -c "import gobby.cli"`.

User preference for workflow design: make pipelines, agent launching, and rule enforcement simple and direct. Avoid requiring complex lifecycle plumbing or polling-heavy machinery for straightforward pipeline behavior.

In gobby-cli/dev-parity-plus, gwiki no longer keeps blanket `#[allow(dead_code)]` annotations on `crates/gwiki/src/lib.rs` module declarations. Task #634 moved the remaining dormant warnings to item-level `#[allow(dead_code, reason = "reserved gwiki CLI/API split")]` annotations and tightened `MAX_RENDERED_PDF_PAGES` to `#[cfg(feature = "documents")]`. Future gwiki CLI/library split work should remove those item-level annotations as code paths become either reachable or truly deleted.

Memory dream dry runs materialize one immutable, strictly ordered eligible-ID snapshot at run start, then hydrate active/visible IDs page by page in snapshot order. Mutable last_dreamed_at/updated_at values cannot move rows across pages; missing or hidden rows are logged and skipped. Complete validated dry-run actions are stored in run.plan.actions and rendered by `gobby memory dream status`, while live run action_sample remains capped.

The bundled `/gobby build` skill documents the interactive E2E pattern: keep a claimed coordinator/tracking epic separate from the automation/document epic, use `--quick` only for smoke checks, run final validation without `--quick` with bounded `--max-active-agents`, keep root `README.md` out of docs/guides refresh scope unless explicit, and verify real merge SHA/no agents/no claimed build tasks/no stale worktrees or clones.

Droid spawn runtime in Gobby uses the existing tmux spawn path. execute_spawn provider='droid' calls _spawn_droid_terminal, which builds `droid exec --input-format stream-json --cwd <cwd> ... --auto high <prompt>` and never passes Gobby's UUID as droid --session-id. Droid auth env vars are FACTORY_API_KEY and FACTORY_API_BASE_URL. pre_approve_directory('droid', cwd) is intentionally a no-op because spawned agents use --auto high rather than a trust database.

Gobby wiki freshness must hash the rendered source-page prompt content and prompt path, not only the prompt file path; wiki_source_context_hash is the shared helper used by synthesis and lifecycle refresh checks.

Codex now has native hook support in Gobby. Use the stable `[features].hooks` flag; graceful Codex CLI exit uses a matcherless native SessionEnd hook via `ghook --gobby-owned --cli=codex --type=SessionEnd --enqueue-only` with timeout 3. Antigravity terminal title setup: setting terminal.integrated.tabs.title to ${sequence} is necessary but not sufficient after recent Antigravity builds because the terminal tab list can be hidden for a single terminal. Gobby's installer should force terminal.integrated.tabs.hideCondition=never for Antigravity and Antigravity IDE while preserving other VS Code-family IDEs' default tab visibility.

TmuxSessionManager.send_keys(..., literal=True) delegates to send_literal_text_to_tmux_target, which strips only trailing newlines, pastes remaining text through a named tmux buffer with `paste-buffer -p`, waits 1.0 second after a non-empty paste, and then sends exactly one raw Enter when trailing newlines were present. Internal newlines remain in the paste; text without a trailing newline sends no Enter; newline-only input sends one Enter without a paste delay. The older 200 ms interval from task #18664 / commit a2b62ca87 is superseded: Josh explicitly requires 1.0 second because 200 ms is too short for Codex long-paste processing such as `[Pasted Content …]`.

Task #17270 decomposed `src/gobby/memory/services/search.py` into a 401-line compatibility facade plus focused helpers under `src/gobby/memory/services/_search_*.py`; public imports for `DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT`, `SearchDebugHit`, `SearchDebugSnapshot`, and `SearchService` remain stable.

Memory Dream truth-digest policy: global-only sweeps use canonical platform facts only; non-daemon project sweeps use only that project's wiki sidecar digest; the daemon's current project blends canonical platform facts first with its project wiki sidecar digest second. Missing or invalid sidecars are omitted cleanly rather than substituted with platform facts.

Epic #16998 one-surface activity-panel migration has a foundational guide at docs/guides/one-surface-tab-recipe.md, added by task #17013 in commit 696bc110d. Downstream UI migration leaves should load the gobby-skills impeccable skill, read .impeccable.md, then follow this guide for exemplars, file-family shape, Save/Discard, QuickMenu, registration, teardown, verification, and pitfalls.

Scheduled communications routing contract (task #18858, commit 19a4f3647): Cron completion callbacks emit cron.run.<status> through CommunicationsManager even when WebSocket is disabled, using the cron run ID as a durable event_id and the job project_id for routing. OutboundCommunications derives a deterministic per-event-type/per-channel message UUID, persists a pending reservation before platform delivery, and returns the existing persisted record on restart or concurrent replay so Telegram is not sent the same completion twice. Final status and platform_message_id are persisted after delivery. Telegram home delivery uses the channel's existing config_json.default_destination plus a cron.run.* communications routing rule; WebSocket failures are isolated and cannot suppress communications delivery.

Structured attention responses persist {kind, excerpt, options:[{option,label}], fingerprint}, with detector excerpts capped at the final 12 lines/4096 characters. POST /api/attention/{entry_id}/respond validates exactly one of option/text/key and requires the stored episode plus a fresh pane fingerprint. Autonomous tmux input is routed through TmuxInputArbiter, which persists per-pane FIFO requests and handles delivery acknowledgment/recovery; direct send_keys remains confined to private primitives and the raw user-owned PTY bridge. Attention routes remain centrally registered from src/gobby/servers/_app_routes.py.

TerminalType enum was removed from the agent spawner system. Everything uses tmux now (TmuxSpawner). MCP `gobby-sessions:get_session` hydrates `claimed_task_refs`, `created_task_refs`, and `closed_task_refs` from `SessionManager.fetch_task_refs_by_session([session.id])` before serialization.
