Task #17269 decomposed `web/src/hooks/useSessionDetail.ts` into a public hook facade plus focused helpers under `web/src/hooks/useSessionDetail/` (`api.ts`, `chatPolling.ts`, `realtimeEvents.ts`, `summaryActions.ts`, `usageEvents.ts`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts`). `useSessionDetail.ts` still re-exports `SessionMessage` and `TranscriptStatus` for existing component/test imports.

In Gobby's tmux session manager, real tmux treats semicolons inside inline `-e KEY=value` environment arguments as command syntax hazards. Route env values containing `;` through the private sourced env-file path, and use exact session targets of the form `=<session>:` for session-name operations to avoid prefix matches such as `agent` resolving to `agent-extra`.

The spawned-agent worker-safety rule `no-npx` was intentionally disabled for Gobby on 2026-05-07 because it was too broad: docs/tech-writer agents need `npx -y @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` for Mermaid validation, and npx is a runner rather than necessarily a package install. The bundled template `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/worker-safety/no-package-install.yaml` now has `no-npx.enabled=false`; neighboring install blockers (`no-npm-install`, `no-yarn-add`, `no-pip-install`, `no-uv-add`) remain enabled.

User clarified Linear task identity for Gobby sync: keep the task ref itself as the canonical identity (`#N`) and rely on the Linear project name (`gobby`, `gobby-cli`, etc.) as the namespace. Linear may still generate its own team issue key like `GOB-6`, but Gobby should treat that as secondary Linear metadata; user-facing Gobby output should emphasize the Gobby ref and project scope.

DaemonClient.check_health classifies connection failures by httpx exception type: httpx.ConnectError returns DaemonHealthError.NOT_RUNNING, while other httpx.HTTPError subclasses return their diagnostic string. Callers that distinguish an absent daemon must compare against the typed sentinel rather than treating None as a failure sentinel.

In the Gobby CLI daemon commands, PID liveness checks should use gobby.cli.utils._is_process_alive instead of os.kill(pid, 0), because the helper treats zombie/defunct processes as not alive and keeps status/health/stop behavior consistent.

WorkflowLoader returns None only when no matching workflow definition exists. A matching DB row whose workflow or pipeline definition cannot be parsed or validated raises ValueError; evaluate_workflow converts that into WORKFLOW_LOAD_ERROR so malformed definitions remain distinct from WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND.

The app-level project selector owns effectiveProjectId. App.tsx passes that project ID to scoped pages and their data hooks; pages must not create independent project-ID state, because backend resolution can otherwise fall back to the first project alphabetically. App.tsx remains the shell orchestrator while focused hooks under web/src/components/app handle project settings/sync and session actions.

Gwiki deep ask (`gwiki ask --deep`, task #18565) reuses the existing bounded agentic lanes: daemon uses exactly the read-only gwiki tools `search`, `read`, `backlinks`, and `sources`; direct uses the semantically equivalent VaultToolExecutor tools `search_vault`, `read_document`, `backlinks`, and `sources`. Deep citation validation checks cited `[[wiki pages]]` against the whole vault because the agent can discover pages after seed retrieval. Agentic provenance is honest end to end: daemon `turns` and `stop_reason` remain optional/provider-native, direct maps its concrete StopReason, and limit exits degrade with `deep_unavailable` unless `--require-ai` is set.

The bundled Bash language skill is src/gobby/install/shared/skills/bash. Its discovery rule covers .sh, .bash, .bats, common Bash dotfiles/config names, PKGBUILD, Bashfile, and shell template suffixes while excluding zsh/fish, .profile, Makefile, and Dockerfile. For standard Bats @test syntax, validate with shfmt -ln=bats and bats; ShellCheck should target Bash scripts rather than the Bats file. The skill is independently authored: Google Shell Style Guide is the attributed normative source, while the SkillsMP seed repositories are cited only for topic discovery because one uses FSL-1.1-ALv2 and the other declares no license.

Gobby web has ONE canonical button surface (styling consolidation Phase 1, 2026-07-27): React `Button` in web/src/components/ui/Button.tsx + buttonVariants.ts (cva). Variants: secondary (default; bordered transparent), primary (solid accent, true CTAs only: chat Send, Approve), accent (TINTED: --accent-tint bg, --accent text, accent-35% border; the canonical meaningful-action style), destructive, outline, ghost. Sizes: sm 28px/--text-xs/medium, md 32px, lg 40px, icon 32px square. Coarse-pointer 44px promotion is baked in; the boolean `dense` prop strips it for desktop-only chrome (activity-panel toolbars, app-header cluster) — this replaces the old `.activity-panel-toolbar .btn-sm` 28px specificity pin.
DetailActionButton (web/src/components/activity/fields/DetailPaneHeader.tsx) is a thin wrapper over Button, size=sm dense; since #19151 its DEFAULT variant is accent (tinted) — header actions read as Hide-Chat-style accent buttons; destructive stays destructive.
The `.btn` CSS system (web/src/styles/buttons.css) is being retired: Phase 1 C6 migrates all ~65 raw `btn btn-*` call sites onto ui/Button and deletes buttons.css. Never author new `.btn` usage or hand-rolled Tailwind buttons. Toolbar hook classes (`activity-panel-action-btn`, `activity-filter-button`) survive as layout hooks during attrition.
Still-current toolbar facts: `.activity-panel-toolbar` min-height var(--activity-panel-bar-height)=44px nowrap; ActivityPanelSearch renders input.activity-panel-search at var(--status-bar-control-height)=28px; tokens in web/src/styles/tokens.css (--activity-panel-bar-height 2.75rem, --status-bar-control-height 1.75rem, --activity-panel-row-height 2.25rem). Metadata chips: shared `.activity-chip` pill (text-2xs, radius 9999px) + accent/info/warning/error variants. Toggles: SwitchField → ui/Switch.tsx; since #19151 the SwitchField row is min-h-8 with the label adjacent to the toggle (gap-2, no justify-between).

compact_self handoff refreshes intentionally persist digest_fallback revisions with source_context_hash=NULL when cached summary metadata is stale. The fallback cannot claim the exact full-summary prompt context, so the scheduled background summary sees missing_summary_metadata and performs a full rebuild, restoring source hash and digest watermark. The reason on the later generation describes the preceding cached/fallback revision, not the newly generated summary.

SDK autonomous mode does NOT replace terminal mode. Terminal mode is permanent — it's how developers actually use Claude Code at the desktop. SDK autonomous is for Gobby-spawned agents. Web chat + /rc (remote control) is for session shifting to mobile or other devices. All three modes coexist.

Web project selection must have one app-shell source of truth. Use the app-level project-selection state/hook and thread the effective project ID into scoped pages and data hooks; do not create independent page-level project selection state, which can cause backend fallback project resolution.

Workflow definition drift hashing canonicalizes JSON by parsing and dumping with sorted keys and compact separators before SHA-256. This matches PostgreSQL JSONB row normalization, so serialization formatting does not create drift. Malformed definition JSON remains explicit via json.JSONDecodeError.
For the Gobby repository, never modify or commit directly to the `main` branch. Perform agent work on the active release/task branch and use isolated task worktrees for concurrent remediation.

In clone workflows, only the merge agent should close a task after the merge reaches main. Autonomous development agents may hand off with needs_review and QA with review_approved; interactive agents should instead close when requirements are met or reopen/release their claim.

In Gobby, lifecycle close validation in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_lifecycle_validation.py now strips benign zero-failure tokens such as `0 failed`, `zero failures`, and `failed=0` before matching failure-feedback regexes. NEVER add startup code that kills other processes on ports. _clear_port() using lsof + SIGTERM was added to GobbyRunner.run() to handle orphaned test daemons, but it caused e2e tests to kill the production daemon. The correct approach to port isolation is preventing collisions at allocation time (find_free_port without SO_REUSEADDR + excluded ports), not killing processes at startup.

Memory Dream architecture (epic #19251; #19254 commit 9978080c2, #19255 commit 3494aa8ed, #19256 commit 73b2f5fd5, #19257 commit ef327aa66, #19258 commit 872d18a18, #19264 commit 859b3cc68, #19265 commit dedcbef8b, #19266 commit 87515506f, #19273 commits 1332098dc+92eed9be2, #19274 commit ac7393cd4):

Admission (storage.py, migration 348): PostgreSQL enforces at most one status='running' row in memory_dream_runs via partial unique index idx_memory_dream_runs_single_running. 'running' marks the ADMITTED run (MemoryDreamStore.admit_run returns admitted | coalesced | conflict; the index is the race arbiter via UniqueViolation). Aggregate fan-out rows use status='started' and never pass through 'running'. 'partial' is terminal; shared terminal set is storage.RUN_TERMINAL_STATUSES. Coverage: equivalent normalized options coalesce; an all-due run covers a project request when dry_run/skip_consolidation/memory_type/full_sweep match and include_global is not False; else conflict. Durable progress persists in the checkpoint JSONB column (DreamCheckpoint). Constraint repair lives ONLY in migrations — ensure_schema must not ADD CONSTRAINT (MEMORY_DREAM_RUNTIME_NORMALIZERS in tests/storage/test_migration_contract.py).

Execution (#19255): run bodies live in gobby.memory.dream.orchestrator (DreamSweepOrchestrator); service.py is the facade, and service._stream_sweep is the seam lock/cancel tests patch. One work unit = select ≤25 candidates (planner_batch_size clamped to WORK_UNIT_MAX_CANDIDATES=25) → required evidence → serial planner → validate → apply → checkpoint, under work_unit_timeout_seconds (default 1500, enforced PER unit via asyncio.timeout in _run_unit). Planner pages run serially so Dream holds ≤1 host spawn-cold slot; the request sets total_timeout_seconds=1200 (PLANNER_TOTAL_DEADLINE_SECONDS) — TextGenerationService.generate_json enforces it. Planner absence, failed planner page, exhausted fallback, evidence-channel exhaustion (RelatedEvidenceError), or unit timeout raise typed DreamDependencyError: no implicit keeps, no cursor stamps, single-scope run failed with checkpoint stop_reason='dependency_failure', candidates remain due. skip_consolidation=true is inventory-only. Dry runs keep the immutable ordered eligible-ID snapshot contract in 25-candidate units, and (#19266, commit 87515506f) mirror the sweep path's durability: run_dry_run folds units into self.totals, persists a checkpoint after every unit plus a final terminal checkpoint (stop_reason 'drained' on completion — the orchestrator's stop_reason DEFAULT is 'drained', set in __init__), persists the dependency_failure checkpoint before re-raising, and checks window_open before each unit (window_exhausted → status 'partial' via the path-agnostic handling in _execute_run_locked). Terminal dry-run rows carry a non-null checkpoint, so the CLI's checkpoint-change rendering shows progress for dry runs too. A live 1000-candidate dry run takes ~35 min (40 units; each unit's serial planner page is a spawn-cold codex exec taking 1-3+ min).

Live mutating acceptance (#19271, run 3e010239, 2026-07-29): full project-scope drain of 2,866 candidates in 115 units took ~2h (~25 candidates/min); actions delete 218 / keep 2042 / promote 35 / refresh 557 / review 16, mutations 823, exactly one applied snapshot row per reviewed candidate (2,866). Planner refreshes colliding with the unique-content constraint log WARNING 'Memory dream action failed', are recorded in summary.error_details, and advance the candidate's cooldown cursor — designed dedup behavior. The other live warning class ('keep action requires non-empty memory_id') was a bug fixed by #19274 (commit ac7393cd4): validate_dream_plan deliberately emits id-less _keep_marker actions ('Audit-only keep with no candidate id') when the planner references unknown/missing candidate ids, and the primary _apply_action dispatcher now short-circuits them as no-ops instead of failing _required_memory_id (the legacy non-transactional path already tolerated them). summary['snapshots'] is a PER-CALL DELTA (#19273 commits 1332098dc+92eed9be2): apply_dream_plan counts via MemoryDreamStore.count_snapshots (COUNT(*) WHERE run_id AND applied) before/after, because the orchestrator SUMS unit summaries — reporting the run-cumulative count per unit inflated totals quadratically (166,741 reported vs 2,866 actual pre-fix).

Scheduling (#19256, extracted by #19264): aggregate/all-due lifecycle lives in gobby.memory.dream.aggregate._AggregateDreamRunner. MemoryDreamService remains the stable facade and single-scope executor; it constructs one runner, keeps execution-lock acquisition in run_all_due_projects, and delegates locked aggregate work plus execute_all_due_projects_run. Aggregate preview fan-out, round-robin passes, child-run lifecycle, durable aggregate checkpoints, and parent terminal persistence are owned by aggregate.py. The runner invokes service._open_scope_sweep, service._run_scope_unit, service._close_scope_sweep, and service._admission_window_open through its typed host protocol so instance monkeypatches remain effective; service._run_nested_target and service._stream_sweep also remain service-level seams. Mutating aggregate work runs one unit per due scope per pass (stable order from list_dream_scopes: projects by id, global last), with backlog re-enumerated between passes; zero-candidate/short/no-progress scopes drop out via WorkUnitOutcome.drained(unit_size). DreamSweepOrchestrator is steppable: run_unit()/finalize_sweep(); run_sweep() loops them. max_runtime_seconds (default 14400) bounds EVERY run via an admission-deadline check before each unit (orchestrator.window_open / service._admission_window_open — the test seam). Stop states: window exhaustion → status='partial', stop_reason='window_exhausted', INFO only; dependency failure → coordinator stops, aggregate 'partial' + exactly ONE WARNING (failing scope's child row 'failed', cut-off scopes 'partial'); structural per-scope failures isolated at ERROR (aggregate 'failed' only when all failed). Cron: schedule_cron default '0 2 * * *', dry_run=False always (allow_unattended_mutations removed). MemoryDreamConfig (pre-0.5 schema, extra=forbid) removed allow_unattended_mutations/planner_max_concurrency/page_size/candidate_page_timeout_seconds/scan_limit/max_scan_rows/stale_age_days; added max_runtime_seconds, work_unit_timeout_seconds, evidence_channel_timeout_seconds, evidence_retry_attempts, evidence_phase_timeout_seconds (wired through related.py via _ChannelContext; module constants are the defaults). Web MemoryKnowledgeSection mirrors these knobs.

Triggers (#19257, wiring fixed by #19265): all Dream triggers are always asynchronous. One daemon-owned MemoryDreamCoordinator (gobby.memory.dream.coordinator) is constructed in runner_init/orchestration.init_orchestration, stored as runner.memory_dream_coordinator, AND (#19265, commit dedcbef8b) copied into ServiceContainer by init_servers (field memory_dream_coordinator on app_context.ServiceContainer). The container is what HTTP routes and MCP tools getattr against — a runner-only attribute is invisible to those surfaces and yields 503 'memory dream coordinator is unavailable' while cron (runner attribute) still works. General ServiceContainer gotcha: any service resolved via server.services needs BOTH a container field and an init_servers pass; MagicMock/SimpleNamespace services in tests accept any attribute and mask missing wiring, so wiring regression tests must construct a real ServiceContainer (see test_route_resolves_coordinator_from_real_service_container). Cron (register_memory_dream_cron takes coordinator=, uses coordinator.service inline for its completion report), HTTP routes (getattr(server.services, 'memory_dream_coordinator')), and MCP tools (dream_coordinator_resolver threaded setup_internal_registries → create_memory_registry → register_memory_dream_tools) all resolve the same instance — never construct MemoryDreamService ad hoc. Coordinator.trigger(options)/trigger_all_due_projects(**kw) perform admission then launch execute_run/execute_all_due_projects_run as a named task 'memory-dream:<run_id>'; response contract: admitted → {success, run_id, status='running', coalesced=False} (HTTP 202); coalesced → +active view with checkpoint progress (HTTP 200); conflict → error_code='dream_run_conflict' + conflict view (HTTP 409); launch failure → record_run_failure terminal row + {status:'failed', run_id} (HTTP 500); disabled → plain failure (HTTP 400). No public wait parameter anywhere; MAX_BACKGROUND_DREAM_TASKS, the MCP BoundedSemaphore, module task set, and cleanup_background_dream_tasks are deleted — HTTPServer shutdown calls coordinator.aclose() (cancel = interruption, not failure; restart recovery owns row state). Executor crash records failure via done-callback; failed result only warns (executor already persisted status). memory_dream_status exposes durable checkpoint via run.checkpoint for running AND terminal runs. Daemon restart mid-run marks the admitted run 'interrupted' (verified live on run 90fcf455: mutations already applied stay applied, stamped candidates drop out of the next run's due scope, snapshots remain revert-capable).

CLI (#19258): gobby memory dream POSTs the trigger with a fixed 30s network timeout, prints the run ID immediately (started or coalesced), then polls GET /memory/dream/{run_id} every 2s (_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS), printing a checkpoint line only when the checkpoint dict changes. --timeout is a CLIENT-side polling deadline (default 0 = wait until terminal); deadline expiry exits 0 and Ctrl-C exits via click.Abort — both leave the daemon run active and print 'gobby memory dream status <run_id>' as the resume command. Terminal rendering: completed exits 0 (aggregate runs render from summary + plan.runs, inventory-only runs from plan.candidate_ids/candidate_count with a 'candidates remain due' notice, scoped runs via summary/dry-run actions); partial/failed/interrupted exit 1 with run ID, stop reason, completed counts, remaining, backlog. Terminal detection imports storage.RUN_TERMINAL_STATUSES. The status subcommand renders the checkpoint line too. Tests patch gobby.cli.memory.dream.time.sleep/monotonic and drive a MagicMock client with side_effect response queues (helpers _dream_client/_dream_started/_dream_run_status in tests/cli/test_memory_cli.py).

Test conventions: patch build_raw_plan/gather_related_evidence in the orchestrator namespace (RelatedEvidenceSession and revert_dream_run still patch in service); sweep tests need a non-None llm_service — use MagicMock + _keep_all_planner() in tests/memory/test_dream.py (_delete_all_planner() forces snapshotting mutations; the fake DB answers SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM memory_dream_snapshots). _FakeDreamDB is NON-transactional, so apply tests in test_dream.py exercise the legacy dispatch (_apply_action_legacy — the seam kept for non-transactional protocol test doubles); force the primary transactional path by subclassing the fake with a contextlib.nullcontext transaction() (see test_apply_skips_audit_keep_marker_without_memory_id). Aggregate-private helpers and logger capture come from gobby.memory.dream.aggregate, and aggregate seam regressions must patch the service instance lifecycle methods including _close_scope_sweep to prove host routing. Coordinator tests use the _coordinator_service harness (patches _open_scope_sweep/_run_scope_unit; child run rows are real against the fake DB); trigger surfaces are tested with fake coordinators (tests/servers/routes/test_memory_routes.py, tests/mcp_proxy/tools/test_memory.py) and the real coordinator over service mocks in tests/memory/test_dream_coordinator.py. Dry-run checkpoint tests record persisted checkpoints by wrapping DreamSweepOrchestrator._persist_checkpoint and force window exhaustion by patch.object on window_open with an iterator lambda. Global memories = project_id=PERSONAL_PROJECT_ID + is_global=True (create_memory requires project_id since #19003).

Use configured feature profiles and canonical provider-scoped candidates instead of hardcoding full Claude model IDs. `gobby.config.feature_base.normalize_feature_candidate` normalizes Claude labels containing haiku, sonnet, or opus to `claude/haiku`, `claude/sonnet`, or `claude/opus`; feature defaults and runtime candidate requests share that path. Claude provider implementation is split across `claude.py`, `claude_sdk.py`, `claude_runtime.py`, and `claude_payloads.py`.

Plan-mode structured scratch writes are governed by src/gobby/providers/path_policy.py:is_plan_scratch_path. ProviderMetadata.user_directory maps claude=.claude, codex=.codex, droid=.factory, grok=.grok, qwen=.qwen, agy=.gemini. The predicate requires absolute or home-relative paths, resolves symlinks/traversal, and permits only the active provider home plus OS temp roots. Plan workflow rules call plan_write_paths_allowed; Claude web chat and Codex/Droid managed permission gates share the same predicate. Multi-file writes fail closed unless every target is the plan artifact or approved scratch path, lifecycle hygiene retains precedence, and shell mutation policy is unchanged.

Feedback-lesson-loop design (plan .gobby/plans/feedback-lesson-loop.md, approved after 12 adversarial rounds, epic #18719; spike docs/spikes/feedback-lesson-loop.md, task #18598). Core decisions: (1) Lesson-domain partition: required `lesson-domain:<code|plan>` tag derived at record time from a total source_kind→domain map, fail-closed in record(); centralized CODE_DOMAIN_EXCLUDED_TAGS applied as tags_none on semantic recall AND both file-recall paths; plan-domain recall is positive opt-in only — semantic ranking is never the safety mechanism. New source kinds: plan_review, task_validation (pr_verdict, human_correction deferred). (2) Class-scoped identity for every multi-class recorder: pattern_id `plan-review:<lesson_type>:<category>:<check-key>`, `epic-qa:<lesson_type>:<check-key>`, `task-validation:recurring-validation-failure:<check-key>`; explicit validated kebab-case check_key with `check-key:`/`category:` tags; deterministic `list_check_keys` enumeration is the identity-resolution mechanism (versioned catalog is the documented escalation; canonicalization gate explicitly declined). Five reserved lesson_type classes: reviewer-miss, fixer-induced-defect, recurring-validation-failure, qa-miss, validation-miss. (3) Recording ownership: the reviser/coordinator side holding cross-round ground truth records; reviewed agents never grade themselves; enhancer never records. Unproven classification mints nothing. (4) Evidence: immutable pre-M1 snapshots via side-effecting `prepare_plan_review_round` → `plan_review_evidence` table (per-section hash manifest from a trusted producer; agent-generated hashes prove nothing); two-phase `bind_evidence_run`; lease bounds only pre-bind rows; per-class evidence bundles (reviewer-miss: unchanged sections; fixer-induced: causal changed sections + prior finding). (5) Interactive approval: unified commit order (durable pre-finalization intent → apply manifest → V1 checkpoint → lossless finalize stamping lesson_mint_status=pending → mint checkpoint); V1 round checkpoint fence is the enforced durable step-2 marker; preparation owns recovery via a deterministic drain (pending-apply no-drift convergence checkpoints applied then drains; drift executes the atomic pending-plus-drift revoked transition); incomplete-round rule scoped to rejection rounds and pre-intent crashes only; `pending_lesson_mint` refuse-gate blocks new rounds until the mint tail completes. (6) Stage-native mint: idempotent mint at approve_review (errors never block the verdict), workflow-owned single backfill via `backfill_plan_review_lessons`; activation boundary is planning-stage-only — all other stages' approve/reject byte-for-byte unchanged. (7) Promotion: no promotion.py change — explicit guardrail_target honored at occurrence 2+; plan classes → checklist, qa-miss → checklist, validation-miss → validation. (8) Retirement: explicit `retire_review_lesson` (never overload record(decision=stale)); retags confirmed→stale under the ReviewLearningPatternMutation advisory lock. (9) Expansion serialization: dependency edges come only from explicit manifest depends_on; shared-target-file pairs need explicit edges (7.1 depends on both 3.2 and 5.2 because 2.1/5.2/7.1 all touch mcp_proxy/tools/review_learning.py).

Plan-review repair preparation is owned end to end by `PlanReviewEvidenceService.prepare_plan_review_round`. Current contract after tasks #19211 and #19241 (commit bdd45d095): canonicalize prior resolutions, attestations, submitted SweepScope, and its digest; perform one settled index operation when repaired findings exist; derive current CandidateSiteInventory and `current_sweep_scope` from finalized prior evidence plus the current snapshot; validate proof against the submitted scope; compute `required_scope_delta` and `inventory_churn`; and atomically persist both scopes, deltas, requirements, and carried context. Repository churn does not refuse the round. Current scope drives downstream coverage, while deltas are adversary inputs. The MCP producer delegates to the same `review_evidence_preparation.py` derivation helper.

For Gobby 0.4.0 docs, `docs/guides/webhooks-and-plugins.md` should document hook extension webhooks (`hook_extensions.webhooks`) and pipeline webhooks as the supported webhook surfaces. Python workflow plugin actions such as `plugin:<name>:<action>` are retired/stale patterns; installer-copied `.gobby/plugins/` files and the `claude-plugins` skill hub are separate from workflow action plugins.

gobby-cli design decision for session wiki scope: gwiki sync-sessions should default Detect scope to machine-global topic `sessions`, preserving daemon page `project:` as `session_project` frontmatter provenance. Explicit `--project`/`--topic` remain escape hatches. Tracking context: gobby-cli #940 / session-wiki Model B.

When gsqz or other output compression mangles tool output (ripgrep, grep, search results), file a bug task immediately instead of just working around it. Mangled output forces agents to fall back to slower approaches (Read instead of Grep), defeating the purpose of the optimization. Track these so the compression can be improved.

As of commit 5e6dc8573 for Gobby task #15476, the daemon exposes `/api/embeddings/status`, `POST /api/embeddings`, and `/api/embeddings/doctor`. Status is sourced from AICapability.EMBED, generation uses `gobby.search.embeddings.generate_embeddings` with `config.embeddings.model/api_base/api_key/dim`, and responses expose only safe endpoint/config metadata with no raw API keys.

Gobby's shared workflow TemplateEngine in src/gobby/workflows/templates.py uses Jinja2 SandboxedEnvironment with StrictUndefined. Pipeline exec, prompt, and MCP argument templates therefore fail the step on missing variables instead of silently rendering empty strings. Established by task #16879 / commit b02cb2cc7.

Task #17250 decomposed src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/backends/codex.py by extracting Codex app-server turn notification streaming into src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/backends/codex_turns.py. CodexWebChatBackend keeps health/thread guards plus approval translation/handling facades for existing tests, while codex_turns.py owns delta extraction, notification handler registration, tool event replay, transcript fallback, usage normalization, and DoneEvent emission. A pre-existing Ruff format drift in src/gobby/workflows/engine/core.py was also normalized during validation.

The daemon constructs SessionLivenessMonitor after HookManager during app lifespan startup because the monitor depends on HookManager summary dispatch. EventHandlers therefore receives the running monitor through set_liveness_monitor, and session_end marks the canonical platform session recently handled before cleanup/status work.

Legacy task status fields may remain in compatibility and export surfaces, but new workflow logic and tests must use canonical projected task state from closed_at, escalation metadata, and current_stage.state. Do not add new internal state checks based on status.

Gobby CLI commands should use the top-level CliRuntime's shared HubDatabase via runtime.require_database(); Click teardown is the sole owner and closer. Short-lived standalone managers must use their ownership context managers so PostgreSQL connections close on success, early return, and exceptions.

Detection manifests use engine version 1 in src/gobby/agents/detection. load_manifest() strictly validates dotted-numeric versions, unique lowercase rule IDs, blocked-rule reasons, and the three regions whole_recent, bottom_non_empty_lines(N), and prompt_box. compile_manifest() caches compiled rules by SHA-256 content fingerprint, sorts matches by priority, and returns MatchEvaluation with controlled invalid_pattern or pattern_timeout issues. All data-controlled regexes go through safe_regex.py, which enforces a 2,048-character pattern limit and a fixed 10ms search timeout.

Task #15326 added docs/research/cron-durable-dispatch-semantics.md defining target cron semantics as durable dispatch: pipeline and agent_spawn cron runs become terminal status dispatched after child IDs are persisted; shell and handler stay inline until separate observable child-run records exist. docs/guides/cron-scheduler.md now says internal dispatcher and pipeline-heartbeat automation live in SystemAutomationLoop and cron history should represent real scheduled jobs only.

Two dev mode detection functions:

1. `is_dev_mode(project_path)` in `src/gobby/utils/dev.py` — checks if the project IS the gobby source repo by looking for `src/gobby/install/shared/` dir. Use this when gating behavior based on whether the current project is gobby itself.

2. `_is_dev_mode()` in `src/gobby/cli/installers/service.py` — checks if running from a dev install (sys.executable in gobby project dir or CWD is gobby project with .venv). Used by the service installer to decide install strategy.

Bundled agent sync ownership is defined by src/gobby/agents/sync.py::_is_sync_managed_bundled_agent: project_id must be null, source must be installed/template, and tags must include gobby. Update, restore, and orphan cleanup paths should use that same predicate before mutating existing workflow_definition agent rows.

Task CLI policy is now split cleanly: `src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_tool.py` no longer hardcodes any `gobby tasks` shell block. Native task CLI mutation blocking lives in the installed/bundled `block-gobby-tasks-cli` rules-engine rule, which allows read-only commands such as `gobby tasks list --ready` and blocks mutating subcommands. Hook-level tests should assert the native handler allows task CLI paths; rules tests cover mutation/read-only behavior.

Wiki health reports are generated artifacts from gwiki health and should remain ignored rather than tracked. GwikiGateway.health() may normalize a report payload's leading 'Wiki health report' line to a Markdown H1 in the generated health report.

SDK client initialization was extracted from session-lifecycle.yaml into claude-sdk-lifecycle.yaml (#8756). The new workflow (priority 11, sources: claude_sdk, claude_sdk_web_chat) handles on_before_agent init (plan_mode, mode_level, baseline files, memory/task sync, session context injection, skills, task context, pre-existing error policy) with its own _sdk_initialized guard variable. The _session_initialized variable was removed from session-lifecycle.yaml entirely. on_pre_compact in claude-sdk-lifecycle resets _sdk_initialized so re-init fires after context loss.

ACP golden contract fixtures live in tests/adapters/test_acp_contract_fixtures.py with JSONL fixtures under tests/fixtures/acp_contract. They fake subprocess stdin/stdout to validate supported ACP client request shapes and normalized streamed message/thought chunks. Re-recording guidance belongs in tests/fixtures/acp_contract/README.md; do not retain Gemini-specific fixture or client assumptions after the Gemini removal.

All installer uninstall functions must respect GOBBY_HOOKS_DIR env var for test isolation. Pattern: `Path(os.environ.get('GOBBY_HOOKS_DIR', str(Path.home() / '.gobby' / 'hooks')))`. Tests using --all flag must mock ALL uninstallers (claude, gemini, codex, copilot, cursor, windsurf), not just the ones being asserted on, because --all auto-detects installed CLIs on the developer's machine and will call any unmocked uninstaller for real. Fixed in windsurf.py:199 and test_cli_install.py (commit 8ae3fee7).

Task #17256 decomposed src/gobby/cli/tasks/crud.py by keeping Click command wrappers and the legacy test patch surface in crud.py, while moving command bodies into _crud_listing.py, _crud_detail.py, _crud_mutations.py, shared choices/helper into _crud_common.py, and dependency injection into _crud_services.py.

Product decision for activity-panel Tasks UI: remove the kanban/board view and the List|Board selector. The activity panel Tasks surface should be list-only; do not reintroduce the board/drag-and-drop stage lanes unless the user explicitly reverses this decision. This supersedes the prior one-surface UI memory that asked for a Jira-style activity Tasks board.

Gobby project convention: use XML-ish semantic tags such as `<project-memory>` for model-facing context blocks that agents should read as named structure. Use HTML comment fences such as `<!-- gobby:injected-context:begin -->` / `<!-- gobby:injected-context:end -->` for machine-facing injected context boundaries that Gobby may detect, strip, replace, or deduplicate while staying render-hidden in Markdown. HTML comments are still visible tokens to models, so they are a transport/cleanup fence rather than true hidden context.

Codewiki staged publication reconciliation (#18252, commit 14071a327): `_meta/codewiki-stage/manifest.json` is private v2 `StageManifest { fingerprint, force_full_hash_scan }`. Exact fingerprints resume with the sticky flag. Drift in source hashes, AI mode/settings/routes/outcomes, aggregate candidates, snapshots, or `since_changed` retains staged bytes, atomically records the new fingerprint, and forces `ReusePlan` plus `DocSink` to ignore the `--since` shortcut and perform full per-page freshness checks. Version, canonical project-root, normalized-scope, missing, corrupt, and legacy v1 manifest changes reseed. Successful publication removes the stage and clears the flag; fail-closed link validation still protects live bytes.

In gobby-cli daemon text generation, `ai.text_generate.*` is the CLI standalone/direct namespace only. The daemon does not accept `ai.text_generate.*` config_store writes; daemon-side named local endpoints are configured under `ai.generation.local.endpoints.<name>` and selected with provider `local:<name>` plus request-level `model`, `profile`, or `candidates`. `GET /api/providers/models` reports named local endpoints with `source: "config"` and model objects (`value`/`label`).

Design decision for Gobby cross-session file edit protection: guard all Git-visible dirty states (tracked, staged, deleted, renamed, and untracked) using atomic before_tool reservations scoped by machine ID + canonical Git worktree root + repo-relative path. Same-worktree foreign owners block; separate worktrees do not. Notify only the blocked requester with the owner session and gobby-agents:send_message guidance. Release claims on real session end, retain across compact because compact keeps the same Gobby session, and let the first guarded writer claim a dirty file with no recorded owner. Ship as a bundled enabled-by-default rule while preserving the installed DB operator toggle. Deprecated /clear parent-child handoff cleanup is tracked separately as task #18742.

In Gobby, chat attachment cleanup for cleared web chat conversations must delete chat_attachments metadata before deleting chat_messages, because attachment message_id uses ON DELETE SET NULL and deleting messages first loses the link. Use storage.chat_attachments.delete_attachments_for_conversations(...) to collect conversation-bound and message-bound attachment records, then unlink their local files after metadata deletion.

After task #14248, live dry-run of `gobby tasks repair-lifecycle --provenance expansion-run:expand-1242485f202e` exposed a repair edge case: historical phase-wrapper parents could start at holistic_qa while leaves already had development/pr/merge, causing naive parent-derived repair to propose removing development from leaves. Task #14251 fixed LifecycleRepair to skip removing development from development-first children and to repair historical phase wrappers to development-first shapes when their parent has no manifest.

For Gobby release-gwiki.yml Windows gwiki builds under Git Bash, normalize RUNNER_TEMP and GITHUB_ENV with cygpath -u before Bash tools; convert only the final pdfium DLL path back with cygpath -w for PDFIUM_BUNDLE_LIB. Use Strawberry Perl for OPENSSL_SRC_PERL and set the ARM64 MSVC linker explicitly for aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.

When mocking PromptLoader for tests that use validation or other template-rendering code, the render mock must pass through context variables (not return a static string). Use `side_effect=lambda path, ctx: '\n'.join(str(v) for v in ctx.values() if v)` so tests that assert specific content appears in the rendered prompt still pass. A static mock like `render.return_value='fixed string'` will break tests that check for file_context, criteria_text, etc.

Long-running or timing-sensitive gwiki CLI smoke fixtures should expose test-only timeout knobs via environment variables with conservative defaults, e.g. `GWIKI_TEST_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECS` defaulting to 15 seconds for HTTP fixture watchdogs.

Gobby web MCP management now lives in Chat's MCP Activity tab. The top-level MCP sidebar/nav page route was removed; legacy #mcp entry and /mcp browse actions route to Chat and select the MCP activity tab instead. Keep server import out of this surface; durable import/config belongs in Config.

For Gobby Postgres migration docs, comments, and user-facing text, describe the runtime hub as the PostgreSQL hub or hub database. SQLite references should be explicitly scoped to `DEPRECATED_SQLITE_IMPORT` migration-only tooling, `DEPRECATED_SQLITE_IMPORT_TEST_ONLY` fixtures/LocalDatabase compatibility, or historical archives; gcode/code-index references should describe the external gcode toolchain over the PostgreSQL hub/pg_search.

Gobby web UI responsiveness uses a 768px breakpoint through web/src/hooks/useIsMobile.ts for component-level adaptation; do not rely on Tailwind responsive variants for product UI logic. For persisted desktop preferences, mobile should derive an effective value without overwriting the desktop localStorage value. The older Workflows-page CSS/tag specifics are implementation detail and should be verified when editing those surfaces.

Telegram DM enrollment contract (task #18850, commit d6cb589ed): when a Telegram channel's allow_from is empty, only the first exact private /start atomically binds and persists that sender's numeric Telegram user ID. Group messages and other first DMs cannot claim the channel. Once bound, unknown Telegram DMs are acknowledged for poll-offset advancement but dropped before identity resolution, message/attachment persistence, session creation, or responder dispatch. Re-enrollment requires explicitly clearing allow_from through local channel configuration.

For Gobby local generation routing, prefer the local model `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat` over Qwen models for feature-profile/local-fallback planning because the Qwen models are too slow for this purpose. Keep built-in feature profiles cloud-only; use named local endpoint opt-in such as `local:lm-studio/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat` when local generation is explicitly desired.

Step-scoped MCP enforcement now treats gobby-sessions:compact_self as a capability-neutral allowlist exemption: explicit blocked_mcp_tools are evaluated first and still deny it, while omission from allowed_mcp_tools permits it. Focused parameterized coverage lives in tests/workflows/test_step_enforcement.py. Implemented for epic #19213 leaf #19214 in commit 886c6651f.

For cross-stack field removal, trace the model, CRUD/serialization, protocols/backends, managers/services, MCP/CLI/routes, sync and bundled content, and focused tests. For PostgreSQL schema changes, keep the current baseline schema and any future numeric SQL migration above baseline version 305 synchronized; validate both fresh-baseline and populated-hub paths.

WorkflowLoader resolves filesystem project scopes through .gobby/project.json via get_project_context, then uses the canonical UUID for workflow and pipeline database filters and cache keys. Discovery delegates to the same loader resolver so path- and ID-keyed calls share cache entries.

Managed web-chat permission and plan behavior is shared through ManagedWebChatPermissionsMixin. ACP providers use ACPManagedChatSession; Codex and Droid have distinct wire protocols and use CodexManagedChatSession and DroidManagedChatSession. The unified mixin owns pending-plan detection, broadcast, permission-mode synchronization, and post-plan-mode retention. Keep Droid session/process orchestration in backends/droid.py, with plan helpers in droid_plan.py and permission resolution in droid_permissions.py.

Task #13863 added the Phase 6 lifecycle board frontend contract. The web stage row shape consumed by the tests/components is `name`, `display_name`, `category`, `state`, `review_policy`, and `updated_at`; `web/src/lib/stageActions.ts` is the single authoring site for `StageAdvanceAction`, `StageStateView`, `LifecycleTask`, `resolveAdvanceAction`, `taskAtStage`, `taskStateAt`, and `currentStage`. `LifecycleBoard` supports both `stagesRegistry` and `registry` props, persists the Hide blocked toggle under `lifecycle-board:hide-blocked`, and derives visible swimlane columns from each task's stage rows.

BuildProfile drift invariant (src/gobby/storage/build_profiles.py): when adding a new BuildProfile field that is part of the bundled-row hash, you must update THREE payload builders consistently or unchanged installed bundled rows will be misclassified as user-edited and skipped on upgrade. (1) Add the field to _profile_payload (template hash basis) AND _row_payload (current DB-row hash). (2) Shift _legacy_row_payload forward one generation: set its body to the PREVIOUS _row_payload shape (the field set used by the last release, WITHOUT the new field). The sync() drift guard skips a row only when `current_hash != stored_hash AND legacy_hash != stored_hash`; an unchanged pre-field bundled row has stored_hash == legacy_hash (old shape), so legacy_hash matching lets it refresh instead of being treated as a user edit. _hash_payload uses json.dumps(sort_keys=True) so dict field ORDER is irrelevant — only the field SET matters. Also touch _insert_profile/_insert_params/_update_profile/_profile_from_row/_profile_dataclass_profile and add a baseline column + numbered migration + the build_profiles.yaml profiles. Precedent: plan_enhancement_rounds added this way under gobby-#17141 (migration 288).

Gobby PostgreSQL bootstrap now uses database_url directly in bootstrap.yaml with 0600 permissions for both root runtime and generated isolated gcode helper homes. database_url_ref, keyring refs, daemon:gobby:postgres_database_url, the local runtime database-url broker route, and local_cli_token-based DSN brokering are obsolete/removed.

MCP default installer configs should persist optional secret-backed CLI args as $secret:<name> references, not plaintext values; runtime secret resolution in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/client_manager/secrets.py resolves args along with env and headers and strips unresolved secret args without logging the secret name.

In the Gobby repo, `cd web && npm run build:setup` updates the tracked `web/dist-setup/cli.mjs`. It may recreate `src/gobby/install/shared/setup/setup.mjs`, but that shared bundle was deliberately removed and should remain untracked rather than be committed.

In gobby-cli `.config/nextest.toml`, the `required` version field accepts a bare version such as `0.9.133`; comparator syntax like `>=0.9.133` is rejected by cargo-nextest's config parser in this repo. Treat the bare version as the minimum required nextest version.

Session storage recognizes statuses active, paused, handoff_ready, completed, cancelled, closed, expired, and deleted. Expired and deleted remain guarded terminal states for generic storage, bulk, and API status writes. Confirmed hook activity routes through update_status_from_activity, which accepts only active/paused, atomically updates any non-deleted row including expired, resets transcript_processed, refreshes updated_at, and emits one session_updated notification; deleted remains irreversible. Registration, web-chat activation, and transcript-driven terminal revival paths remain available for their existing callers. Implemented by task #18384 / commit 9a22190d5.

In gwiki index, index-time Qdrant/FalkorDB projection sync failures are non-fatal but surfaced through `IndexReport.degradations` in `crates/gwiki/src/commands/index.rs`. `sync_qdrant_vectors` reports service `qdrant` and `sync_falkor_graph` reports service `falkordb`; `render_index` serializes the structured `DegradationKind` array and renders text labels via `degradation_label`. Documentation should describe `gwiki index` as synchronously updating Qdrant vectors and the FalkorDB graph after PostgreSQL indexing, not writing daemon sync flags for delayed daemon-owned index work.

Web app shell architecture (July 2026): the legacy sidebar was replaced by ActivityPanel inside web/src/components/chat/ChatPage.tsx. AppErrorBoundary now scopes the App header, FilesProvider/chat surface, modal region, ActivityPanel, and the root mount in web/src/main.tsx, so render failures stay contained by region.

HTTPServer.skill_manager (services.skill_manager, app_context.py) is a LocalSkillManager (the storage manager with metadata + file mixins), NOT the SkillManager wrapper from src/gobby/skills/manager.py — there is no .storage attribute on it. Routes in src/gobby/servers/routes/skills.py must call mixin methods directly (get_skill_files, get_skill_file, update_skill_file). Route tests use a MagicMock skill_manager, which silently accepts wrong attribute paths — verify new skills routes against the live daemon, not just mocks.

Prefer named agent definitions for spawning when an appropriate definition exists, because they supply the intended workflow and runtime configuration. Agent definitions use timeout as their definition-level runtime limit; max_turns is not a supported definition field. Normal cooperative completion uses gobby-agents:end_agent_run, while kill_agent or stop_agent are cancellation and cleanup controls.

Memory limits on macOS: RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA are NOT enforced for Mach VM allocations on Darwin, so setrlimit cannot cap process memory there. Gobby's memory enforcement is therefore polling-based: MemoryWatchdogHandler (src/gobby/agents/memory_watchdog.py, wired into AgentLifecycleMonitor._check_loop) sums psutil RSS over tmux pane process trees and kills via the existing kill_agent + cleanup_agent path. Config lives on TmuxConfig (agent_memory_limit_gb per tree, agent_memory_total_limit_gb aggregate with 0 = 50% of physical RAM, warn/critical system pressure thresholds). torch MPS memory is capped separately via torch.mps.set_per_process_memory_fraction / PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO because MPS unified-memory allocations are unbounded anonymous memory. Established during incident #18196 remediation.

gwiki ask is read-only in both gobby-cli and the daemon. Generation is requested exactly when llm or deep is true; deep ask uses bounded read-only search/read/backlinks/sources lanes and propagates through GwikiGateway.ask, GET /api/wiki/ask, and MCP wiki_ask without WikiUpdateCoordinator.

Codewiki refresh is a JSON-body API: POST /api/code-index/codewiki/refresh accepts {root_path, project_id?, out_dir?, ai?}, where root_path must be an absolute daemon-side path. Generated hooks must send Content-Type: application/json and a JSON body, not query parameters. An accepted:false response means nothing was scheduled and its reason should be surfaced.

Async FastAPI handlers in src/gobby/servers/routes/skills.py offload synchronous skill-manager and database work with starlette.concurrency.run_in_threadpool(partial(...)). Route responsiveness can be verified with httpx.ASGITransport plus threading.Event: block the sync worker, issue a second request, and assert it completes before releasing the worker.

Telegram inbound media contract: TelegramAdapter.parse_webhook normalizes photo (largest size), document, voice, and video into attachment messages with captions preserved and a token-free metadata_json.telegram_attachment descriptor. BaseChannelAdapter.download_inbound_attachments is the generic adapter hook; Telegram resolves getFile, downloads with its initialized client, then stores bytes through AttachmentManager. InboundCommunications persists the message and CommsAttachment rows atomically via LocalCommunicationsStore.create_message_with_attachments, cleaning downloaded files on failure so polling retries cannot acknowledge half-stored media. Implemented in task #17891, commit dc1620b30.

InternalToolRegistry context injection pattern: Tools that need session context (like canvas tools) declare a `_context: Any = None` parameter. The `_` prefix causes it to be excluded from the JSON schema (internal.py:166). When `call()` is invoked with a `context` dict, it's injected as a `types.SimpleNamespace` for tools that declare `_context`. Verification readiness outcome classification is tri-state. Generic status values `complete`/`completed` do not prove shell success. ## Lesson
- principle: A committed Rust crate change is not delivered behavior: the daemon and hooks shell out to ~/.gobby/bin binaries, so epic-level verification must prove the binaries were rebuilt, reinstalled, and probed for the new surface before close.
- root_cause: Leaf validation gates prove code-level correctness (cargo test in the worktree) and no gate compares installed-binary state or plan verification-section execution against the epic close.
- prevention: Before closing an epic whose plan has a verification section touching crates/, require evidence that ~/.gobby/bin binaries were reinstalled after the final Rust commit (mtime >= last crate commit, or a --help/--version probe of a new flag) and that each verification-section step has a receipt.

## Diagnostic
- title: Epic closed without executing plan V2 end-to-end verification; installed Rust binaries predate epic commits
- message: All 19 leaves of epic #18553 closed valid with scoped tests green, but ~/.gobby/bin/gwiki (built 2026-07-22 12:33 CDT) and gcode (2026-07-18) predate the first epic commit 8e78486ae (2026-07-22 15:46 CDT). Probes: installed `gwiki ask --help` lacks --deep; installed `gcode codewiki --help` lacks --compare-to. The plan's V2 End-to-End Verification (rebuild+reinstall, daemon restart, live wiki_ask checks, exports job, full-repo wiki regeneration) was never run; wiki/code pages remain stale with ghost pages for files renamed in 2.1.

When composing Tailwind classes in web/src/, ALWAYS use cn() from web/src/lib/utils.ts. Never use template-literal composition like `${BASE} ${cond ? ACTIVE : ""}`.

Why: web/tailwind.config.ts has `important: true`, which marks every utility !important. When two utilities target the same CSS property, neither !important wins source-order ties. Tailwind sorts arbitrary values alphabetically within a category, so `border-[var(--accent)]` sorts before `border-[var(--border)]` in the generated stylesheet, and the base `border-[var(--border)]` ALWAYS wins when both are in the className string — regardless of source order. The `!` prefix is redundant under global important.

cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge) resolves this by deduping same-property utilities at compose time, keeping only the last for each property.

How to apply:

- Drop redundant ! prefixes from class strings

Source IDs contain a volatile hash and stable location slug; deduplication, matching, and link resolution must use the location slug, not exact source_path or the full hash-prefixed ID. Existing source stubs should update in place when their stable identity matches, preserving Used by backlinks; different stable identities with title collisions receive suffixed paths. Manifest-backed source digests use source_hash as their separate provenance key.

In gobby-cli task #880, codewiki file-page verification now receives the same SymbolSummary table used by file_prompt. verify_prompt(blocks, symbols, sources) includes the Symbols table only when symbols are non-empty, so markdown/config/content-only files keep source-only verification with no fabricated empty symbol table; curated pages pass an explicit empty symbol slice. The verifier system prompt treats symbol evidence as authoritative for symbol names, kinds, components, line ranges, and purposes.

Activity Agents tab migration (#17026): the one-surface Agents panel lives under web/src/components/activity/AgentsTab.tsx and web/src/components/activity/agents/. It loads /api/agents/definitions, provider catalog, and pipeline workflows; row actions call /api/agents/definitions for enable/disable, duplicate, and delete; details use useDetailDraft plus shared agent editors for skills/rules/variables/steps/tool blocks. Backend route src/gobby/servers/routes/agents.py now accepts enabled and tags on create and tags on update for this surface.

gcode Elixir symbol extraction treats `def`, `defp`, and `defmacro` heads inside `defmodule` as `function` symbols, not `method` symbols. The Elixir symbol query captures paren-less identifiers, parameterized `(call target: identifier)` heads, and guarded parameterized heads under `when`; AST call extraction skips those declaration-head calls so definitions such as `def run(name)` do not materialize self-call edges.

PostgresHubDatabase hub pool configuration is injected from typed bootstrap `postgres_pool` settings (defaults min_size=2, max_size=20, acquire_timeout_seconds=5, open_timeout_seconds=30); legacy PGPOOL_* environment variables no longer affect it. PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT is also not a compatibility alias for hub pool acquisition. Transaction acquisition handles psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout by logging pool_stats from ConnectionPool.get_stats(), calling pool.check() once, then retrying acquisition once. Telemetry span PoolTimeouts are warning-level drops, and local span storage exporter registration is one-per-cached TracerProvider to avoid duplicate BatchSpanProcessors during repeated runner initialization.

Gobby task and agent isolation uses none, worktree, or clone. Dispatcher-spawned agents may set an explicit isolation value; unset or inherit falls back to task isolation. Planning agents run with isolation:none in the main project context. CLI and MCP build surfaces expose isolation while retaining validated compatibility for legacy clone/workspace-backend inputs.

## Lesson
- principle: A leaf commit inside a plan-scoped epic must not modify bundled templates outside the plan's target list; template edits ride the same purely-additive constraint as code.
- root_cause: Skill-contract commits touch many YAML surfaces at once; an unrelated cleanup rode along without plan attribution and leaf QA only checked the planned surfaces.
- prevention: Epic and leaf QA must diff the commit's touched file list against the plan section's named targets and treat any un-cited bundled-template change (especially deletions) as a blocking finding until justified.
