PipelineExecutor async execution paths route synchronous execution-manager operations and top-level child-session registration/setup through its injected run_db bridge; the fallback uses asyncio.to_thread. ApprovalManager approve_step and reject_step likewise route token consumption plus execution reads/status writes through its typed _run_db bridge. This contract is covered by focused workflow unit tests as of task #16872 / commit 1e8af01f4.

Managed web-chat plan presentation has two models. Text-plan CLIs (Codex and ACP providers, plus Droid prose turns) broadcast a tagged assistant plan after the stream completes through ManagedWebChatPermissionsMixin._maybe_broadcast_pending_plan; blocking inside that stream prevents the broadcast. Tool-plan CLIs (native Claude ExitPlanMode and Droid ExitSpecMode) park an explicit plan-exit tool on an approval event. Droid ExitSpecMode reaches Gobby only as droid.request_permission, is filtered from the session stream, and is handled by DroidPermissionResolver._resolve_plan_mode_request. Approval maps to proceed_once; user-requested changes map to cancel and preserve revise feedback. As of #18344 / commit 36d8907b1, expiry maps to the distinct "timeout" outcome, clears pending plan state, emits mode_changed(reason="plan_approval_timed_out"), interrupts the provider turn, then maps to cancel. Managed cancel_pending_approval releases _pending_plan_event so an external interrupt cannot strand the gate. Frontend plan actions live on the agent status bar, and plan_pending_approval options come from the provider registry.

Close-validation verdict concurrency uses the task row's updated_at as an optimistic verdict token: valid close/reset and invalid count/escalate both require an open, non-escalated row with the expected timestamp, so the first committed terminal transition wins and the loser raises TaskStaleStateError. Escalation side effects consume PostgreSQL's authoritative is_escalated/escalated_at row; the stable delivery identity is derived from task_id plus escalated_at, making a later re-escalation a fresh event.

Linear sync treats exhausted transient issue-list fetch failures as deferred, not errors: pull_linear_updates reports pull.errors=0 and pull.deferred for linked rows when retryable network, timeout, 429, or 5xx failures exhaust. sync_all does not advance synced_at and skips push whenever pull has errors or deferred work; cron raises only for real errors and reports deferred-only runs as deferred.

When applying older CodeRabbit suggestions in Gobby's shared 0.5.0 worktree, audit current HEAD and landed commits first, preserve newer behavior on overlapping paths, and avoid reintroducing UI or other regressions from stale review advice.

Drawbridge UI-annotation workflow for tier-consistent mobile work: open https://mbp.tail4125a0.ts.net/?tier-preview (TierPreview in web/src/components/dev/, switch in main.tsx). It renders the app in a centered same-origin iframe at tier sizes (portrait 440x956, landscape 932x430, desktop fill) so the Drawbridge in-page panel keeps the full window. Why this exists: viewport emulation via chrome-devtools MCP made Drawbridge unusable (panel renders inside the emulated page). Verified: Drawbridge screenshots use chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab so iframe pixels capture correctly; daemon serves the app with no anti-framing headers. Limitation: pointer:coarse/hover media queries resolve against the host device, so coarse-pointer styles do NOT apply inside the iframe (width queries and useIsMobile DO resolve per-iframe). The gobby chrome-devtools MCP server is configured with --ignoreDefaultChromeArg=--disable-extensions and --chromeArg=--load-extension=<Comet profile Drawbridge path> in ~/.gobby/mcp-servers.json so the automation browser loads Drawbridge.

For the Gobby daemon dev UI proxy, Vite HMR uses the /__vite_hmr WebSocket path and requires Sec-WebSocket-Protocol negotiation (for example vite-hmr) to be forwarded to Vite and echoed back to the browser. If the daemon accepts /__vite_hmr without the selected subprotocol, Chrome reports Vite HMR handshake failure even though normal UI assets and the Gobby /ws app WebSocket still work.

In Gobby build cleanup, dirty descendant worktree artifacts are classified and deferred by default. `build clean` deletes dirty descendant worktrees only when `delete_dirty_worktrees=True` is explicitly passed; if any artifact is deferred, branch cleanup is skipped to preserve the worktree/branch relationship. When explicit deletion is enabled, delete a closed dirty worktree only when its closed commit matches its HEAD and that HEAD is integrated; otherwise defer it to preserve local changes.

Files under `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/` are templates, not active enforcement. Installed DB rows are the active source; templates intentionally default to disabled. Check workflow-definition DB state when debugging enforcement. Rules, agents, variables, and pipelines all live beneath the shared `workflows/` template tree.

In gobby-cli, Python call extraction now resolves local `from ... import ...` bindings to canonical `CallTargetKind::Symbol` targets. `ImportResolutionContext` builds a Python local symbol index from top-level `def`/`async def`/`class` definitions, `parse_python_import_statement` records local bare aliases including relative imports like `from .service import Service`, and `materialize_call` promotes those bindings with `Symbol::make_id(project_id, file_path, name, kind, byte_start)`. Same-file constructor calls such as `Service()` resolve after `class` was added to callable kinds.

During gobby build dogfood #15385/#15446, internal gobby-agents spawn-style tools were fixed to inherit the caller session as parent_session_id when omitted. This prevents merge-orchestrator merge-worker spawns with isolation=none from falling back to the coordinator repository project context. The merge-orchestrator plan step also now allows gobby-agents list/inspect tools required by its prompt.

Task #18335's authoritative 2026-07-18 Ruff G201 inventory is 272 sites: 152 servers and 120 elsewhere. The migration is decomposed into bounded semantic-review leaves #18460–#18478; integration leaf #18479 depends on all 19 and alone enables G201 in pyproject.toml. Each leaf must inspect active exception context, preserve severity/control flow, and justify any retained logger.error(..., exc_info=True) with targeted noqa.

Gwiki URL ingest exposes one CLI freshness knob: `gwiki ingest-url --max-age-hours <HOURS>` defaults to 24 and `0` forces refetch. The value is required on both CliCommand::IngestUrl and Command::IngestUrl and is forwarded by cli/mapping.rs through commands::dispatch, commands::index::execute_ingest_url, and ingest::url::ingest_urls into ingest_urls_with_fetcher. Human/JSON ingest rendering now lives in crates/gwiki/src/commands/index/render.rs; cached URL results serialize requested_url, source_id, fetched_at, and age_hours and appear as `Cached: N`. Keep the Rust contract builder and crates/gwiki/contract/gwiki.contract.json synchronized when this flag changes.

In Gobby gwiki, the research loop persists code-grounding metadata through ResearchCodeCitation. Research observations carry code citations and degradations, accepted notes retain matching metadata, and model-off research degrades to a retrieval-only scaffold rather than rejecting --ai off.

Validation detection wrapper defaults are applied in the effective wrapper-rule path (`_iter_wrapper_rules`) rather than serialized into project overrides. `ValidationDetectionConfig.wrapper_rules` is additive; legacy `recognized_wrappers` are converted to prefix wrapper rules at classification time.

Rule enforcement depends on initialized session variables. Define defaults such as require_task_before_edit, require_commit_before_close, require_uv, enforce_tool_schema_check, max_stop_attempts, task_ref, and task_claimed through installed session-default rules so rule conditions have stable values. Template files are not active enforcement; installed workflow-definition DB rows are.

Session-end commit auto-linking must derive both scope values from the persisted session: pass session.project_id directly and resolve project_name from the Project row keyed by that ID. Allowing auto_link_commits to fall back to the daemon's current project context can mis-scope or silently skip [project-#N] commit references. Implemented for task #16867 in commit 3ba15f3da.

ExpansionService.compile_plan_to_spec is manifest-driven: it preserves manifest task fields, emits section_id::single for tdd:false, wires dependencies by blocker TDD mode, and keeps deferred sections separate. Deliverable-only contract plans do not fall back to LLM expansion; when an authored M1 manifest is missing, _parse_contract_plan deterministically synthesizes one with emit_stub_manifest before compiling.

gobby-cli build/test flag convention: `--no-default-features` only needs to work for CI testing. For local issue diagnosis and installing binaries, use the normal default-feature build unless the user explicitly asks for CI/no-default parity.

Holistic descendant gate audit markers use their Markdown heading (`Holistic QA deferred`) as the stable idempotency identity. The blocker body intentionally retains mutable stage/state diagnostics, while `has_audit_marker` in `src/gobby/dispatch/audit.py` prevents `holistic_descendant_gate_rule` from appending another marker as descendant states advance. Regression coverage in `tests/dispatch/test_rules.py::test_holistic_descendant_gate_rule_appends_marker_once` exercises ready, in_progress, needs_review, and review_approved blocker states. Implemented by #15895 in commit cd61941fe.

In gwiki audit, generated code-projection pages are page-level exempt from unsupported-claim auditing when their path is `code/`, frontmatter has `trust: generated`, and `generated_by: gcode-codewiki`; their projection identity is the grounding. Curated knowledge pages remain per-claim audited. Daemon-generated concept pages (`source_kind: concept`, `synthesis_mode: daemon`) may credit all prose in a section when that section carries inline source attribution. Source-material sections such as citations, sources, backlinks, extracts, source excerpts, used by, missing evidence, and conflicting claims are ignored.

Memory recall is daemon-owned under DaemonConfig.memory_recall / MemoryRecallConfig, and the removed memory_recall_helper config key must fail loudly at startup. Session activation seeds parent_turn_seq. BEFORE_AGENT recall is scheduled asynchronously per session and parent turn, writes a daemon_memory_recall self-addressed message, and delivery accepts it only when origin_turn_seq freshness matches the immediately preceding turn.

Task #14211 changed TTS-only text normalization so standalone ok/OK/O.K. tokens become 'okay' before synthesis, avoiding Chatterbox pronouncing short confirmations like 'TTS check ok' as 'o'. Non-standalone words such as 'book' are unaffected.

Skill updater persistence uses LocalSkillManager.update_skill_with_files to replace updater-managed metadata and synchronize optional skill files in one hub DB transaction. SkillFilesMixin._set_skill_files accepts an existing Transaction so callers can compose file synchronization atomically; notifications fire only after commit.

Settled shared-daemon vs standalone identity/key boundary: standalone Gobby users do not use user accounts, user identity, or API keys. Standalone/direct mode retains the existing install-scoped secret DEK wrapped by local key-file or scrypt-passphrase KEK. Shared-daemon mode adds users and shared user API keys; API key authenticates to user_id, and user_id selects user-scoped secret key material. Do not derive encryption keys from API keys. Use a stable random user DEK wrapped by the daemon installation/root KEK so API-key rotation has no encryption effect. Every daemon API request also supplies machine_id; valid user credentials auto-enroll unknown machines and enforce machines.owner_user_id. Binaries use daemon identity only in daemon mode; auto fallback to configured direct mode crosses into standalone install trust and must never occur for 401/403.

Gobby activity-panel list rows use the shared `.activity-list-row` / `.activity-list-row__body` primitive and `--activity-panel-row-height` token (2.25rem). Top-list rows are single-line: status, truncating title, trailing metadata/chips, and a kebab action. Keep desktop kebab controls compact and promote to 44px only for coarse pointers. Selected rows use `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 8%, transparent)` with no inset side stripe; put secondary descriptions in the detail pane. Traces is no longer an Activity Panel tab entry.

Task #17268 decomposed src/gobby/servers/app_factory.py into focused modules: startup/shutdown lifespan wiring lives in src/gobby/servers/_app_lifecycle.py, route registration in src/gobby/servers/_app_routes.py, and WebSocket/UI proxy mounting in src/gobby/servers/_app_ui.py. app_factory.py remains the public compatibility facade and resolves HookManager/CodexAdapter through runtime getters so tests and callers patching gobby.servers.app_factory.HookManager still affect lifespan startup.

Workflow observer MCP results are intentionally stored as bounded summaries: at most 64 tool entries, 16 top-level scalar fields per result, 128-character names, and 256-character strings. Nested payloads are excluded while null/presence and safe-evaluator fields remain available. Implemented by task #18318 in commit 247629a30554b5adaa41b9d48cf614a903de43ad.

Variable architecture has 2 active scopes: (1) WorkflowInstance.variables (per-workflow per-session, in workflow_instances table), (2) SessionVariableManager (shared across all workflows, in session_variables table, primary/preferred). WorkflowState.variables is legacy and no longer used as a fallback (removed in v0.2.22). Rules use SessionVariableManager exclusively via set_variable effects. Pipelines have their own separate input/output data flow and don't use workflow state variables at all.

Telegram inbound destination contract: TelegramAdapter.parse_webhook includes metadata_json["conversation_reference"] = {"conversation_id": str(chat_id)} for both private and group chats. InboundCommunications persists that reference on the resolved CommsIdentity, and OutboundCommunications.enrich_metadata uses it to set platform_destination when replying with only session_id. Covered by task #17889, commit 2be2a56f1.

Task #17412 established that represented transcript unknowns should not write `Unknown block type` entries to parser-error logs. Codex, Claude, Droid parser represented-unknown branches and the renderer unknown fallback now preserve unknown blocks for UI/API inspection while leaving parser-error logs for malformed/non-object diagnostics. Regression coverage includes a real `/api/sessions/{id}/messages` Codex JSONL path asserting an `unknown` content block and no parser-error spam, plus updated Claude/Qwen/Droid fail-soft expectations.

In gobby-cli task #674, codewiki frontmatter range serialization was changed to coalesce contiguous or overlapping line ranges before YAML emission. Repository overview pages use `frontmatter_with_degradation_without_ranges`, preserving complete source file provenance for hashing/reuse while omitting per-file `ranges` blocks so `code/repo.md` stays compact; body references still use the full source spans.

Review bots (CodeRabbit etc.) flag model names newer than their training cutoff as 'nonexistent' or 'invalid'. NEVER fix such review findings by deleting the models. Precedent: commit 71319547f ('address CodeRabbit review findings') deleted claude opus/fable from CLAUDE_ALIASES and the static catalog, deleted gpt-5.5 from the codex static catalog, and added a web-chat blocklist for gpt-5.5 — breaking the chat UI model dropdowns for weeks (fixed in task #17775, commit 165ef6a11). When triaging any review-bot finding about an unknown/nonexistent/suspicious model ID, verify against live discovery first — probe_claude_model in src/gobby/servers/provider_model_discovery.py (CLAUDE_ALIASES is probed against the real claude CLI), codex app-server list_models, ACP session models for qwen/grok — and reject the finding if the model is real. Regression guards live in tests/servers/test_provider_models.py (test_claude_aliases_cover_all_current_model_families) and tests/servers/routes/test_providers.py (test_filters_hidden_codex_models_from_web_chat_surface).

For the #12285 Droid CLI adapter, the canonical hook contract is the plan's exact 9 PascalCase events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, SessionStart, SessionEnd. Droid Stop maps to HookEventType.STOP, not AFTER_AGENT. EVENT_TYPE_CLI_SUPPORT is informational and Claude currently duplicates Stop there; do not use that table to infer Droid's adapter mapping.

In web useTaskInlineEdit, WebSocket reconciliation makes server state authoritative by bumping in-flight field generations: stale PATCH responses must not apply data or roll back the reconciled task. PATCH rejection messages remain user-visible even when the generation is stale, so failed edits cannot disappear silently. Covered by task #16509 / commit 6d9ea662d.

Gobby task readiness should treat open metadata-only tasks with no task_stage_states as ready/actionable, while tasks with all manifest stages completed are non-actionable. Claimed tasks count as active work for ancestry proximity and conflict avoidance, and next-task suggestions should not return tasks already claimed/in progress.

In the Gobby Rust workspace, PostgreSQL test DB resolution is centralized in `gobby_core::bootstrap`: `postgres_database_url_from_bootstrap_file` reads `bootstrap.yaml`, returns a trimmed `database_url` only for `hub_backend: postgres`, treats missing/non-Postgres configuration as no URL, and errors on malformed YAML. `gobby-code` test helpers resolve DB sources in this order: `GCODE_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, `GOBBY_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `GOBBY_POSTGRES_TEST_*` components, then `GOBBY_HOME/bootstrap.yaml`.

Web-chat usage persistence must distinguish missing usage from reported zero values; never use `0 or None` for token fields. Persist model/context-window metadata safely without overwriting valid values with NULL. Context occupancy is canonicalized separately through normalized snapshot fields such as context_used_tokens and context_usage_ratio; cumulative usage counters are historical accounting only.

Gobby chat attachment limits default to 100,000,000 bytes per file, 20 files per message, and 2,000,000,000 total bytes per message. `ChatConfig` now rejects configured totals above `attachment_max_file_bytes * attachment_max_files_per_message`; runtime limit resolution still caps the effective total defensively. Limits are configurable via DB `config_store` and apply to stored chat attachment upload validation and WebSocket binding.

Gobby mirrors ghook diagnose schemas under schemas/. Active sandbox diagnose validation now targets schemas/diagnose-output.v2.schema.json from gobby-cli commit 4f4be047a46abf722b4fc9e61a6251031e819d52; schemas/diagnose-output.v1.schema.json remains frozen historical compatibility data.

In gobby-cli gcode semantic code-symbol search, initializing the CLI logger alone is not enough to surface Qdrant outages: `gobby_core::qdrant::with_qdrant` converts unreachable Qdrant into `(default, ServiceState::Unreachable)` instead of an error, so `semantic_search`'s `Err`-path `log::warn!` does not run. Log degraded `ServiceState` in `crates/gcode/src/vector/code_symbols/qdrant.rs::vector_search` while preserving the empty-result fallback. `crates/gcode/src/dispatch.rs` now initializes a quiet-aware stderr logger after CLI parse, defaulting non-quiet runs to warn and honoring plain `RUST_LOG` levels.

Task #19090 / commit d09f741d3 makes verbose-once workflow block rendering preserve recovery instructions. `recovery_directive_suffix` in `workflows.engine.blocked_tool_recovery` extracts every actionable sentence, balances multiline direct/MCP call expressions through their closing parenthesis, preserves backticked and alternative commands, normalizes the result to one line, and returns an empty suffix for reasons with no directive. `EvaluationMixin._finalize_block_response` appends that suffix only when an identical block reason collapses to the per-turn terse stub. Acceptance inventory is derived from enabled bundled rule YAML in `tests/workflows/test_block_rendering.py`, so new actionable reason forms must remain extractable.

Gobby web-chat provider normalization: Codex web-chat live events can arrive as response_item/event_msg plus transcript token_count records. Normalize those through shared ToolCallEvent/ToolResultEvent/DoneEvent paths, including cache-read/cache-creation tokens, so UI tool cards and context usage match other providers. Main chat and Activity Panel transcript scrollers should use behavior:auto, overflow-anchor:none, and overscroll-behavior:contain to avoid streaming bounce.

Task stage ownership rule: manual `move_to_stage` operations now honor active task claims. A task claimed by a different session must reject stage moves unless the caller passes `force=True`; the HTTP stage route threads this request flag through to the task manager.

PipelineStep in src/gobby/workflows/definitions.py inherits Pydantic's default extra-field ignore behavior. Removing an execution-type field alone will not reject that key when another valid execution type is present; removed pipeline step keys that must fail definition loading need an explicit mode="before" validator (or a deliberate extra="forbid" policy).

Web chat model selection is catalog-aware. Provider groups and models are surfaced from supported CLI/provider contracts and eligible live-discovered endpoint catalogs; endpoint-backed selections preserve their `endpoint:<name>[/<model>]` identity while routing through the appropriate execution provider. Generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints that do not meet web-chat requirements remain unavailable rather than appearing as selectable models.

Gwiki catalog-owned `_context.md` files carry frontmatter `generated_by: gwiki-catalog`. Concept-quality or lifecycle passes must use that stamp to distinguish generated folder navigation surfaces from a synthesized junk concept page at the same reserved path. For dry-run parity when governance can mutate lifecycle first, discover deterministic concept-quality decisions before governance and apply their transitions afterward.

Gobby web_chat live ChatSession instances are now shared through WebChatSessionRegistry (`src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/session_registry.py`). `runner_init.init_servers` creates one registry, passes it through `ServiceContainer` to `setup_internal_registries`/`compact_self`, and passes the same instance to `WebSocketServer`, whose `_chat_sessions` and `_active_chat_tasks` are the registry backing dicts.

Recall fit contract (task #18425): pairwise evaluation is normalized per mixed request. Full-candidate cohorts assign each of P×N pairs weight 1/(P×N); injected cohorts assign IPS(pos)/(N×sum positive IPS), preserving within-request position correction while each request totals exactly 1. PairwiseEvalResult reports raw pair_count separately from mixed_request_count, and partial pooling shrinks in mixed-request units via mixed/(mixed+shrinkage_requests). Request partitions are SHA-256 ordered from a version plus request ID; split, evaluator, and audit-sampler versions form the evaluation cohort identity. Shrinkage candidates (2,5,10,20,50) are selected from planted synthetic requests plus validation nested inside the outer training partition, so selection has no holdout input.

Observations are stored in the `_observations` session variable, not WorkflowState fields. The `observe` rule effect appends structured observation entries during rule evaluation, and context injection reads them through SessionVariableManager. WorkflowState `observations` and `reflection_pending` were removed in migration v121.

Frontend coarse-pointer touch targets use Tailwind's pointer-coarse:min-h-11/min-w-11 convention. The shared ui/Switch preserves its 44x24 visual track by nesting that track inside a button whose coarse-pointer height expands to 44px, keeping fine-pointer rendering unchanged.

In Gobby, gobby-core exposes shared graph analytics behind the graph-analytics Cargo feature. crates/gcore/src/graph_analytics.rs remains transport/datastore-free and uses neutral in-memory AnalyticsGraph inputs so gwiki and gcode can adapt their graph data without coupling to FalkorDB, Qdrant, or PostgreSQL.

Memory async-path design (#16185): synchronous LocalMemoryManager operations in async recall/lifecycle paths are dispatched through the injected daemon run_db executor, with asyncio.to_thread fallback. Digest session reads/title updates/atomic persistence and PromptLoader DB rendering use asyncio.to_thread. Event-loop regressions deliberately block storage calls and assert loop progress.

ChatSession communications transport contract (task #17895, commit a7a325c2e): gobby.servers.chat_stream_transport.ChatStreamTransport is the structural frame transport shared by ChatStreamingMixin. WebSocketChatStreamTransport remains the web/voice concrete transport, while ChatStreamingMixin._run_chat_turn owns shared session creation, persistence, event handling, model switching, and cleanup. ChatSessionCommsBackend keys turns by CommsMessage.session_id, passes responder provider/model config, and installs on CommunicationsResponder during server initialization. CommunicationsChatStreamTransport accumulates TextChunk frames; edit-capable adapters get an immediate first send, edits throttled to 1.5 seconds, and an unconditional final flush, while other adapters receive one final send. BaseChannelAdapter edit_message plus supports_message_edit and CommunicationsManager.edit_message form the generic adapter seam.

As of commit 0738ba927 (task #19223), the stdio MCP proxy has no ambient session cache, bootstrap query, retry throttle, or resolver dependency. It captures allowlisted terminal context once at initialization and sends X-Gobby-Terminal-Context on every ambient request; explicit per-call and GOBBY_SESSION_ID pins send X-Gobby-Session-Id instead. Explicit calls do not affect later ambient identity. session_bootstrap.py was deleted; terminal capture/compact serialization live in terminal_context.py and read_project_id lives in stdio_proxy.py. Daemon 409 SESSION_REQUIRED detail is returned as the typed proxy result.

Web destructive actions should require explicit confirmation. For web-chat session deletion, use the confirmed optimistic-removal flow: mark deleting, send the request, remove only after acknowledgement, and restore on timeout; keep this logic in the focused useChat/useSessions modules.

Inter-session messages use delivered_at as their lifecycle signal. The unused read_at/mark_read/unread_only surface was removed in task #16817, including the MCP filter and PostgreSQL baseline column/index.

Gobby task/session concurrency model: PostgreSQL is the authoritative shared store, and ordinary manager updates build SQL SET clauses only for supplied columns, so concurrent writes to different SQL columns preserve each other under PostgreSQL row serialization. Same-column conflicts use targeted policy—conditional UPDATE/rowcount checks or advisory locks for lifecycle invariants, atomic JSONB operators for task labels/commits and session terminal_context registration/backfill. There is no generalized per-field timestamp/CRDT layer. Task JSONL restore is an explicit recovery operation and intentionally applies whole-record LWW only when backup updated_at wins; sessions have no JSONL backup/restore sync.

NEVER delete gobby tasks without first checking the dependency tree via `get_dependency_tree` or the `blocking`/`blocked_by` fields on `get_task`.

`delete_task(cascade=true)` (the default) deletes the task AND all *dependent tasks* — anything with `blocked_by` pointing at the target, and their dependents, transitively. Not just subtasks. In Gobby #3207 I deleted #12145 (a subtask of #12044) with cascade=true and it took out #12044, #12077 (the planning epic), #12081, and #12129 via the `blocked_by` chain. Seq numbers were freed and reused when the next expansion ran, making the damage hard to spot.

**Always before a delete:**
1. Call `get_task(task_id, brief=false)` and inspect `dependencies.blocking` — that lists every task that will cascade-delete if cascade=true.
2. If the list is non-empty and you don't intend to delete those, use `cascade=false` (fails if there are dependents) or `unlink=true` (removes links, keeps dependents).
3. If you genuinely want the cascade, state the full deletion set explicitly to the user before running.

Why: cascade delete is destructive and not reversible in Gobby — tasks are hard-deleted, not soft-deleted (no `deleted_at` column in the schema). The user explicitly told me to save this rule after I caused the incident.

Hub and admin aggregate queries should use `tasks.state_bucket` rather than recomputing task state with a CASE join to `task_stage_states`.

In gobby-cli, code graph read behavior is split with `crates/gcode/src/graph/code_graph/read.rs` as a thin facade. Child modules live under `crates/gcode/src/graph/code_graph/read/`: `support.rs` contains shared Cypher fragments, graph result row mapping, clamping, count extraction, and blast-row dedupe; `relationship_queries.rs` contains caller/usage/import/blast Cypher query builders; `payload_queries.rs` contains graph payload Cypher query builders for project/file/symbol/blast views; `graph_payloads.rs` builds `GraphPayload` values for project overview, file graph, symbol neighbors, and blast radius; `relationships.rs` exposes count/find/import/blast read APIs returning `GraphResult` lists or IDs. The parent `code_graph.rs` still re-exports the public read API and imports three test-only query helpers through the facade.

For failed-run recovery, verify the process/tmux session is dead, acquire the run-linked task dispatch mutex with recovery ownership, reread task ownership and stage under that lease, then atomically fail the stage and release the task claim. Pass `preheld_mutex_run_id` so recovery retains the same lease across both writes.

In Gobby workflow_definitions, source values 'installed' and 'template' are Gobby-owned definitions. Source values like 'custom' and 'project' represent user/project-authored definitions, so template refresh or reinstall flows should preserve them unless explicitly operating on user-owned content.

Memory search remains semantic-first. similarity is the numeric semantic confidence after source boost and temporal decay; keyword-only hits have similarity=null. ranking_score/RRF may expand recall but must not displace higher-similarity results. Apply min_score only to numeric-similarity hits. MemoryRecallConfig.min_score defaults to 0.0; the LLM selector is the quality gate.

For Gobby plan coverage, PostgreSQL is authoritative: `gobby plan coverage --task-tree db` must read live task data through LocalTaskManager, not `.gobby/tasks.jsonl`. JSONL is export/backup material and should be read only by an explicit JSONL mode. CI coverage checks must not use task JSONL as their live task source.

In gobby-cli, gwiki local file ingest is split so crates/gwiki/src/ingest/file.rs stays the facade for StdinSnapshot, LocalFileIngestResult, ingest_path, ingest_path_without_index re-export, ingest_stdin, and the TEXT_INLINE_LIMIT_BYTES policy. Local kind dispatch lives in crates/gwiki/src/ingest/file/dispatch.rs; generic borrowed-file ingest in generic.rs; raw markdown rendering in render.rs; replay metadata updates in replay.rs; source-kind classification, source locations, asset threshold checks, and source-file reads in source.rs; degradation summary formatting in degradation.rs; behavior tests in tests.rs. Keep future file-ingest behavior tests in ingest/file/tests.rs and keep helper visibility pub(super) only where sibling modules or tests need it.

The web/ directory now has two TypeScript projects: (1) the Vite web UI (tsconfig.json, includes src/ but excludes src/setup/) and (2) the Ink setup wizard (tsconfig.setup.json, includes only src/setup/ with Node types instead of DOM). The main tsconfig.json has `"exclude": ["src/setup"]` to prevent DOM type conflicts. Build commands: `npm run build` for web UI, `npm run build:setup` for setup wizard. Dev: `npm run setup` runs the wizard via tsx.

Tmux prompt automation is centralized in src/gobby/agents/terminal_prompt_monitor.py. Trust dismissal must send Enter only (`\n`), never option 2, because option 2 trusts the parent folder and is unsafe with sibling clones. Lifecycle monitoring handles trust prompts before loop and approval prompts.

tmux set-titles-string gotcha: When enabling `set-titles on` globally, tmux uses the default `set-titles-string` which is `#S:#I:#W - "#T" #{session_alerts}`. This prepends session name and window index to the title (e.g. `8:1:My Title`). Must explicitly set `set-titles-string "#W"` to get just the window name. The _rename_tmux_window function in summary_actions.py had this bug for user sessions (agent_depth 0) while TmuxSessionManager.rename_window already had the correct behavior for spawned agents.

Codex should use the same dedicated scratch-planning apparatus as Claude for large Gobby review/fix batches: write concise, decision-complete scratch plans under .gobby/plans/ after the required task is claimed. Plans must be execution artifacts only: no open questions, options, or stream-of-consciousness reasoning.

Memory lookup behavior is layer-specific: LocalMemoryManager.get_memory raises ValueError for missing or hidden active-visibility rows, while MemoryManagerFacade.get_memory returns `Memory | None`. Callers and tests must use the contract of the layer they invoke and gracefully handle stale index references where appropriate.

FilesTab renders root-level file tree entries from rootEntries, while nested directories render from childrenMap. Its loadChildren callback treats the empty path as the root and updates rootEntries, allowing delete, rename, move, and duplicate handlers to share the same post-mutation refresh path.

The gobby-sessions `send_keys` and `capture_output` MCP tools target sessions by `session_id`. Resolve agent sessions through LocalAgentRunManager and interactive sessions through terminal context. `send_keys` authorizes only the caller's session, same-project sessions, or ancestor/descendant sessions; use `literal=true` for text and `literal=false` for tmux key names.

For structured stage-native plan-review rejection, use StageReviewRejectionMutation at advisory-lock priority 290 outside the dispatch mutex (300) and plan-review evidence mutation (475). This makes stage transition, description projection, round_result, and evidence finalization atomic without lock inversion. Round uniqueness indexes exclude expired plan_review_evidence rows, preserving failed-spawn audit rows while allowing same-round re-preparation.

Voice dependencies faster-whisper>=1.0.0 and chatterbox-tts are base project dependencies; the `voice` extra is an empty compatibility alias. Dependency overrides retain gradio>=6.14.0 to resolve chatterbox-tts==0.1.7's gradio pin alongside the Starlette >=1.0.1 floor. Voice health checks report missing packages with `uv sync` guidance rather than auto-installing them.

In gwiki session ingest, deterministic session frontmatter metadata is carried through ParsedSessionMetadata plus ParsedSessionMessage.tool_names. render_session_markdown emits model, tool_counts, token_totals, duration_seconds, hour_buckets, is_subagent, and gitBranch via MetadataValue bool/json support. Claude Code token usage is de-duplicated by message.id before summing; Codex token_totals uses the latest cumulative event_msg.payload.info.total_token_usage, with model from turn_context.model and branch from session_meta.git.branch.

gcore `StandaloneConfig::from_yaml_str` derives default `ai.text_generate.*` LM Studio direct routing settings for non-empty standalone `gcore.yaml` files when no explicit text-generation routing/base/model keys are present, and copies `ai.embeddings.api_key` into the derived text-generation API key. Explicit `ai.text_generate.*` YAML values are preserved.

Codex app-server commandExecution item/completed outcomes are normalized in src/gobby/adapters/codex_impl/item_normalization.py before shared tool normalization: aggregatedOutput, exitCode, and status become a structured tool_response/tool_output contract consumed by direct AFTER_TOOL observers and web-chat post-tool lifecycle handling. Live Codex CLI 0.144.5 evidence captured on 2026-07-17 proved exitCode=0/status=completed for success and exitCode=7/status=failed for nonzero execution; the sanitized fixture is tests/fixtures/provider_contracts/codex/command-execution-items.json. ACPHookAdapter.normalize_tool_name must consult the concrete provider's TOOL_MAP before normalize_acp_tool_name so provider-only aliases such as Grok run_terminal_command remain canonical Bash after shared ACP extraction. Validation detection treats jq as evidence only for explicit jq empty, jq -e, or jq --exit-status prefixes; plain jq selectors remain read-only and produce no readiness evidence.

Task #16065 established workflow rule/variable template sync ownership semantics: orphan cleanup runs only after a nonempty, error-free authoritative scan; a single non-gobby root is partial and cannot prune; project and global user roots are passed together as one authoritative namespace. Sync-managed installed rows are restored when their template reappears. Implemented in commit a3f9246e3.

Gobby rule authoring should prefer semantic workflow events `turn_start` and `turn_end`; raw `before_agent`, `after_agent`, and `stop` are provider/runtime escape hatches. Installed rule definitions use `RuleDefinitionBody` with an `effects` list, and agent termination is handled separately via `end_agent_run`.

Gobby web UI theming discipline (user feedback, learned the hard way in #14718): light-mode design changes MUST be scoped to [data-theme="light"] in CSS, or branched via the existing useResolvedTheme() hook for Tailwind/TSX (e.g. SegmentedControl). NEVER alter shared selectors or shared tokens globally for a light-only fix — it regresses dark. Dark mode is a FROZEN shipped baseline; the user's reference is .gobby/screenshots/IMG_3754.PNG (accent/chartreuse text+tints on near-black; transparent .app-header over var(--bg-primary)). Concretely: body backdrop is theme-split — default/dark body = var(--bg-primary) (near-black, matches IMG_3754), [data-theme="light"] body = var(--bg-secondary) (intentional light recessed-depth). .impeccable.md 'one system, two postures' means different problems per theme: accent washes look muddy on light's near-white paper but are the correct signature on dark's near-black — do not neutralize dark to fix light. font-semibold on selected segmented options + .chat-scope-btn.active is a confirmed universal good-fit kept in both themes. Verify dark is byte-unchanged (diff screenshot vs IMG_3754) whenever touching shared chrome.

Shipped light selected-state system (#14722, commit 68dca99bf; rebuilds the globally-applied c16fecad1 that was reverted in 3b39e531e): light-only token --surface-selected: oklch(98.5% 0.005 125) — a brighter neutral well lifted ABOVE the --bg-secondary track and --bg-primary canvas; selection reads via lightness + font-semibold, NOT hue. It is undefined in dark (only referenced by light-scoped rules) so dark never resolves it. Light treatments: selected (SegmentedControl active via useResolvedTheme branch, .command-palette-item.active, .chat-scope-btn.active which also DROPS the inset accent stripe in light, .session-item.attached) = --surface-selected + --text-primary; applied filter/constraint (.activity-filter-button[aria-expanded], .activity-filter-dropdown__item--active) = solid --accent + --accent-foreground (the one decisive accent moment, 5.51:1); session-kind .chip--* = neutral mono pills (--bg-tertiary/--text-secondary), accent NOT spent on identity metadata. Verify light WCAG 2.2 AA via chrome-devtools canvas-2D sRGB readback (Chrome returns computed colors as oklch() strings, so JS regex parsing is invalid — rasterize via canvas fillStyle+getImageData).

Initialize task lifecycle session variables defensively (`task_ref` to `""` and `task_claimed` to `false`) so rule conditions and templates have stable values. Use `task_ref` (`#<seq_num>`) for human-facing task display rather than truncated UUIDs.

Gobby's PostgreSQL hub, FalkorDB graph, Qdrant vectors, and embedding API are required infrastructure for full product behavior. Commands must still report clear degradation or return bounded contract-defined results when dependent services are unavailable; describe this as degraded required infrastructure, not optional enhancements.

gwiki librarian near-duplicate detection treats the current `lint::collect_pages()` snapshot as authoritative. `near_duplicate_pairs` builds `pages_by_path` before semantic queries and ignores any semantic hit absent from that map, preventing removed pages retained in a stale semantic index from becoming candidate pairs. Live pairs still pass through existing structural, redirect, session/source, citation, and reviewed-distinct exclusions. Implemented by task #18864 in commit f030a26ca.

Task #17257 decomposed gobby-clones MCP tools: public factory stays in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/clones.py, with implementation registries in _clones_creation.py, _clones_read.py, _clones_operations.py, _clones_cleanup.py, and shared dependencies in _clones_context.py.

Telegram operator documentation authority (task #18895, commit fef59fed8): docs/guides/telegram.md is the canonical operator guide for BotFather setup, secure channel updates, DM/group authorization, Telegram privacy modes, responder/project/model behavior, shipped capabilities, limits, and troubleshooting. docs/guides/comm-integrations.md remains the cross-channel architecture and API overview; docs/reviews/channel-parity-matrix.md records Telegram parity completion and defers only the Mini App dashboard under #18498. Documentation prose and parity research are reviewed against source rather than enforced by committed pytest contracts.

To check if a gobby task has already been implemented: 1) search git log for commits referencing the task ID (git log --grep), 2) search codebase for the specific fix mentioned in the task, 3) run relevant tests to confirm they pass. Tasks often get fixed as side effects of other work without being closed.

When loading bundled prompt .md files at runtime (not via PromptLoader/DB), you must strip YAML frontmatter manually. Pattern: split on '---' with maxsplit=2, take parts[2].strip(). The sync system (sync.py) handles this via parse_frontmatter(), but direct file reads (like instructions.py) need manual stripping. See build_gobby_instructions() for the pattern.

Gobby integrations docs audit finding: `gobby github import/sync/pr` CLI paths use the configured `github` MCP server via `GitHubSyncService`, while the `gobby-tasks-ops:import_github_issues` MCP tool shells out to the local `gh` CLI. Document these prerequisites separately to avoid drift.

CommunicationsManager channel lifecycle now keeps adapter initialization failures in runtime state via _channel_init_errors and exposes real active/init_error status through channel_to_dict(); HTTP communications routes and the communications MCP add_channel tool should use channel_to_dict for channel payloads instead of plain dataclass asdict when runtime status matters.

Workflow hook project-path warning policy: keep warnings when project_id is missing or unknown because that catches lost project context; only demote no project_path resolution to debug for known no-repo system projects such as _personal/_global via _is_known_no_repo_project. Dirty-file helpers should treat None project_path as no-repo and return empty DirtyFiles without shelling out.

Agent definition source of truth for current Gobby: `AgentDefinitionBody` lives in `src/gobby/workflows/definitions.py`; bundled agent YAML lives under `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/` with deprecated templates in its `deprecated/` subdirectory. Agent definitions do not have a `max_turns` field; stale YAML/API payload keys are ignored or scrubbed on normalized write/output paths, and `timeout` is the only definition-level runtime limit. Normal spawned-agent self-completion is via `gobby-agents:end_agent_run`; `kill_agent`/`stop_agent` are operator or parent cancellation/process cleanup controls.

For the PostgreSQL 18 upgrade immediately after the SQLite-to-PostgreSQL hub migration, Gobby has not launched publicly, so do not build a PG17 backward-compatibility or dual-runtime path. The accepted approach is backup-first, then destructive Docker volume recreate/restore for internal installs.

gwiki uses gcore AI source helpers: operational paths use ai_source_for_conn or ai_source_without_primary, and hub_ai_config_source uses lazy ai_source_with_primary so daemon mode does not open a PostgreSQL connection. In daemon mode, database URL layering is environment > daemon-served DSN > bootstrap and excludes gcore.yaml; standalone mode uses environment > bootstrap > gcore.yaml. Effective-config transport and non-2xx failures propagate as hard errors.

HTTP telemetry middleware derives http.target from the routed request scope after call_next (and in the exception path), uses the fixed value "unmatched" when no route exists, and excludes request-derived session_id/project_id labels to keep Prometheus metric cardinality bounded.

One-surface UI (epic #14767) design directives from the user: (1) Standalone TasksPage is deleted, and its LifecycleBoard is obsolete. Real Codex fixtures can be supplied via `GWIKI_CODEX_ARCHIVE_FIXTURE`.

Codex app-server `token_count.info.last_token_usage.output_tokens` already includes reasoning tokens. Gobby's Codex transcript and web-chat usage normalization must use `output_tokens` directly and must not add `reasoning_output_tokens`, which would double-count usage. This contract was established by task #16090.

In gobby-cli task #931, ghook recognizes `--cli=agy` for Google Antigravity CLI with canonical source `agy`. Antigravity CLI's documented command hook events are PascalCase: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `Stop`. In ghook's registry only `SessionStart` and `Stop` are fail-closed critical hooks; prompt/tool hooks are non-critical but still dispatch and spool normally. Regression coverage includes `cli_config::agy_uses_antigravity_hook_contract`, `diagnose::agy_uses_antigravity_pascal_case_hooks`, and contract forwarding for all five event names.

HTTPServer consumes runner-owned text-generation and LLM service references through ServiceContainer. Runner initialization is the single construction point; HTTPServer must preserve missing/degraded references instead of recreating them, so daemon consumers and HTTP routes share identical service state.

Session event-loop offload design (#16236): async HTTP session routes should use server.run_db for synchronous SessionManager/database calls and asyncio.to_thread for filesystem/archive work. SessionLivenessMonitor has no HTTP server dependency, so its synchronous DB query, tmux subprocess batching, session touch, and status update run through asyncio.to_thread. Regression tests verify the exact liveness offload calls and that transcript restore/stat execute on worker threads.

Consecutive-tool-block recovery identifies MCP tools by server:tool rather than treating every wrapper call as one tool. Counters are reset on workflow step transitions so failures from one step do not bleed into later steps. Rule-engine block behavior is now organized across core, event utilities, and evaluation layers.

TranscriptReader.get_rendered_messages() intentionally bypasses the database to avoid corrupted str() data, reading directly from JSONL or gzip archives instead. A robust gzip decompression implementation in transcript_reader.py now gracefully handles truncated or malformed archives by returning partial lines and logging warnings.

Gobby task #17168 made daemon vector sync treat gcode indexed-file misses as expected stale per-file work: `sync_worker` catches `GcodeIndexedFileNotFoundError` from `vector_sync_file`, reloads the indexed row, logs INFO with no warning/error if the row disappeared, purges the project if the root disappeared, silently leaves pending if the source file disappeared, and logs one WARNING without traceback when the row and source still exist. It leaves `vectors_synced=false` and does not clear vector projection cleanup state for these stale misses; real vector failures still log ERROR with traceback.

Task #17405 removed dead Gemini-as-a-Gobby-provider runtime/test coverage while intentionally retaining Gemini model-family metadata for AGY/Droid/Qwen paths. Remaining src gemini references in provider_model_defaults, model_registry google/ mapping, provider_models model-family handling, context window lookup, AGY .gemini installer/config paths, Qwen auth type, typed transcript legacy value, and migration 295 are expected keep-list items rather than live Gemini provider support.

Merge campaign reporting persists outcomes through record_merge_result. Leaf-task close evidence is derived by the checklist gate from session transcripts; verify_in_worktree is execution-time verification only and must not mint close evidence. close_task is reserved for the explicit already_implemented no-op path.

AgentCleanupHandler.post_terminal_cleanup treats remove_agent_completion_subscribers as best-effort: failures are logged with exc_info and later worktree, session, runtime, and artifact cleanup must continue. codewiki module-link integrity invariant (crates/gcode/src/commands/codewiki): a file page renders `Module: [[code/modules/<file.module>]]`, where `file.module` comes from `cluster_file_modules` -> `cluster_module_name`. INVARIANT: the module-doc emitter (`build_module_docs_with_filter`) MUST emit a page for every distinct non-empty `file.module` a file page links to, regardless of the doc-prune scope filter (`doc_scope.includes_module` -> `in_scope`, which keys on file-PATH scopes). Before commit 6292f52ac, a scoped/incremental heal emitted the file pages but the scope filter dropped the synthetic cluster module page, producing dangling file->module links that GREW every heal (curated_broken_link_count diverged 21->38->57->117->140 under the pre-fix binary) and pinned `gwiki trust` at attention_required. Fix: keep direct `file.module` link targets in the emitted set regardless of the scope filter; the filter still bounds ancestor-only modules. Whole-vault trust flip also needs daemon-synthesis concept-page citations (#17704) and pending-source compilation (#17705, note: default `gwiki compile` fail-loud is intended #17635 behavior, use --write-intent).

When a Gobby skill requires entering native Plan Mode and no direct EnterPlanMode tool is available, use the Gobby send_keys command path to send `/plan` plus Enter. Client-specific Gobby triggers like `/gobby plan` or `$gobby plan` may also be used when they are the configured native Plan Mode trigger.

Task #15433 introduced a frontend transport boundary: WebSocket usage payloads use RawSessionUsageUpdatedMessage/RawTokenEventMessage for string-or-number wire values, then normalize through normalizeSessionUsageUpdatedMessage and normalizeTokenEventMessage before consumers such as handleTokenEvent and useTokenEventsStream see strict numeric fields.

Daemon one-shot feature/text-generation CLI calls must run from a neutral temporary cwd, never the project directory, to avoid project context and lifecycle-hook startup overhead. Each adapter owns this isolation; CLI subprocesses use the neutral cwd and stdin=DEVNULL, never request.cwd. Codex must run with its neutral-workspace bypass flags, including --skip-git-repo-check; preserve bounded validation prompts, adapter-appropriate candidate timeouts, and durable error/backoff handling for infrastructure failures. When adding or changing an adapter, verify its working-directory and trust gating first.

As of task #18830 / commit 153ae3b63, daemon code-index projection sync handles GcodeProjectNotFoundError through shared vector/graph lifecycle logic: a vanished root purges the indexed project once; an existing root logs one warning without traceback and stays pending. Vector handling exits the file before graph sync and does not record a circuit-breaker success/failure. Memory KG relation cleanup now fetches outbound then inbound relations through entity_key-anchored UNWIND queries, excludes CO_OCCURS, preserves first-seen exact-triple order, and propagates either query failure to the service partial-failure path. The deletion prompt exposes deterministic r0/r1-style opaque IDs via relation_ids_to_delete; extractor maps valid IDs back to canonical triples, deduplicates, and warns on malformed/unknown IDs.

Gobby storage managers target the backend-neutral HubDatabase protocol, while PostgreSQL is the only supported hub backend. HubDatabase exposes transaction and migration lifecycle operations; typed LockTarget ordering is enforced for immediate transactions to prevent deadlocks. Runtime paths open storage through gobby.storage.hub.runtime, and PostgresHubDatabase remains the public PostgreSQL adapter.

Task #18560 hardened pg_search sanitization and PostgreSQL backend errors. Commit 8e78486ae1c320833b8f708a3ff5b16b5734d3e8. `sanitize_pg_search_query` in crates/gcore/src/search.rs now counts unescaped quotes before scanning: balanced quoted phrases retain their interiors, while dangling quotes are escaped. Outside balanced phrases it escapes Tantivy metacharacters `? ' * : ^ ~ { } / !` in addition to the existing brackets, literal parentheses, leading-minus, and boolean handling. gobby-code and gobby-wiki expectations were updated. gobby-wiki now maps postgres errors through `backend_error`, preserving database detail when present, across all BM25 queries. A real pg_search integration test covers the reported crash corpus, balanced phrases, and dangling quotes; focused results were 9 gobby-wiki BM25 tests, 10 gobby-core search tests, and 4 gobby-code sanitizer tests passing. Targeted cargo fmt and clippy -D warnings passed, and the mandatory test-quality audit found 37 tests with 0 issues. `.gobby/project.json` now registers `gobby-test-quality-audit` as a custom validation matcher so the required `gobby test-quality audit ... --fail-on-new --min-severity ...` command is retained as structured validation evidence.
Gobby Linear sync CLI: `gobby linear sync-all --forward` is the shipped command for active-only forward sync. The earlier pre-release `--active` alias was removed and is now an unrecognized option.

Shutdown cleanup treats expected `asyncio.CancelledError` during graceful shutdown as cancellation rather than a shutdown failure. `MCPClientManager.disconnect_all` cancels and awaits health, reconnect, and disconnect tasks; clears connection, reconnect, health, and lazy connection state; and completes teardown without re-raising cancellation from cleanup. `search.embeddings._fetch_embeddings` owns and awaits `AsyncOpenAI.close()` in a `finally` block.

Gobby storage SQL now uses psycopg/PostgreSQL %s positional placeholders directly; the old hub-layer qmark/$N placeholder remapper was removed, so callers must duplicate/reorder params themselves and escape literal percent signs in parameterized SQL.

For work assigned to one Gobby project when target files are in another repository, create an editable target-repository worktree with gobby-worktrees.create_worktree using the target project_path and a writable temporary worktree_path. Commit in that target worktree with the task ID. Task commit linking and closure remain project-path allowlisted: arbitrary separate-repository commits cannot be linked to the originating task, so record verification evidence and use the approved cross-repo close flow when required. The former gobby-cli sibling repository is now merged into the gobby monorepo under crates/.

For task #19118, the feature itself owns protection of the privileged `live-session` task label against autonomous or spawned-agent mutation. The label guard ships with the stop-gate exemption. Draft #18647 remains focused on broader protected enforcement variables and installed-rule/tag hardening; #19118 does not wait on #18647 for label safety. Decided by the user on 2026-07-27 in session #9771.

Do not create or claim Gobby tasks for plan drafting, plan review, or other read-only planning work. Create or claim a task only before the first authorized file edit when the applicable workflow requires it; planning evidence is recorded through the plan-review protocol rather than a task.

Gobby build is fire-and-forget: after build_task starts lifecycle automation, the dispatcher should advance routine stage transitions itself. For example, when a QA reviewer calls approve_review, dispatcher should advance review_approved -> done and continue merge/downstream dispatch without requiring a coordinator to tick build_task. Coordinator agents for build epics exist to debug/fix automation bugs, not to drive normal lifecycle progression.

In gcode Rust call extraction, local Rust import targets must compute Symbol::make_id with the tree-sitter declaration node byte_start, not the identifier name byte_start. Rust `function_item`/`struct_item` symbols start at the declaration line start (e.g. `pub(crate) fn ...` at `pub`), so `LocalImportBinding.byte_start` for Rust local imports must use declaration-start offsets or graph CALLS edges point at synthetic non-canonical target IDs and `blast-radius` cannot traverse the real symbol.

CLI Postgres ownership is centralized in gobby.cli.runtime.CliRuntime. One top-level Click invocation lazily memoizes a single HubDatabase, shares it with DB-backed config loading and operational helpers, and closes it through Click teardown. Root help and other paths that do not need config must not open the Hub database: CliRuntime also lazily memoizes DaemonConfig through its config_loader. Direct subgroup tests and bounded compositions should inject CliRuntime(config=...) instead of an obj dict. Operational helpers borrow injected databases; runtime_hub_database is reserved for bounded standalone/bootstrap composition roots. PostgresHubDatabase keeps a strong open-instance registry so leaked or failed-close pools remain retryable at atexit.

Block reasons and recovery guidance must keep agents scoped to the immediate user-requested work. Do not suggest backlog browsing such as `list_ready_tasks`. Direct agents to the concrete work in front of them; do not create or claim tasks for plan drafting or plan-review rounds, which use the plan-review protocol instead.

Gobby Rust testing uses `cargo nextest run` for primary non-doctest tests and `cargo test --doc` for doctests. CI and release jobs install nextest and use the `ci` profile for package tests. `--no-default-features` is required for CI degraded-feature coverage; gwiki CI intentionally runs both default-feature and `--no-default-features` nextest jobs to protect both paths.

Pipeline restart recovery is project-independent. Startup discovers projects with RUNNING or INTERRUPTED executions through an unscoped `LocalPipelineExecutionManager(project_id=None)`, then builds or reuses a project-scoped runtime per recoverable project. Resume-on-restart processing must occur before stale-execution failure handling so resumable executions are not broken. Unscoped storage predicates must treat `project_id=None` as all projects; cron execution resolves and retains the executor for each job's project.

Gobby web `useChat` tests should use `web/src/hooks/__tests__/useChat.setup.ts` helpers (`createUseChatTestContext`, `cleanupUseChatTestContext`, `loadUseChatModule`) instead of duplicating WebSocket, fetch, localStorage, and console setup. The shared context seeds `gobby-conversation-id`/`gobby-db-session-id` and mutes console `log`, `debug`, `warn`, and `error` output for Vitest.

Daemon YAML secret migration pattern: GobbyRunner._migrate_yaml_secrets() (runner.py) runs after Phase 2 config reload. It checks known secret fields for plaintext values (not $secret: refs or None), encrypts them via ConfigStore.set_secret() into the SecretStore, rewrites the YAML to use $secret:<name> references, and reloads config. To add a new secret field to migration, add a tuple to the secret_fields list: (dotted_attr_path, secret_name). The $secret:<name> pattern is resolved by expand_env_vars() in config/app.py during config loading.

Web-chat interactive permission gates must preserve tool_use_id end-to-end: pending waiter dictionaries, UI pending frames, and approval, question, and plan response handlers all use the same ID. This prevents one concurrent response from resolving a different tool call's waiter.

Codewiki per-run observability can be threaded without expanding GenerateDocsOptions: let generate_hierarchical_docs own and return the aggregate, pass a mutable reference only through producers, then attach the completed aggregate to DocSink before finish. Diagram statistics use the unique slot key (page path, diagram kind), log only on first record, and serialize only counters so `_meta/codewiki.json` stays stable while the in-memory slot set enforces one final outcome per attempted slot.

Gobby session boundary contract after task #18994 / commit 27b748110 (supersedes #18742 compact semantics): SessionEnd(reason='clear') expires the session; only reason='compact' marks handoff_ready. SessionStart(source='clear') creates an independent session with no parent discovery, predecessor expiry, summary/task/skill transfer, or claim reassignment. Compaction is an IN-PLACE handoff: the compact restart reactivates the SAME sessions row (handoff_ready -> active) via resolve_session_start_identity in _session_start/handoff.py — no parent matching, no transfer, no child row. Identity, session variables, workflow instances, claimed tasks, parent linkage, and agent-run ownership carry through untouched; bounded summary injection, required-skill preservation, and compact_self continuation run on the same row. A one-shot 'handoff_source' session variable marker (set by pre_compact rule, consumed on successful reactivation) classifies compact restarts for providers that omit source='compact'; expired rows with an unconsumed marker revive as compact; missing rows degrade to startup registration with a structured WARNING; only contradicting terminal identity blocks. Resume and ordinary exits expire; idle web-chat sessions pause. Clear remains a native provider hook value and context-loss source for startup, memory, skill, and progressive-discovery resets.

For Gobby CodeWiki/gwiki narrative generation, use configuration-selected profile-based generation. Single completions use the `one_shot` route; agentic aggregate narrative uses the shared local tool-enabled `tool_loop` route. Do not restore the removed codex-exec writer API or writer plumbing.

Pipeline templates now live in src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/pipelines/ as individual YAML files with `type: pipeline`. The sync_bundled_workflows() handles both workflows and pipelines by detecting the `type` field. There is no separate pipelines sync target. The orphan cleanup in sync_bundled_workflows filters by workflow_type='workflow', so pipeline rows are preserved.

wait_for_agent is an immediate subscribe-and-return MCP tool. Its public signature is wait_for_agent(run_id: str). Terminal runs return inline with notification_registered=false. Active runs require ambient session context, the completion registry, and DB; they register and persist only the calling session through subscribe_agent_completion(strict=True). SessionManager and lineage resolution are not required. The status re-read, registration, post-registration re-read, and fresh-entry cleanup remain one owning-loop no-await critical region; cleanup deletes only subscription.inserted_session_ids, while merged entries remain for a pending notify snapshot. Updated by task #18928 / commit f2e7feb27.

Rule-engine MCP-call effects are carried in hook response metadata and dispatched by the hook/MCP dispatch layer through `ToolProxyService`. Dispatch must pass only schema-valid tool arguments: do not inject prompt text or other extra parameters, because schema validation rejects unknown fields. Log dispatch failures rather than discarding call results.

Web chat sendMode semantics: before a conversation exists, changing mode is an intentional local selection and succeeds. Once a conversation exists, sendMode commits currentMode only after set_mode is sent successfully over the still-open same WebSocket; SendModeAction returns boolean success so transport failures are observable.

In Codex sessions, Gobby skill routing is commonly invoked with `$gobby <skill> ...`; `/gobby <skill> ...` is the router-contract form used in Gobby skill docs. Skills intended for Codex should mention `$gobby` when giving user-facing invocation examples.

RuleDefinitionBody no longer supports singular `effect=` parameter. Only `effects=[...]` (list) is accepted. The backward-compat `_normalize_effect_to_effects` model validator was removed. All YAML templates already used `effects:` — only test code used the singular form.

Pre-0.5.0 workflow preservation uses the current multi-row `workflow_instances` model. Task #18973 (92b3ca567) made SESSION_END classify compact/idle before cleanup with compact/web-chat-idle retention; task #18994 (27b748110) then made compaction an IN-PLACE handoff: the compact restart reactivates the same sessions row (tri-state terminal identity match/conflict/unknown; one-shot handoff_source marker consumed on reactivation), and `transfer_compact_handoff_state` plus the parent→child transfer model were deleted. Orphan handoff sweep is expire-only with a marker-gated retention sweep pruning workflow instances after the revival horizon.

Task #18974 (commit 6af56e35c) + fix round #18995 use the DURABLE-SESSION daemon-resume model. A managed child session_id never changes across daemon stop/start. Shutdown preserves active runs INCLUDING reconciliation_pending ones; `_preserved_agent_terminal_pids` returns set[int] | None — None means run enumeration failed and the caller SKIPS child reaping entirely (never mass-kill); pane PIDs are resolved per-run from persisted tmux socket identity (tmux_socket_name/path in resume_metadata_json, #18936 model) with stored-PID fallback. Startup: lifecycle monitor is the serialized reconciliation owner and its start() failure fails agent-lifecycle startup closed; barrier replay (fresh+stale inbox) → provisional resolution → dead/live classification → only then subscriber recovery, which excludes recovery-pending parked originals from terminal redelivery. The reclassification pass runs ONLY when reconciliation_pending runs exist — an empty fence set never triggers the barrier, so transient inbox residue cannot fence healthy runs.

Parking is `cancelled` with terminal_reason=`daemon_stop`: session paused, workflow rows/task claims/worktrees/clones/merged-task artifacts/subscriber delivery all retained, only the dispatch mutex cleared. Session-terminal expiry sweep is back-pointer-authoritative (`sessions.agent_run_id = run.id` only; the child_session_id disjunct was dropped so a consumed original can never expire a live successor's session); accepted deviation: non-back-pointed child sessions rely on the 24h expire_stale_sessions idle sweep. Protocol keys live in `src/gobby/storage/daemon_resume_keys.py` (daemon_resume_consumed/unconsumed_condition is the canonical consumed predicate). Relaunch creates a new run on the SAME session via `prepare_terminal_resume`, guarded back-pointer CAS (rebind_agent_run COALESCEs a None workflow_name), deterministic tmux title `gobby-resume-<run_id>` (boot correlates exact-then-prefix), JSONB phases prepared→launch_requested→runtime_persisted→finalized via expected-phase CAS. finalize_daemon_resume is idempotent (repeat → already_finalized) and shares an advisory fence with wait_for_agent registration; the reaper seeds the in-memory completion registry from DB completion_subscribers before delivering, so DB-backed waiters get real terminal results. Successors inherit metadata with ALL protocol keys stripped (`_INHERITED_PROTOCOL_KEYS`), so the failure budget resets; the failure count increments only on actual failures, with a regex-guarded ::int cast. Non-task parked runs are retried by a lifecycle-monitor pass (`_retry_parked_non_task_resumes`, 3-failure budget); `gobby build stop` flags parked runs and routes them through the orphan reaper (parked_runs_released).

Hook ingress: the terminal-event gate applies to SESSION_END/STOP/AFTER_AGENT only (TERMINAL_INGRESS_HOOK_TYPES; the dead SESSION_START gate branch was deleted). Session lookup defers revive/backfill mutations until the gate accepts (resolve(apply_session_mutations=False) + apply_session_mutations after). Daemon-not-ready is never fail-open: health gate raises DaemonNotReadyError → /api/hooks/execute returns 503 {"status":"retry"} and releases the processing claim; ghook treats 503+status=retry as backpressure (envelope retained, child continues); STOP/AFTER_AGENT still fail closed with decision=block. ID-less inbox envelopes replayed with 2xx are quarantined (missing_envelope_id) so the startup barrier settles. Dispatcher resume never falls back to fresh spawn after candidate selection; the retry-exhaustion escalation marker distinguishes clean retries-exhausted from workspace-dirty. A 24-hour orphan reaper performs the deferred full cleanup and suppressed delivery, with per-run error containment. `clone_instances_for_session` remains deleted (replacement-child design rejected). #18879 remains future migration work and must preserve these semantics.

Tmux window-title repair should derive the visible session prefix from Session.seq_num when available and treat any literal "session_ref" text in a ref, title, or window name as an unresolved placeholder. The repair sweep intentionally re-renames already-managed tmux windows when their current window name contains that placeholder.

`sessions.chat_mode` persists web-chat mode and remains distinct from workflow `session_variables.chat_mode`. For attached tmux/CLI sessions, session table mode and reasoning-effort columns can be stale; use workflow session variables for the freshest observed values.

Gobby source branches keep the root-anchored local `wiki/` vault ignored. Git hook installation and Git-root `gobby init` use `wiki_branch_setup.py` to prepare or reuse sibling `../<repo-name>-wiki` on branch `wiki`, mirror vault contents there, and publish only when the detected default branch is pushed. Claude Code 2.x records hook blocks as top-level `type: "attachment"` entries whose `attachment.type` is `hook_blocking_error`. Gobby workflow rule evaluation expands raw `before_agent` to semantic `turn_start`, and raw `after_agent`, `stop`, and `stop_failure` to semantic `turn_end` in `src/gobby/workflows/engine/core.py`. `src/gobby/workflows/hooks.py` uses a narrower observer turn-end helper for `after_agent` and `stop` during hook-side bookkeeping.

MCP transport health checks preserve their latest bounded one-line failure reason in BaseTransportConnection.last_health_error. Client manager health aggregation records that exact reason, and get_server_health plus admin status expose it as last_error; successful checks clear it.
