In the Gobby repo, `crates/gwiki` is the Rust crate package `gobby-wiki`; focused gwiki tests should use `cargo test -p gobby-wiki <test-name>` rather than `-p gwiki`, which is only the binary target name.

Rule-condition helpers have a canonical shared builder, with rule-engine-specific helpers layered on top. Add generally safe reusable helpers to the shared builder so conditions gain them consistently; keep rule-specific enforcement helpers in the rule-engine layer. Rule-engine evaluation is now split across workflows/engine/core.py, event_utils.py, and evaluation.py.

TaskSyncManager.import_from_github_issues derives deterministic UUIDv5 task IDs from project ID plus normalized owner/repo/issue number, deduplicates within the target project on github_repo and github_issue_number, and fills seq_num/path_cache via _ensure_task_sequence_metadata.

Task #19071 (commit 3377c679c) changed repair attestation `deviation_from_minimal_repair` from a nullable free-form string to null or one closed five-key object. The canonical keys, in order, are `violated_invariant`, `original_counterexample`, `how_alternative_closes_it`, `validation_evidence`, and `accepted_risk`; every value is a non-empty string, and literal `none` records an explicit absence of added risk. `DEVIATION_PROOF_FIELDS` is the named schema in `gobby.plans.review_repair`; taskless building, submission canonicalization, JSON encode/decode rendering, staged transport, and round-preparation coverage all route through the same nested canonicalizer. The bundled plan skill and planner contract teach the identical object.

Gobby config API/default/export surfaces should use Pydantic aliases (`model_dump(..., by_alias=True)`) for external config keys. In particular, the external task config key is `gobby-tasks` to match the MCP server name; `gobby_tasks` is only the Python attribute spelling.

Checklist criteria-review accounting after epic #19101: an invalid bounded LLM verdict appends task_validation_history and increments validation_fail_count. Provider, timeout, dependency, environment, and verdict-parse infrastructure failures append history, persist validation_status=error, and advance TaskValidationBackoffStore without incrementing the semantic failure counter. A valid verdict clears active infrastructure backoff; successful close resets live validation failure state while preserving history. Transcript evidence consumes settled provider outcomes at close time and stores no verification receipts.

Task JSONL restore rebuilds path_cache for newly inserted tasks only after every backup task is present in the transaction. This makes hierarchical refs order-independent while preserving final seq_num collision handling and same-project parent scoping.

In Gobby agent terminal spawn flow, prepare_terminal_spawn creates the child session and inserts the agent_runs row using the provided agent_run_id before terminal/tmux spawn. Resume code should not pre-insert the same run_id unless prepare_terminal_spawn is changed to support an existing run row.

As of task #18659 (commit fd7ceaaa5), install-time environment readiness checks are owned by src/gobby/cli/_install_daemon.py: source-checkout detection, Docker availability, port availability, and full-install preflight. src/gobby/cli/install.py retains Click orchestration and imports _run_install_preflight as the command-level patch seam.

PostgreSQL, FalkorDB, and Qdrant are the required Gobby runtime infrastructure: PostgreSQL is the authoritative hub, FalkorDB is the knowledge-graph backend, and Qdrant backs embedding recall. Commands must still handle a required service being unavailable according to their contract—such as bounded empty graph results or surfaced degradation—without describing those services as optional product enhancers.

Remote skill installation security contract: src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/skills/install_skill.py treats hub, GitHub, and ZIP sources as external via is_external_source. If scan_parsed_skill raises ImportError because clawcare is unavailable, those installs return success=false before persistence; local filesystem installs warn and continue. Regression coverage for all external source types lives in tests/mcp_proxy/tools/skills/test_install_skill_scanning.py (implementation from #17658; complete remote-type coverage added by #16108, commit ce40fc669).

Gobby-created ACP-backed provider sessions use the existing Sessions tab and canonical session model alongside TMUX and WEB sessions; their supported actions remain capability-driven. Provider-native `session/list` history is excluded from canonical sessions, and there is no browser ACP discovery or separate provider control panel.

Gobby voice startup dependency checks import the Chatterbox stack and can trigger resemble-perth's `pkg_resources is deprecated as an API` UserWarning. Runtime code should suppress only that known import-time Perth warning via `gobby.voice._warnings.suppress_perth_pkg_resources_warning()` around Chatterbox/voice dependency imports; pytest's `filterwarnings` does not affect daemon startup logs. Implemented for task #17184 in commit d430b77c8.

Codex Plan Mode reaches the digest-owned session-title lifecycle through the installed `digest-on-plan-turn-end` rule matching normalized `PostToolUse` tool name `request_user_input`; Claude boundaries `ExitPlanMode` and `AskUserQuestion` remain supported. Added in task #18901 / commit f9f0ff8c4. Prompt-derived title bootstrapping remains intentionally removed.

For Gobby build-autonomy regression work, the repeatable CI-safe coverage lives in tests/e2e/test_build_dispatcher_autonomy.py as a deterministic fake-agent mini-build harness. Idle wakeup regressions should assert no direct test sleeps, semantic reprompts only after the 300s idle delay, Escape before prompt text, and a separate raw Enter keypress.

Skill ingestion resource limits are centralized in src/gobby/skills/limits.py. Current boundaries are 1 MiB per SKILL.md, 64 KiB frontmatter, 20 YAML aliases, 1 MiB per loaded companion file, 10 MiB total stored content per skill, and 64 KiB hub stream chunks. Parser and loader reject overages before unbounded reads. Hub response handling is centralized in src/gobby/skills/hubs/_streaming.py and used by both GitHub Collection and Claude Plugins.

Task #17042 removed the legacy top-level Memory page subtree from `web/src/components/memory/` and deleted the AppPages lazy `MemoryPage` export, the `activeTab === "memory"` branch in `web/src/App.tsx`, and the top-level Memory nav/APP_VALID_TABS entries in `web/src/components/app/appNavigation.tsx`. The canonical Memory UI is now only the Activity panel Memory tab under `web/src/components/activity/memory/`.

In dev-parity-plus ghook, source detection lives in `crates/ghook/src/source.rs`. `detect_source` only honors non-empty `GOBBY_SOURCE` for the canonical Claude source; `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py` no longer has a separate branch and falls through to `claude`. Statusline downstream commands on Unix are started in their own process group and killed by process group on timeout to avoid nextest child-process leak warnings.

As of task #18796, GET /api/config/effective in configuration_effective.py requires a valid Bearer or X-Gobby-Local-Token via AuthService.verify_bearer even when global auth is disabled, rejects cookie-only access, and returns Cache-Control: no-store. It serves only ai./databases./indexing./gwiki. dotted keys, excludes routing and ai.embeddings.switch_run, resolves ConfigStore $secret: and ${ENV} references through SecretStore.get, omits unresolved or undecryptable values, and overlays resolved DaemonConfig embeddings/FalkorDB/Qdrant/Postgres DSN values with overlay None deleting stored rows.

Task #17240 decomposed Linear sync while preserving the public `gobby.sync.linear` facade. `LinearSyncService` now inherits implementation from `gobby.sync.linear_task_ops.LinearTaskOpsMixin`, which builds on `linear_project_ops.LinearProjectOpsMixin`; shared exceptions, title/ref parsing, state mapping, and repeated fetch-failure limiting live in `gobby.sync.linear_support`. `gobby.sync.linear._linear_fetch_failure_limiter` remains as a compatibility alias for existing tests/callers.

In gobby-cli on macOS, a fresh `cargo nextest list/run --workspace --no-default-features` after rebuilding `gobby-wiki` test binaries can sit silent for ~30 seconds while nextest children run `--list --format terse`. A `sample` of `target/debug/deps/cli_sources-* --list --format terse` during task #560 showed 4510/4510 frames in `_dyld_start`, 96 KB footprint, and 0% CPU, before Rust/libtest/repo code. Treat this as macOS cold loader latency unless a sample reaches Rust frames; warmed runs complete normally.

For Gobby pytest runs with GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, tests/fixtures/postgres.py falls back to ~/.gobby/bootstrap.yaml when DATABASE_URL is unset. To avoid touching the user daemon database during agent validation, create an isolated temporary database in the local gobby-postgres container, install pg_search and pgcrypto there, run pytest with DATABASE_URL=postgresql://gobby:gobby_dev@localhost:60891/<temp_db>, then drop the temp database after the DB-backed tests finish.

HookManager decomposition completed in task #14829: public imports remain through gobby.hooks.hook_manager.HookManager, while workflow rule evaluation lives in gobby.hooks.rule_evaluator.WorkflowRuleEvaluator, #N MCP session ref rewriting in gobby.hooks.session_ref_resolution, session summary scheduling in gobby.hooks.session_summary_dispatcher.SessionSummaryDispatcher, project ID fallback/DB ensure in gobby.hooks.project_context.ProjectIdResolver, and fire-and-forget broadcast scheduling in gobby.hooks.broadcaster.schedule_hook_broadcast.

Claude Agent SDK ResultMessage subtype must be preserved on ClaudeSDKProviderFailure. When subtype=error_during_execution occurs while a fresh, valid shutdown-intent marker is active, the daemon's child reaper interrupted the SDK process; claude_runtime converts it to ClaudeSDKShutdownCancellation, and session summary generation propagates asyncio.CancelledError so background task cleanup stays quiet. Outside planned shutdown, the same provider failure remains warning-visible.

For Gobby monolith/refactor decisions, the 1,000-line principle applies to non-test code files, especially Python, TypeScript, TSX, and CSS. Large generated, SQL baseline, test, documentation, and content files do not by themselves require refactoring or block the current task.

Gobby task expansion has two compile paths: Plan-Coverage Contract plans compile deterministically through `src/gobby/tasks/expansion/_contract.py`, while ad hoc expansion of existing non-contract tasks continues to use the LLM-backed path.

In the Gobby repo, `gobby unpack` validates tar archive extraction paths with `src/gobby/cli/pack.py` `_safe_archive_target`, rejecting absolute paths, parent-directory traversal, and non-regular/non-directory members before writing under Gobby home, project `.gobby`, or temporary PostgreSQL restore roots.

Describe Gobby as an agent control plane for interactive and autonomous work. Emphasize deterministic boundaries for task lifecycle, hooks, rules, validation, review, isolation, and commits while preserving agent freedom for creative implementation.

CRITICAL: Use `uv run gobby` instead of `gobby` for development! The system-wide `gobby` CLI (`~/.local/bin/gobby`) uses a global uv tools install that may be outdated. Always use `uv run gobby start` to run the daemon from the local development environment. Commands: `uv run gobby start` (start daemon), `uv run gobby stop` (stop), `uv run gobby restart` (restart).

Task #17564 made memory content revision first-class: storage update_memory now accepts normalized non-empty content while preserving memory IDs, rejects same-scope duplicate revised content including hidden rows, handles old deterministic ID collisions on recreate, and MemoryLifecycleService refreshes embeddings, graph pending state, graph artifacts, and crossrefs after content edits. Commit: a2e1d26db.

Gobby cross-session and cross-tool handoff transfers a generated or agent-authored `summary_markdown` into successor session variables; the full provider transcript remains a separately stored/retrievable session record and is not injected verbatim as the handoff. Provider-side prompt caches, native conversation state, and provider-private reasoning/thinking artifacts are outside this handoff contract.

Gobby task lifecycle state is canonical. Hub/admin aggregate queries should use persisted `tasks.state_bucket` rather than recomputing task state through a CASE expression joined to `task_stage_states`; migration 244 and schema triggers keep the bucket current. Cross-project task queries expose and filter the serialized task state payload, while session statistics continue to use `by_status`.

Subscription-authenticated SDK integration direction: use existing CLI OAuth only and never invoke SDK login or accept API-key auth. OpenAI Codex SDK 0.144.4 may support eligible Codex text/vision routes subject to paid-tier account validation, but it has no dynamic-tool surface, so Codex tool chat must remain on CodexAppServerClient rather than AsyncCodex. Droid SDK routes require bounded single-use/custom transport handling; do not use `droid_sdk.query`. Preserve legacy routes until separately approved cleanup, keep Gobby lifecycle authoritative with `GOBBY_HOOKS_DISABLED=1` for children, and do not change the user's active branch during planning/review.

Web-chat usage handling persists token accounting and model/context-window metadata while treating context pressure separately. Canonical occupancy uses session snapshot fields context_used_tokens and context_usage_ratio with context_window; cumulative usage_* and token-event session totals are historical accounting and must not drive occupancy UI.

Gobby task state is PostgreSQL-authoritative; `.gobby/tasks.jsonl` is an append-style backup/sync surface. When inspecting JSONL directly, collapse records by task id and newest `updated_at` before drawing conclusions, because older rows may still look active. Prefer current task APIs or PostgreSQL-backed views for authoritative state.

As of task #16607 / commit 75bf7ed51, session registration identity is project-independent: SessionRegistration serializes (external_id, machine_id, source, session_type), excluding project_id. A projectless registration that runs after a project-scoped registration reuses the matching cross-project row; a later known-project registration can recover and move that same row.

As of task #16013 / commit 3ce01a731, PipelineHeartbeat protects healthy executions by treating a persisted active session as liveness even without agent runs, skipping stalled rows with no owning session, and letting agent-store probe errors abort that candidate. Heartbeat refresh/failure writes use LocalPipelineExecutionManager.update_stalled_execution_status, a CAS requiring both RUNNING status and the scanned updated_at; races log that state changed and leave the newer state intact.

Testing pattern: Many gobby modules use lazy imports inside function bodies (e.g., `import litellm` inside `_discover_models()`, `from gobby.sessions.transcripts import get_parser` inside route handlers). When mocking these, you MUST patch at the source module level (e.g., `patch('litellm.model_cost', ...)`, `patch('gobby.sessions.transcripts.get_parser')`) rather than at the importing module level (e.g., NOT `patch('gobby.servers.routes.admin.litellm')`). Key examples: websockets in tts.py, litellm in admin.py, get_parser/generate_summary in sessions.py, LocalProjectManager/RunningAgent in admin.py.

Task #14291 implemented epic integration build workspaces: public build surfaces use --clone or workspace_backend/clone instead of isolation; epic tasks store integration_branch plus integration_workspace_id/integration_clone_id; descendant leaves target the nearest parent integration branch; non-root merge stages dispatch MergeWorkspaceAction to merge worktree/clone sources into the parent integration workspace under integration_workspace_mutex.

Gobby plan parsing shares resolve_plan_id() between parser and manifest handling. Missing or literal unknown Plan IDs are draft-mode warnings and implementation-plan expansion/strict-mode errors, preventing covers:unknown manifests from validating; strategy plans remain unaffected. extract_section_dependencies(title) splits comma-separated (depends: ...) annotations while preserving values such as Phase 1.

For Gobby Codex spawned agents, the Codex MCP config overrides for the internal gobby server must carry the child context env (at least GOBBY_SESSION_ID and GOBBY_PROJECT_ID, plus related agent env when available). The stdio DaemonProxy reads these env values to send X-Gobby-Session-Id/X-Gobby-Project-Id so lifecycle tools such as gobby-tasks:claim_task work without wrapper session_id arguments in child sessions.

In dev-parity-plus ghook, `crates/ghook/src/transport.rs::atomic_write` fsyncs the tmp file, renames it into place, then best-effort fsyncs the parent directory; directory fsync errors are intentionally ignored for platforms/filesystems that reject them. The repo nextest config also assigns package `gobby-hooks` to the `ghook-process` test group with `max-threads = 2` because full parallel ghook runs on macOS produced intermittent nextest `LEAK` markers on pure `cli_config` tests while serial/lower-concurrency runs and isolated subprocess tests were clean.

When testing WorkflowLoader after the DB-first refactoring, use LocalWorkflowDefinitionManager to insert workflow definitions into the DB rather than creating YAML files on disk. The loader fixture should be WorkflowLoader(db=temp_db) not WorkflowLoader(workflow_dirs=[...]). The workflow_dirs parameter is legacy/unused at runtime.

Plan-review findings use one four-tier severity vocabulary: blocking, major, minor, nit. `minimal_repair` is the only remedy field; lane candidates alone retain `suggested_fix`. Task #19087 (commit c351b71c7) adds required `repair_scope`, closed to `existing_sections` or `new_deliverable`. `new_deliverable` requires a non-empty `new_deliverable_justification` explaining why no existing host section can own the obligation; `existing_sections` forbids that field and uses `section_id`/`participating_section_ids` as its host. Blocking findings still require an all-or-nothing `failure_trace`. The canonical validator, rejection renderer, staged reject-review JSON Schema, quality ledger, lesson reconstruction, bundled plan-review skill, and both adversary producer contracts preserve the same shape.

Gcode CodeWiki reuse keys pages on `CODEWIKI_RENDER_VERSION` plus source hash and AI mode. A render-version bump invalidates reuse globally; `--since <ref>` targets source-changed pages and does not apply a render-only change. Full AI regeneration is sequential and costly, so use deterministic in-place updates for small curated render-only deltas when appropriate. `_meta/codewiki.json` and `.obsidian/*` are gitignored and must not be staged.

Droid CLI exposes a documented one-shot text path via `droid exec [prompt]` with `--output-format`, `--model`, `--session-id`, stdin/file input, and noninteractive execution. It does not expose an ACP flag in top-level help as of 2026-05-30, so daemon text_generate should use Droid exec rather than fabricating an ACP adapter.

SafeExpressionEvaluator intentionally rejects keyword spread (`f(**values)`) and dictionary spread (`{**values}`) with clear ValueError messages as of task #18313 / commit 6a0a2f503. Ordinary named keyword arguments and dictionary literals remain supported; the guards run before evaluating spread operands so unsupported syntax cannot be silently discarded.

Step workflow enforcement now supports handler-level `when` conditions on both `on_mcp_success` and `on_mcp_error`. The handler context merges `vars`, `tool_output`, and a flattened `tool_input` that exposes inner MCP `arguments`/`args` keys at the top level, which is what allows installed planner workflows to gate on expressions like `tool_input.name == 'plan-draft'` or `tool_input.name == 'plan-review'`.

Qwen one-shot text generation uses a direct headless CLI path, disables chat recording, and receives configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint credentials through child environment variables rather than command-line arguments or stale `~/.qwen/settings.json` provider/model settings. Endpoint configuration follows the current generic generation-endpoint contract.

As of task #18690, daemon HTTP `/ws` is mounted as a direct ASGI adapter over the shared `WebSocketServer._handle_connection` handler and client/subscription registry. The old loopback TCP bridge and local-token forwarding are gone. Authentication is checked before ASGI accept; unauthenticated handshakes are rejected as HTTP 403. Authenticated text messages, binary TTS frames, backend close codes/reasons, and registry cleanup all use the shared handler. Vite HMR keeps its separate proxy.

As of task #12649, session lifecycle cleanup treats terminal sessions without terminal_context as legacy/untracked and expires them by created_at once they exceed stale_session_timeout_hours, even if updated_at was refreshed by transcript/stat processing. SessionManager.register also backfills terminal_context and workflow_name when an existing session re-registers, so tmux liveness can map the pane. Regression coverage lives in tests/storage/sessions/test_lifecycle_expiry.py and tests/storage/sessions/test_register_fallback.py.

Web chat display is a provider-agnostic canonical renderer: regardless of CLI/provider, transcript ingestion should normalize upstream into shared ContentBlock/tool_chain/text/unknown shapes so the web chat output renders consistently for users with no provider-specific frontend branching.

TextGenerationService now receives `config.ai.generation.profile_defaults` from `build_daemon_text_generation_service`; profile-only generation requests check those configured profile candidates before falling back to hardcoded default_candidates_for_profile. Candidate overrides stay normalized through normalize_feature_candidate and preserve explicit candidate/provider routing precedence.

`compact_self` behavior is provider-specific: Codex sends C-c before `/compact`; Claude, Qwen, and Droid use Escape before their slash command. Codex continuation captures a pre-command pane baseline, persists a marker, waits for a fresh `Context compacted` marker, then atomically submits the pending prompt; stale markers must not trigger and failed sends restore the marker. Tmux pane IDs such as `%NN` are targeted raw, while named sessions use exact `=name:` targeting.

Embedding-switch journals are private lifecycle state: callers must use ConfigStore.get/set/delete_internal_lifecycle directly, never public config fallbacks. Abort cleanup must preflight all current vector aliases before deleting any staged physical collection, and refuse cleanup if a staged name is still alias-targeted.

Dependabot/security dep bumps in web/: do NOT force esbuild to >=0.28 globally. Vite (^0.25.0) uses esbuild to downlevel for the old build target (chrome87/es2020/etc.), and esbuild 0.28+ dropped destructuring downleveling for that target, so `vite build` fails with 'Transforming destructuring to the configured target environment is not supported yet'. The vulnerable esbuild (CVE range >=0.27.3 <0.28.1) is pulled by tsx (~0.27.0), NOT vite (vite stays on esbuild 0.25.x, which is below the vuln floor and build-safe). Fix: scope the override to tsx only — `"overrides": { "tsx": { "esbuild": ">=0.28.1" } }` — leaving vite/direct esbuild at ^0.25.0. Also prefer within-major override caps (e.g. undici/protobufjs/@babel/core `>=X <8`) so a `>=` override doesn't silently jump a transitive dep to a new major.

Managed web-chat text-plan providers must broadcast pending plans once after the stream completes, using fully accumulated text; never broadcast from an intermediate DoneEvent. In-stream DoneEvents must not terminate a tool-using turn early. Explicit tool-plan flows such as Claude ExitPlanMode and Droid ExitSpecMode instead park an approval event and map approval, revision, cancellation, and timeout through their provider-specific plan flow.

Product navigation direction for Gobby web UI: long term, Chat and Config should become the only top-level pages, with the hamburger/sidebar retired. Feature-specific operational surfaces, such as MCP servers, should move into Chat's Activity panel where practical; durable management/configuration belongs in Config.

spawn_agent now returns observable metadata when a retry finds an active same-task run (run_id, status, child_session_id, parent_session_id, task_id, agent_name), and refuses to launch a new agent for a resolved task that is no longer actionable. This prevents retry paths after caller timeouts from silently creating duplicate work on already-closed tasks.

TranscriptReader remains the public DB-first, gzip-archive fallback facade for rendered session messages. The deprecated search_messages MCP stub was removed; use search_session_messages for transcript-backed substring search. Its implementation is split across transcript helper modules.

Chat UI rules engine parity: MCP normalization is now shared between CLI adapter and web-chat via hooks/normalization.py:normalize_mcp_fields(). MCP call effects from rules are dispatched via hooks/mcp_dispatch.py:dispatch_mcp_calls() (async-native). Direct websocket tool_call messages now fire BEFORE_TOOL/AFTER_TOOL hooks in handlers.py. SESSION_START fires after _create_chat_session(), SESSION_END fires before cleanup in clear_chat, delete_chat, idle cleanup, and server stop(). Session context enrichment (Gobby Session ID: #N) is injected in _fire_lifecycle after workflow evaluation.

Web chat has built-in Gobby slash commands plus per-session ACP commands. ACP commands are normalized from available_commands_update events, stored by useChat, merged into colon autocomplete with duplicate removal, and submitted as normal prompt text through the acp_prompt action. Built-in command behavior remains handled by the web chat action composition layer.

The public fetchWorkflows(params?) and fetchRules(params?) callbacks treat an omitted argument as an explicit unfiltered fetch. Internal mutation and WebSocket refreshes therefore use private refetch callbacks backed by refs holding the latest caller filters, preserving include_deleted and other active filters while retaining the public ability to clear filters with an argument-less fetch. Implemented in task #16671 / commit a70bdbf6b.

For Gobby stdio MCP session references, DaemonProxy derives project_id from GOBBY_PROJECT_ID or the nearest .gobby/project.json. Codex/stdio wrappers may send X-Gobby-Session-Id as #N without X-Gobby-Project-Id, and execution.py bootstraps project scope from this session header before resolving target refs.

Gobby chat attachments are implemented with `chat_attachments` PostgreSQL metadata plus project-scoped files under `GOBBY_HOME/projects/<project-id>/attachments/<id-prefix>/<id>/...`. HTTP routes live in `src/gobby/servers/routes/chat_attachments.py`; WebSocket binding/prompt reference helpers live in `src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat_attachments.py`. Main chat and terminal proxy messages send stored references as `attachments: [{id}]`; the backend binds IDs and injects filename/MIME/size plus `id=<attachment-id>` into prompts, not local filesystem paths. The UI renders attachment content from `/api/chat/attachments/{id}/content`.

Reused agent worktree sync now aborts `git rebase` when the 120s rebase command raises `TimeoutExpired`, then surfaces a RuntimeError. Worktree reuse also checks `LocalWorktreeManager.is_claimed_by_live_session()` before rebasing an existing row and refuses reuse while the row owner session is `active` or `paused`.

In gobby-cli task #620, codewiki symbol loading moved from per-file visibility::visible_symbols_for_file calls to visibility::visible_symbols_for_files, which batches file_path filtering with ANY($2)/ANY($3). Overlay mode preserves existing shadowing semantics by excluding parent symbols whenever code_indexed_files has an overlay row for the same file path, including tombstones. codewiki::run calls load_symbols_for_codewiki once and tests assert the loader is invoked once for multiple files.

Gobby Phase 3 build service (#12805) implements `gobby.build.service.build` as the shared entry point for plan files, epic refs, and leaf refs. It validates skip stages, quick-profile plan-file use, leaf isolation, clone dir writability, git target branch existence when the project repo is initialized, and epic isolation artifact conflicts. Plan-file builds create a planning epic, store plan/target artifacts, set lifecycle automation fields, and record a `gobby build` lifecycle event; leaf builds force `isolation='none'` and `in_development`; epic builds use `LocalTaskManager.cascade_build_state_to_subtree`. Supporting storage conveniences added: `LocalTaskManager.artifacts`, `LocalTaskManager.lifecycle_events`, automation-field updates through `update_task`, and `TaskLifecycleEventManager.list_events`.

Gobby’s managed local Docker Compose stack includes PostgreSQL, Qdrant, and FalkorDB. Installer-managed services use `src/gobby/data/docker-compose.services.yml` with `qdrant`, `falkor`, and `all` profiles. Qdrant is a remote HTTP vector service; embedding dimensions are configured under `embeddings.dim`. Runtime Compose configuration is resolved through `src/gobby/cli/installers/compose_env.py`, with credentials and service settings sourced from the canonical bootstrap, ConfigStore, and SecretStore paths.

As of task #18873 (commit 2e5ef347e), CodeWiki text behavior keeps `crates/gcode/src/commands/codewiki/text.rs` as the caller-facing facade. Its AI generation implementation now uses a thin `text/generation.rs` re-export facade with five child modules: `generation/routing.rs` owns AI-context and direct-tier routing; `one_shot.rs` owns text/verifier resolution, bounded retry, prompt bounding, warning-once behavior, and `maybe_generate`; `outcome.rs` owns generation content/status/observability, failure codes, daemon/tool-loop conversion, echo/refusal detection, and output cleaning; `tool_loop.rs` owns read-only tool policy, direct/daemon agentic execution, prompts, graph-degradation reporting, and limits; `aggregate.rs` owns lane constants and aggregate orchestration. Dependency flow is routing/outcome → one_shot/tool_loop → aggregate → facade. `structural.rs`, `citations.rs`, `frontmatter.rs`, and `sanitize.rs` retain their prior responsibilities, and `codewiki/mod.rs` continues re-exporting through `text`.

Merge tooling bug fix #14889: merge_apply must not return success after a merge commit if git status --porcelain is dirty. Commit e533c8e80 adds post-commit clean-tree checks for active and direct merge completions, returns dirty_files plus merge/commit SHA context on failure, and keeps the resolution unresolved so orchestration does not silently record a dirty merge as complete.

Settings sections use nested DaemonConfig values even when their draft keys are dotted paths: read values by walking the dotted path, and save flat dotted-key drafts through the backend flattener. Save deep-merges and therefore does not delete removed map entries. Reuse configSchema.ts for schema traversal and enum/bounds lookup, and reusable field helpers from web/src/components/settings/sections/configAccessors.ts and configFields.tsx. Keep App-owned ui_settings selections separate from daemon-config section drafts.

Rust CLI progress rendering for gcode/gwiki is centralized in gobby_core::progress::ProgressBar. The gcode and gwiki indexing/sync APIs intentionally take explicit progress/options parameters; do not add no-op compatibility wrappers for the pre-0.5.0 signatures.
InternalToolRegistry.list_tools() returns list[dict[str, str]] with 'name' and 'brief' keys, NOT objects with .name attribute. When checking tool names in tests, use t['name'] not t.name.

VectorStore's Qdrant client contract is dual-mode: local stores use synchronous qdrant_client.QdrantClient, while configured remote URLs use AsyncQdrantClient. Code that directly invokes a client method must narrow QdrantClientLike (for example with isinstance(client, AsyncQdrantClient)) and await the remote branch while offloading the synchronous branch. VectorStoreClient.call is the internal shared dispatcher when operating inside VectorStore.

WebSocket chat messaging was decomposed in task #14827. `src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/_messaging.py` is now a 79-line import-compatible facade for `ChatMessagingMixin`; ingress lives in `_message_ingress.py`, pending inter-session injection in `_pending_messages.py`, interaction responses in `_interaction_responses.py`, streaming orchestration in `_streaming.py`, transport in `_stream_transport.py`, persistence in `_stream_persistence.py`, and event-to-UI frame handling in `_stream_events.py`.

Gobby uuid-column driver asymmetry (post-migration-304/305): Python psycopg3 binds str→uuid transparently (and PostgresAdapter._normalize_value stringifies uuid on reads), but the Rust `postgres` crate (gcode/gwiki) is strict both ways — String/&str binds against uuid columns AND try_get::<_, String> reads from uuid columns fail at runtime with 'cannot convert between the Rust type String and the Postgres type uuid'. Rust uses boundary conversion: domain structs keep String ids, Uuid::parse_str at bind, .to_string() on read (with-uuid-1 feature on the postgres dep). Any new code_*/gwiki_* column or query must follow this. Also: migration tests provision fresh empty schemas and replay all on-disk migrations atop the current baseline, so data-dependent migration failures (uncastable populated rows) are invisible to CI — data-dependent casts need preflight DO guards (see migrations.py module docstring and test_uuid_cast_migrations_ship_a_preflight_guard).

Async DB offloading is path-sensitive in Gobby. Daemon health timeouts on macOS had three independent causes: dial targets using `localhost` could stall while `127.0.0.1` remained responsive; synchronous PostgreSQL calls from SessionMessageProcessor (`UnmodeledObservationStore.record` and `TokenEventStore.record`, plus related session writes) blocked the asyncio event loop under contention; and `/api/admin/health` synchronously read the ghook runtime stamp with `Path.read_text`. Keep daemon dial hosts numeric, pass daemon database work through the bounded `DatabaseExecutor`, and offload health-endpoint filesystem reads with `asyncio.to_thread`. One-shot SIGUSR2 `faulthandler.register` plus an external numeric-loopback probe was effective for identifying the exact Python caller; avoid repeating faulthandler dumps on Python 3.14 because the sampler itself can spin.

Bounded PostgreSQL async work lives in `src/gobby/storage/hub/async_ops.py`. `run_bounded_db` opens a dedicated `psycopg.AsyncConnection` outside the sync pool, reserves `RUN_BOUNDED_DB_CLEANUP_SLICE_SECONDS` (1.0s) inside the caller deadline, cancels once, observes via `asyncio.wait`, hard-closes the main pgconn locally with `finish()`, cancels a second time to interrupt psycopg's separate cancel-connection wait, and reaps the child before returning. Expiry before COMMIT submission raises `BoundedDBTimeoutError` and the socket close guarantees rollback; any failure or cancellation after COMMIT submission but before the outcome is observed raises `IndeterminateCommitError`, including driver `QueryCanceled` and `LockNotAvailable` exceptions. Transaction-local statement and lock timeout values are composed with `psycopg.sql.SQL` and `Literal`. `PostgresHubDatabase.conninfo` exposes the normalized DSN for these consumers. The driver-exception refinement and SQL composition were verified in task #19006 / commit 6d121d19b.

gobby-cli close_task LLM validator gotchas (learned closing #911): (1) It reads the raw commit diff through a ~15.8K-char window in ALPHABETICAL file-path order and TRUNCATES the rest — a file late in the alphabet (e.g. build_parts/curated_content.rs after architecture_diagrams.rs) can be entirely omitted, and the validator then rejects with 'full diff ... not present in the validation evidence'. Fix: for large multi-file commits, INLINE the key code of late-alphabetical files directly in the changes_summary so the validator can verify the criteria without the diff. (2) It demands a confirmed clean validation run on the FINAL COMMITTED TREE — reporting a pass on a 'behaviorally-identical prior tree' is rejected; run the exact validation_criteria command (e.g. cargo nextest run -p gobby-code => 923 passed exit 0) on the committed SHA and state that explicitly. (3) The completion-readiness gate needs a FRESH successful validation command run in the FOREGROUND (background `{...} >> LOG` runs are not auto-recorded as evidence).

## Lesson
- principle: Tests that exercise production entry points must be hermetic with respect to ambient daemon state: process-global caches initialized from the live environment make suite results depend on what happens to be running on the developer's machine and on test scheduling order.
- root_cause: gcore's effective-config OnceLock is process-global and initialized from ambient env/token at first touch; gwiki unit tests call production config entry points (local_index_options, hub_ai_config_source) with no way to force the standalone path, and a validation run that happened to pass (daemon quiescent or cache initialized as Unavailable) recorded 'cargo test -p gobby-wiki passes' as satisfied.
- prevention: Give ambient global caches an explicit kill-switch consulted on every read before the cache (GOBBY_DAEMON_CONFIG_DISABLE in gcore effective_config), set it inside the shared test EnvGuard so guarded tests are standalone by construction, keep exactly one env lock per test process, and recover from mutex poison so one genuine failure cannot cascade. When validating 'suite passes' criteria for code that probes live services, run the suite with the service both up and down.

- title: gwiki test suite depended on live daemon state via gcore's process-global effective-config cache
- message: cargo test -p gobby-wiki failed 14 tests whenever the developer's daemon was running: gcore's EFFECTIVE_CONFIG_STATE OnceLock was initialized from ambient env by whichever test thread first touched it, caching the live daemon's served config; env-guarded gwiki tests then resolved daemon values instead of their temp gcore.yaml, and a bespoke second env lock in support/config.rs tests raced test_env's ENV_TEST_LOCK on GOBBY_HOME while mutex poison cascaded one failure into twelve.

External/natural keys stay TEXT (comms_messages.platform_message_id, sha256 ids, OTel ids, plan slugs).

Autonomous hook progress tracking and AgentLifecycleMonitor stuck detection use separate ProgressTracker instances backed by the same HubDatabase. Cross-component tool lifecycle state must therefore be represented in the persisted loop_progress ledger rather than only in tracker instance memory.

As of task #18540 / commit a93fb4f2c, the web terminal foundation uses @wterm/dom and @wterm/ghostty 0.3.0, deliberately not @wterm/react. web/src/lib/ghosttyCore.ts calls GhosttyCore.load({ wasmPath: '/wasm/ghostty-vt.wasm' }) on every invocation and must never cache/share an instance. Postinstall copies node_modules/@wterm/ghostty/wasm/ghostty-vt.wasm to ignored web/public/wasm/ so Vite carries it to dist/wasm; @wterm modules map to vendor-wterm. npm lifecycle approvals are version-pinned in web/package.json, and the lockfile was refreshed to zero known audit vulnerabilities.

Gobby worktree isolation now captures worktree task base_commit_sha with git merge-base against origin/<base_branch> unless use_local is true, in which case it uses the local base branch. Stale worktree registrations are cleaned through WorktreeGitManager.delete_worktree(force=True, delete_branch=True, branch_name=...) before deleting the storage record so deterministic path recreation can succeed.

Epic #15036 scope clarification from user on 2026-06-16: do not treat AGY as permanently skipped or stubbed during the AGY/Grok fidelity refresh. The goal is to determine whether recent AGY and Grok executable updates now provide parity with other supported providers; if AGY is stable enough for daemon integration, pursue or create the implementation work instead of only documenting a stub row.

Plan semantic lint target coverage is intentionally scoped to owned edit artifacts: acceptance `file:`/`behavior:` refs still require Target inventory, acceptance `test:` refs are evidence and do not require Target entries, body paths count only when the path is preceded by change intent, basename mentions are covered by matching full target paths, and path tokenization requires a non-word/dot/hyphen boundary after known suffixes to avoid symbols like `hashlib.sha256` becoming fake `hashlib.sh` paths.

Task #17264 decomposed `src/gobby/servers/provider_models.py` by extracting live provider discovery mechanics into `src/gobby/servers/provider_model_discovery.py`. `ProviderModelCatalog` remains the public facade and its private methods delegate while passing old-module dependencies such as `shutil.which`, `authorize_model_discovery_trust`, `shutil.rmtree`, and `logger` so existing tests and monkeypatch points under `gobby.servers.provider_models` keep working.

Pipeline heartbeat maintenance uses one stale-task candidate query per tick: PipelineHeartbeat.check_stale_tasks() returns StaleTaskCheckResult(recovered, candidates), and SystemAutomationLoop records both metrics from that single result. The stalled-handled metric counts only execution status transitions; liveness touches return zero.

Settings overlay (epic #16998) pattern for App-owned ui_settings.* preferences: a ui_settings field that is NOT a useSettings field — e.g. ui_settings.selectedProvider, ui_settings.selectedProjectId — is owned and persisted by App.tsx (its own useState + a PUT /api/config/ui-settings effect), NOT by the useSettings hook. To expose such a preference inside a settings section, do NOT call useSettings or useProjects for the selection state in the section. Instead thread a dedicated *Selection context value through SettingsSectionContext, mirroring the providerSelection precedent: define a <Name>SelectionContextValue interface in SettingsSectionContext.ts, add an optional field on SettingsSectionContextValue, create a memoized object in App.tsx bound to App's existing state+setter, and pass it App -> SettingsOverlay -> SettingsSectionProvider -> context. The section consumes it via useSettingsSectionContext() and renders a controlled control (e.g. ProjectSelectField value/onChange), with a graceful fallback when the context value is absent. This keeps a single source of truth shared with the app chrome. Implemented for projectSelection in leaf #17119 (commit 4de10c9cc). Sections owning daemon DaemonConfig dotted-path config still use the per-section draft via SettingsSection's render-prop fields, separate from these live client selections.

Runtime-owned workflow variables are centralized in src/gobby/workflows/reserved_variables.py. Agent/pre-tool and gobby-workflows.set_variable writes use is_reserved_workflow_variable; user-authored rule effects are also blocked. Installed global rules tagged gobby (and not user) are the explicit trusted path because bundled progressive-discovery rules legitimately update unlocked_tools, listed_servers, and servers_listed.

As of task #19294 / commit 2140f54fd, `pre-push-test.sh` writes `reports/pre-push-<timestamp>.json` through `pre-push-manifest.py`. The manifest snapshots starting HEAD plus a Git index/dirty/untracked worktree fingerprint (excluding reports), records every gating and informational command outcome, rechecks integrity after each command, and becomes terminal `invalidated` if HEAD or source state drifts. Pytest still uses isolated HOME/GOBBY_HOME/config/hooks/log paths; before isolation, pre-push resolves the managed FalkorDB host, port, and password and exports all three so the memory-dream E2E does not depend on the isolated home directory.

As of task #16755, GitHub and Linear issue import reconciliation compares the tracker record's update timestamp with the local task updated_at before applying existing-task metadata or lifecycle changes. GitHub imports additionally update only changed fields, retain all existing local labels, union non-empty remote labels in stable order, and never interpret an unlabeled issue as a request to clear local labels.

Gobby build is intended to run unattended without an agent coordinator. When using a coordinator for a build epic, the coordinator should identify and fix any gobby build bugs that prevent unattended operation; blocking bugs are fixed immediately, non-blocking bugs opportunistically, and all discovered build bugs should be fixed before the target epic is closed.

In Gobby, live web-chat P2P wakeups route through WakeDispatcher when session_type='web_chat'. WakeDispatcher delegates to WebChatSessionRegistry.wake_session(), which drains a hidden web-chat turn so pending inter-session mailbox context is injected. If a web-chat turn is active, wake requests are coalesced and queued behind any queued compaction so compaction runs first, then the hidden wake turn.

Compact handoff timeout decision revised 2026-07-27: use a hard 300-second daemon-side digest-readiness budget. Keep compact_self heartbeat-enabled without an MCP-wrapper deadline so wrapper and application deadlines cannot race. If readiness exceeds 300 seconds, treat it as a synthesis/provider defect, return a precise failure, and do not send /compact or /compress. Add elapsed-time and phase logging. The prior planned 900-second readiness timeout is rejected.

Gobby daemon LLM routes expose GET /api/llm/status from AICapabilityRegistry.status_snapshot() and POST /api/llm/generate through the text_generate capability registry. Generate accepts prompt/provider/system_prompt/model/max_tokens/cwd and returns text, capability, provider, and model; include usage only when TextGenerationService.generate_result() provides it. Vision remains under /api/llm/vision/status and /api/llm/vision/extract.

Recall-signal logging is default-off and fail-open. It writes append-only JSONL search-debug events, preserving search ordering and ranking behavior. Current schema v4 includes session/caller join metadata, a per-run recall_request_id for eligible memory recalls, exact UTF-8 Memory.content hashes on recall hits, and ranking-regime provenance in recall_signal_requests. Legacy digest-labeled rows are retained as read-only evidence while newer audit, prompt-snapshot, judge-state, gate-run, and holdout-consumption data are stored durably.

Use lazy percent-style logging templates rather than f-strings or eagerly rendered messages. Preserve log level, rendered-message semantics, interpolation order, and exception keywords. For percentage formatting that must retain Python rounding semantics, pass `format(value, '.0%')` as a `%s` argument rather than treating `%` as a logging interpolation specifier.

FilesPage diff UI state is selection-scoped using the active project/path key, and asynchronous diff results are accepted only when their request ID still matches. Preserve both guards when changing file-tab or diff behavior.

Task #18735 (commit 5e0bc78b5) defines epic-QA lesson minting at fix confirmation on re-review. A complete Epic Findings entry requires a catalog-consulted validated check_key, explicit lesson_classes, principle or root_cause, prevention, leaf task plus file anchor, confirmed-fix evidence, and stable fingerprint; incomplete entries mint nothing. Each proven class records independently under source_kind qa_rejection and code domain: qa-miss uses pattern epic-qa:qa-miss:<check-key> with checklist guardrail, validation-miss uses epic-qa:validation-miss:<check-key> with validation guardrail. Class-specific fingerprints keep occurrence streams separate; cited paths create path tags. QA reviewers must apply push-injected qa-miss lessons as their mandatory first-pass checklist at review start.

WorkflowsPage tab architecture: All 3 tabs (Pipelines, Agents, Rules) are now extracted into consistent tab components: PipelinesTab.tsx, AgentsTab.tsx, RulesTab.tsx. WorkflowsPage.tsx is a thin shell (~170 lines) with toolbar, TabBar, and tab routing. YamlEditorModal is exported from WorkflowsPage and shared by all tabs. Each tab receives searchText, sourceFilter, devMode, refreshKey props. Create buttons stay in the toolbar; create UI (forms/modals/dropdowns) renders inside each tab via showCreate* props.

Expansion compiler behavior: deliverable-only Plan-Coverage Contract plans validate via validate_plan_file but must not fall back to LLM expansion. _parse_contract_plan synthesizes a missing M1 Task Manifest with emit_stub_manifest before compiling deterministically, so plans lacking an authored manifest still compile into phases and leaves correctly.

Linear sync priority semantics: Gobby priorities are 0=critical, 1=high, 2=medium, 3=low, 4=backlog; Linear priorities are 0=no priority, 1=urgent, 2=high, 3=medium, 4=low. src/gobby/sync/linear_task_ops.py uses explicit tables in both directions. Unsupported Gobby values map to Linear no priority (0); missing or unsupported Linear values map to Gobby backlog (4).

Daemon pipeline lifecycle maintenance is independent of startup CWD. PipelineHeartbeat uses LocalPipelineExecutionManager(project_id=None), startup restart recovery enumerates every project with RUNNING/INTERRUPTED executions, and periodic approval-timeout expiry creates its own unscoped manager even when runner.project_id is None. Unscoped storage predicates must use an always-true project clause; project_id None means all projects. CronExecutor resolves pipeline executors through services.get_pipeline_executor(job.project_id) and carries that resolved executor through background execution and failure recording; its constructor-provided executor remains the standalone/test fallback.

Memory dream planner prompt policy as of task #18623 / commit 2909cb725: `DreamCandidate.to_prompt_dict()` preserves candidate content in full and conditionally emits `related_newer_memories` from immutable `RelatedMemoryEvidence` records with JSON-safe ISO timestamps. `MemoryDreamConfig.planner_batch_max_chars` defaults to 100,000. Planner pages whose stable rendered candidate JSON exceeds that soft limit split recursively in half; an irreducible single candidate is logged with its ID and rendered size, then dispatched exactly once intact. Prompt content is never truncated or skipped.

Web chat input state can trigger broad message-list rerenders. Keep expensive message and tool-result rendering memoized, and memoize costly parsing or derived output, because composer state may be owned above the message list. Re-check memo boundaries whenever ChatInput or message-rendering components are refactored.

In Gobby startup, `runner.websocket_server` is constructed during `init_servers`, but the communications adapters are not active until `runner.communications_manager.start()` runs in `_start_core_services`. Websocket broadcast wiring for `gobby_chat` therefore belongs after communications manager startup, using `runner.communications_manager.set_websocket_broadcast(runner.websocket_server.broadcast)`.

subscribe_agent_completion returns AgentCompletionSubscription for exactly the requested subscriber_session_id; it has no SessionManager dependency and performs no lineage expansion as of task #18928 / commit f2e7feb27. Multiple intentional subscribers are added through repeated calls and the completion registry/storage merge semantics deduplicate them. strict=True persists before registry registration and translates persistence failures to SubscriptionPersistenceError without adding live subscribers; default mode preserves register-first, best-effort persistence. The result tracks whether the registry entry was freshly created and the exact durable session rows inserted by that call. Bulk inserts use one ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING statement, and durable cleanup can filter by session_ids.

Droid CLI 0.174.0 live command-result contract: `droid exec --output-format stream-json` emits `tool_result.isError` as a boolean for both successful and failed `Execute` commands (`false` for exit 0, `true` for exit 7). The terminal hook path emitted `PostToolUse` for the successful command but emitted neither `PostToolUse` nor `PostToolUseFailure` for the nonzero command. Gobby therefore uses stream `isError` as the definitive managed-chat outcome, treats terminal `PostToolUse` as definitive success, and preserves unknown when a failure hook is absent, a stream flag is missing/non-boolean, or only human-readable text is available. Managed lifecycle payloads omit `is_error` for those ambiguous stream results. Captured fixture: tests/fixtures/provider_contracts/droid/command-outcomes-0.174.0.json. Implemented by #18380 in commits e8417351f and 2ae9746d0.

pytest coverage (--cov=gobby) was removed from pyproject.toml addopts to avoid 10-30% overhead on every local test run. Coverage is now only enabled explicitly in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and pre-push-test.sh. To run locally with coverage: uv run pytest tests/path/ --cov=gobby --cov-report=term-missing

Task #15072 fixed de-escalation stage-attempt reset behavior: de_escalate_task(reset_stage_attempts=True) now prefers the stage named by work-attempt escalation reasons like '<stage>_work_failed:max' and '<stage>_max_work_attempts' before falling back to the current stage. This prevents holistic_qa attempt caps from staying stale after holistic QA rewinds an epic to development.

Josh's feedback (2026-07-16): when he asks a question — even inline with other feedback or directives — the answer is the turn's primary deliverable. Lead with the full answer as standalone text before plan edits, tool work, or ExitPlanMode. In a plan-mode session, answers to 'see if you agree' and 'why is TTS part of this conversation?' were buried under plan-file edits and immediate ExitPlanMode calls; he had to interrupt twice and then asked 'why does Fable ignore me when I ask questions?'. The plan-mode end-with-ExitPlanMode rule does not license compressing or deferring answers — defer the approval dialog instead.

ClaudeSDKClient integration pattern for in-process agents: chat_session_helpers.py is in src/gobby/servers/ (not websocket/). Key functions: _find_cli_path(), _find_mcp_config(), _response_to_prompt_output(), _response_to_pre_tool_output(), _response_to_post_tool_output(), _response_to_stop_output(). SDK types for isinstance checks: ResultMessage, AssistantMessage, TextBlock, StreamEvent. When testing SDK integration, use real SDK types (from claude_agent_sdk import ResultMessage etc.) not fake dataclasses — isinstance checks in the runner won't match fakes. Factory helpers: ResultMessage(subtype='result', duration_ms=100, duration_api_ms=80, is_error=False, num_turns=1, session_id=..., result=...), TextBlock(text), AssistantMessage(content=[...], model='test-model'), StreamEvent(uuid=..., session_id=..., event={...}).

Josh's /gobby plan and agent-review workflow is interactive by default: do not launch enhancement or adversarial review passes until he has reviewed and explicitly approved the current plan, unless he says "run unattended." Present every enhancement/adversary/review item's full verbatim output alongside ranked summaries, let Josh vote on each item individually, and record deferred declines in linked follow-up sections. Stop for explicit go-ahead after drafting/validation, after enhancement votes are applied, and before every adversarial round.
For Gobby local model planning, user wants vLLM considered as a managed-server alternative to LM Studio/Ollama for OpenAI-compatible local model serving, not as part of Qwen voice specifically.

Verified in task #18931: bundled merge workflows must model durable result persistence separately from cleanup readiness. `record_merge_result` success sets `merge_result_recorded`; failure results may also set the readiness flag, while transport errors must never count as a durable result. Termination is gated on both flags, so a later linked-issue close failure can terminate only after the merge outcome was persisted. Generic Git command failures such as checkout/fetch authentication or local-change errors remain `FailureCategory.CODE`; only concrete environment evidence such as `not a git repository`, worktree setup/not-found, missing executables/files, or connection failures maps to `ENVIRONMENT`.

Task #14312 implementation detail: `task_stages_registry.reviewer_agent_selector_json` stores a canonical nullable selector JSON loaded from `reviewer_agent_selector` YAML. Stage manifests snapshot the resolved reviewer into `task_stage_states.reviewer_agent` at initialization/add-stage time using precedence: existing stage row reviewer, fixed registry reviewer, first matching category rule, first matching task_type rule, selector default, then no reviewer. Bundled development uses docs -> `doc-reviewer`, default -> `qa-reviewer`; existing manifests are intentionally non-retroactive.

Task #18729 (commit 8570764f9) added project-scoped deterministic review-lesson class recall. ReviewLessonClassRecall validates lesson domains and source-kind/domain consistency, executes OR lists through AND-tagged paginated queries, excludes globals, dedupes by pattern before the cap, and ranks by distinct occurrence count descending, newest created_at, then memory ID. list_check_keys scans all pages and returns sorted distinct check-key tags without depending on possibly hashed pattern tags. Workflow effects route class recall through the existing lesson-injection dedupe formatter with the scope label "matched lesson class".

Circular import pitfall when re-exporting from __init__.py: In gobby, `prompts/__init__.py` re-exporting `sync_bundled_prompts` from `prompts/sync.py` caused a circular import because `sync.py` imports from `storage/prompts.py`, which imports from `prompts/models.py` (triggering `prompts/__init__.py`). Fix: don't re-export from __init__.py; callers import directly from `prompts.sync`. General rule: avoid re-exporting from __init__.py when the submodule has cross-package dependencies.

PostgreSQL migration advisory locks must be scoped by current_schema(), not database-global: pytest-xdist uses one isolated schema per worker, and a global lock can deadlock against each worker's open schema DDL transaction when a non-transactional migration runs. The local managed PostgreSQL instance also cannot safely handle unbounded xdist auto workers dropping large schemas concurrently; cap auto workers at 8 and serialize final DROP SCHEMA operations with a dedicated advisory lock.

When fixing pytest report failures in gobby, use the combined focused pytest command over the reported nodes after individual fixes; some Postgres-backed storage parity cases can run only in the larger focused context and skip when isolated. The memory keyword BM25 backend now tie-breaks memories by created_at then id for equal scores.

_dispatch_mcp_calls (hook_manager.py) and dispatch_mcp_calls (mcp_dispatch.py) must NOT inject extra parameters into MCP call arguments. ToolProxyService.call_tool() validates arguments against tool schemas and rejects unknown parameters, causing silent failures. The return value was also being discarded, hiding the validation errors. Fixed in commit 54b9a8f3 by removing prompt_text injection and adding result logging (warnings on success=False).

## Lesson
- principle: Do not delete discovery rows for orphaned external projections until all configured projection cleanup paths have completed without skip or failure.
- root_cause: The prune loop used a boolean cleanup result that stayed true when graph or vector cleanup was skipped because the corresponding service was unavailable, allowing SQL orphan rows to be deleted and preventing later rediscovery.
- prevention: Track skipped projection stores separately from failed stores and gate SQL deletion on confirmed non-skipped cleanup.

Workflow post-tool routing uses the hook layer's canonical tool_outcome after normalize_tool_fields. Route failures to on_mcp_error, including when legacy is_error=True or provider metadata.is_failure indicates failure; direct, nested, and JSON-string MCP results share this classification path.

Process preference from Josh (observed 2026-07-16, epic #12010 refresh): he cross-reviews plans with Codex and pastes its feedback into plan-approval rejections, often over multiple rounds (expect 2-3 before approval on substantial plans). How to handle: treat each rejection-with-feedback as a revision round, not a restart; VERIFY every load-bearing code claim in Codex's feedback against the tree before adopting it (Codex corrected two of my exploration errors that day — Rust crates do use the log crate with stderr loggers, and the gcode gateway forces --quiet — but its pasted text also contained mangled words/typos that must be cleaned, never propagated into task text); state which claims were verified when presenting the merged plan.

Direct Codex, Claude, Qwen, Droid, Grok, and AGY MCP calls rely on provider-native PostToolUse for AFTER_TOOL. The MCP proxy synthesizes AFTER_TOOL only for PIPELINE and UNKNOWN sources; direct BEFORE_TOOL enforcement remains synchronous for every source. Transcript-derived Codex receipts are evidence only, not generic lifecycle events.

Rust gcore secrets (crates/gcore in the gobby monorepo) decrypt the shared Python SecretStore envelope directly: secret_key_material.default holds wrapped_dek + KEK posture metadata; Rust supports key_file via GOBBY_HOME/.secret_kek (default ~/.gobby/.secret_kek) and scrypt_passphrase via GOBBY_SECRET_KEK_PASSPHRASE, then decrypts secrets.encrypted_value with the unwrapped Fernet DEK. Implemented pre-merge in gobby-cli commit dfe52456 for task #17445; parent docs contract clarified in gobby commit 92ef452fe.

Global dispatcher agent-cap admission must use HubDatabase.advisory_lock(AgentCapAdmission(project_id=None)) across count-through-agent_run visibility. PostgresHubDatabase.advisory_lock uses a dedicated non-pooled psycopg connection with the same UTC-normalized conninfo, PGAPPNAME, prepare_threshold=None, and dict_row session options as the typed-config worker pool. It acquires session-scoped pg_try_advisory_lock with explicit commits and shields unlock plus close before propagating cancellation, preventing max-size-one worker-pool self-starvation. Pool sizing comes from injected bootstrap PostgresPoolConfig, not PGPOOL_* environment variables.

Direct MCP after-tool processing in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/result_handling.py::apply_after_tool_workflow builds an after_tool event and calls WorkflowHookHandler.evaluate directly. It bypasses HookManager.handle and ToolEventHandlerMixin.handle_after_tool, so side effects added only to handle_after_tool do not run for direct proxied MCP calls.

For the embedded Lua 5.4 policy boundary scenario, the intended design is: validate and deep-copy untrusted request tables; return an explicit local module table; create metatable-backed policy/stream objects with protected metatables and private state; expose only two injected host callbacks in a restricted text-only environment; translate coroutine.resume into an explicit tagged decision/done protocol only after checking its leading boolean; and close streams with coroutine.close on errors, invalid yields, abandonment, and host shutdown. Native full-userdata resources use idempotent __close plus __gc backstop, registry refs are always unreferenced, and the C harness must assert stack balance and exact result counts.

The gobby-sessions send_keys MCP tool authorizes targets before tmux access: it permits the caller's own session, any session with the same project_id, or sessions connected in either direction by SessionManager.is_ancestor(). Cross-project targets outside that lineage return error_code send_keys_target_forbidden. Target #N resolution is scoped to the caller's project.

In Gobby's 320px chat-column layout with the activity panel open, use an 8px inline-end gutter on chat command/status/input bars because the 4px resize handle makes the visible gap to the activity panel 12px, matching Activity panel Filter/Swap buttons. Avoid Tailwind px-* utilities for SegmentedControl option padding when container-query CSS must override it; use semantic classes such as segmented-control__option--sm/md so responsive CSS owns the padding.

The current settings surfaces for legacy ConfigurationPage prompt/variable correctness are PromptsTemplatesSection and WorkflowVariablesEditor. Prompt async operations use a monotonic request ID so out-of-order detail loads and stale save/revert completions cannot replace newer editor state; thrown or false-result operations surface role=alert messages. Workflow variable fetch now returns a success boolean so the editor can distinguish API failure from an empty list, and create/toggle/delete sentinel failures are user-visible. Covered by task #16665 / commit 0ec7a307a.

Gemini CLI/runtime support is retired in Gobby, while Qwen remains a supported terminal-hook and ACP web-chat provider. Do not restore Gemini CLI spawn, sandbox, trust, command-building, or web-chat runtime support; assess Qwen behavior through its own supported paths.

Gobby 0.5.0 feature LLM routing is profile/candidate based. Feature configs use `profile` plus ordered provider-scoped candidates such as `codex/gpt-5.6-sol`, `endpoint:lm-studio/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct`, and `claude/haiku`. Legacy `provider`/`model`/`tier` inputs are no longer migrated: FeatureDefaultConfig forbids those extras and raises Pydantic extra-forbid errors instead (task #15762). Built-in profile defaults avoid generation-endpoint candidates; configurable `ai.generation.profile_defaults` can opt named endpoints into profiles. As of task #18903 / commit 1dc56d24e, the built-in chains are LOW `claude/haiku` → `codex/gpt-5.6-luna`, MID `codex/gpt-5.6-terra` → `claude/sonnet`, and HIGH `codex/gpt-5.6-sol@xhigh` → `claude/opus@high`; the Codex static catalog exposes Sol, Terra, and Luna. Task #18630 / commit deb775a9e aligned every Rust workspace model fixture and gcode's feature_high documentation with `gpt-5.6-sol`; no `gpt-5.5` literal remains under `crates/`. Task #18632 / commit 42b09cdfb aligned user guides, the chat activity fixture, and provider-catalog test data with the earlier profile generation. Generation endpoints live under `ai.generation.endpoints`, use `endpoint:<name>[/<model>]` selectors, and explicitly declare `wire_api`; old `ai.generation.local.*` and `local:*` generation selectors are rejected after task #18804. The old `llm_providers` config module and DaemonConfig field have been removed; Codex/Gemini/Grok/Qwen/Droid/Claude model state comes from provider discovery/static catalogs and feature candidates. Embeddings remain separate under `ai.embeddings`/runtime embedding config and retain their own local provider selectors independently of generation endpoints.

In gwiki/gcode, attached PostgreSQL resolution uses direct environment, bootstrap, and gcore configuration rather than the retired local daemon database-url broker. Non-standalone `gwiki setup` creates gwiki-owned `gwiki_*` derived tables and indexes while only preflighting the externally managed `pg_search` extension. Include `code/**` in gwiki BM25 path filters, and ignore wikilinks inside Markdown code spans and fences during link extraction.

Spawn boundary drift checklist: when spawned-agent activation behaves unexpectedly, compare agent_run_id, parent_session_id, task_id, isolation context, provider/model, initial_variables, prepare_terminal_spawn run id, runtime update fields, and completion waiter references for mismatches.

Commit afd17971d (#15066) tightened the QA reviewer spawn prompt and bundled qa-reviewer.yaml contract after live #12746 logs showed QA reviewers trying disallowed claim_task/get_workflow_status/full-pytest actions while already in load_skills/review.
