Gobby already has DB-managed prompts, agent definitions with role/personality/instructions, apply_persona, rules-based inject_context, and project-scoped memory. If adopting the idea, implement it as a UI/import/export affordance over existing agent/persona definitions with strict size/security controls, not as an unsandboxed mutable Markdown authority file.

For terminal-context helpers that storage code needs, prefer the pure module `gobby.terminal_context` over `gobby.sessions.tmux_context`; importing `gobby.sessions.*` from storage can cycle through `gobby.sessions.__init__` back into `gobby.storage.sessions`.

Gobby CLI service-managed restart now uses `SERVICE_MANAGED_STOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 75.0` in `src/gobby/cli/daemon.py`, matching launchd `ExitTimeOut=60` plus buffer. `_wait_for_service_stop` treats stop completion as previous PID exited, service no longer running, and daemon health endpoint no longer healthy before `gobby restart` invokes start. Implemented in task #14710 commit 3f7693596c952c8fbe482cd2205fe8838b3603fc.

Cross-project handoff contamination fix for tasks #16179/#17049 landed in commit 124e7e361: inject_context output is fenced with <!-- gobby:injected-context:* --> sentinels, digest/summary/handoff readers strip sentinel and legacy '*Injected by Gobby ...*' blocks, legacy stripping now stops before blank-line ATX headings and ### Turn digest headings, get_handoff_context uses project-scoped find_parent and fails closed without caller project context, explicit session_id lookups must be status=handoff_ready, and recovery with project_id=None searches all projects but returns None on cross-project external_id ambiguity.

User feedback (session #5122, Tasks board mobile work): when a request contains an exploratory phrase like "figure out a better way to display it", scope STRICTLY to the literal ask and keep the diff surgical. Concretely here: the ask was only "make the kanban/Board desktop-only (>=768px) and fall back on mobile" — I over-interpreted it, added an unrequested mobile stage-chip bar to the List (non-jira) view, plus unrelated refactors (TasksTabModel/TasksBoardView dedup, TasksTabDetailSection extraction), and steered the user into it via a "Recommended" AskUserQuestion option. User reacted strongly ("looks like garbage", "I didn't ask for the stage chips", "you made changes to the non-jira view in mobile that I didn't request") and it cost a full revert (#14787).

**Why:** an exploratory phrase is an invitation to think, not license to expand scope onto surfaces the user didn't name; a 'Recommended' option in AskUserQuestion can rail-road a user into scope creep they later reject.

**How to apply:** Implement the minimal literal interpretation first; do not modify adjacent/untouched surfaces or bundle drive-by refactors into a feature fix. If additive UI seems valuable, ship the minimal version and let the user pull for more, or ask plainly/neutrally (no 'Recommended' steering) BEFORE building. Prefer the smallest diff that satisfies the exact words. Related: [[a297c0c5-3dca-58a7-8d05-e15bb56be8b0]], [[84c71ffc-4e44-5aba-bcb0-5649a29c50f8]].

Enforcement block auditing is centralized in src/gobby/workflows/block_audit.py. RuleEngine owns one audit row per BlockGate plus a synthetic row when the final block cause is absent from the gates. Proxy and hook layers audit only block causes created outside RuleEngine, preventing duplicate rows. Synchronous WorkflowAuditManager storage is invoked through asyncio.to_thread and audit failures are warning-only.

In dev-parity-plus/gobby-core, libpq keyword DSN tokenization is centralized in `crates/gcore/src/libpq.rs` as `pub(crate) fn split_keyword_dsn_tokens`; both degradation redaction and postgres sslmode parsing call this always-compiled internal helper.

Gobby workflow_definitions.tags is JSON data; runtime hub storage is PostgreSQL, where exact tag membership should use gobby.storage.sql_dialect.json_array_contains_condition(db, "tags", tag) so PostgreSQL emits JSONB @> with a bound JSON array. Avoid tags LIKE queries against workflow_definitions.tags; they fail on Postgres JSONB. SQLite handling is only relevant for retired/import/test compatibility paths.

Task JSONL import sequence convention: `TaskSyncManager.import_from_jsonl` treats `seq_num` and `path_cache` as machine-local metadata for existing tasks, so LWW UPDATE retains the database values even when newer JSONL provides different values. Only INSERT attempts to preserve an unoccupied JSONL `seq_num` and rebuilds `path_cache` from the final local sequence.

After daemon restart or deployment changes, use context-aware MCP discovery before calling tools: call leased known tools directly; fetch a schema for known unleased tools; list tools for unknown tool names; list servers only for unknown-server or registry inspection. PostgreSQL-backed inventory survives restart, while context reset clears schema leases.

Install button UX pattern for Pipelines/Rules/Agents tabs: derive an `installedNames` Set from the full data array (not filtered), checking source==='installed' && !deleted_at. Then in template cards, use a ternary: installedNames.has(name) renders a disabled 'Installed' button, otherwise the clickable 'Install' button. For RulesTab, pass isInstalled as a prop to the RuleCard component since it's a separate function.

For live Gobby web-chat validation, the Web UI dev server is http://localhost:60889 but the daemon chat websocket is ws://localhost:60887/ws. In current Codex web-chat runtime, explicit brave-search/brave_web_search MCP calls complete with browser-visible chat_stream frames and unlocked_tools tracking, while a separate network-restricted fallback path can surface a Bash pending-approval tool_status instead of an MCP approval frame.

Task and worktree lifecycle are intentionally decoupled: task close/reopen no longer changes linked worktree status. Worktree status changes require explicit worktree lifecycle tools. Merged status is git-backed: mark_worktree_merged and merge_worktree only persist merged metadata when git ancestry shows the worktree source branch is merged into the target/base branch, and get_worktree/get_worktree_by_task report stale stored merged metadata as active with git_merge_state details when ancestry is false.

Task #17382 split Gobby's shared ACP adapter boundaries: src/gobby/adapters/acp_client.py now keeps subprocess/JSON-RPC orchestration and re-exports StreamEvent, while src/gobby/adapters/acp_session_state.py owns session IDs, session info, agent capabilities, default client capabilities, and root URI tracking, and src/gobby/adapters/acp_stream.py owns StreamEvent plus default ACP notification/text normalization. Commit 955e85a68; focused ACP lifecycle and contract fixture tests, ruff, mypy, and test-quality audit passed.

Gobby #15236 fixed Codex web-chat context pie/session split by passing terminal_context.gobby_session_id from CodexWebChatBackend through CodexAppServerClient.start_thread into early thread/started notifications, reusing existing web_chat rows by external_id in SESSION_START, and persisting transcript token_count usage from both live SessionMessageProcessor and lifecycle backfill into token_events plus session usage. Codex session usage for the pie uses latest last_token_usage total input plus model_context_window while token_events keep uncached/cache split for accounting.

Cron durable dispatch design: user pipeline and agent_spawn cron runs should finish as status `dispatched` after durable child work is created/launched and linked via `pipeline_execution_id` or `agent_run_id`. Cron-owned scheduler slots are only `pending`/`running`; dispatched child overlap is enforced via active child statuses (pipeline: pending/running/waiting_approval/interrupted; agent: ACTIVE_AGENT_RUN_STATUSES). `skipped` is neutral and resets cron failure backoff; only `failed` increments consecutive_failures.

For CodeRabbit test-only typing cleanup, DB-backed pytest modules should carry a module-level `pytest.mark.integration`, fixture parameters should use their concrete repository protocols/registry types, and injected factories should be captured and asserted behaviorally. Validate with focused pytest plus both `gobby test-types audit --baseline ... --fail-on-new` and `gobby test-quality audit --baseline ... --fail-on-new`; test-types may still report known baseline errors while passing when `New errors: 0`.

Documentation and workflow guidance should remain provider-agnostic across supported providers. Avoid framing behavior as Claude-default when it also applies to supported alternatives; exclude Gemini CLI from provider matrices and parity guidance.

web/src/components/command-browser/ToolArgumentForm.tsx is shared by both ToolBrowserModal and activity/mcp/McpDetailPanel. JSON object/array fields keep raw local text while typing, emit parsed values only when valid, format on blur, and report aggregate validity through onValidityChange; both call surfaces disable execution while invalid.

ProviderPicker keeps each catalog group’s provider/display name for rendering. Button callbacks use a nonblank `execution_provider` when present and retain the model’s exact selector. Active ownership is the catalog entry whose execution provider matches `currentProvider` and whose model value exactly matches `currentModel`; this keeps endpoint-backed selections distinct from native Codex and other endpoints. Confirmation compares execution providers, so Codex-to-endpoint changes remain in the current conversation while Claude-to-endpoint changes require provider-switch confirmation.

Use the build-coordinator skill only for explicit or directly required build coordination. A coordinator monitors dispatch and build state, investigates and fixes actionable build-system issues under the coordination epic, compacts when context is stale or high, and uses `wait_for_agent(timeout_seconds=300)` only as the final idle action when no actionable work remains.

AGY text generation uses canonical base model IDs in `AGY_MODELS`, with effort and display resolution in `gobby.ai._agy_models`. For AGY Claude Sonnet/Opus, the thinking display variants are keyed by standard effort `high`: `high`, `auto`, or `None` resolve to the thinking display, while `low`, `medium`, and internal `thinking` reject. The effort gate resolves only when `request.model` is set, keeping it aligned with adapter display composition.

Review-learning retirement is an explicit project-scoped operation: resolve the caller session/project, derive the canonical pattern key from the injected pattern_id, and retag every matching review-lesson memory from confirmed to stale while holding ReviewLearningPatternMutation. Return affected memory IDs plus open Guardrail: task refs; task state remains caller-owned. Both deterministic recall paths query the confirmed tag, so retired lessons disappear immediately.

In gobby-cli/dev-parity-plus task #619, gcode no longer implements gcore ConfigSource directly for PostgresConfigSource/FallbackConfigSource because that path swallowed config_store read errors as missing AI/embedding config. Production embedding config, embeddings doctor details, and indexing settings now route service-backed reads through ErrorCapturingConfigSource over ServiceConfigSource so the first database read error is returned with key context instead of silently degrading to BM25-only/default config. Regression test: config::tests::embedding_config_source_errors_are_propagated.

Gwiki uses a 30-second interactive subprocess guard and a 270-second generation guard. wiki_compile always uses the generation guard. For wiki_ask, generation is requested exactly when llm or deep is true; ai and require_ai only choose or constrain a requested generation lane and must be rejected otherwise. Generation-backed MCP calls use the 300-second extended wrapper budget, and the 270-second gwiki guard must remain below that transport bound. Scheduled jobs use their own larger timeouts.

Task #13658 changed Gobby voice TTS chunking: VoiceConfig now has `voice.tts_clause_max_chars` default 180 (bounds 80..400), Chatterbox generation cap defaults to 1000, SentenceBuffer.flush() returns ordered `list[str]`, TTSPipeline enqueues every flushed chunk with the configured max, and web useVoice queue overflow drops the incoming audio chunk with transient error `Audio dropped — connection too slow`.

Task #16680 added GET /api/chat/attachments/limits as the frontend-facing source of the effective chat attachment max-file limit. The route uses resolve_chat_attachment_limits, so DB config_store overrides and daemon defaults match upload enforcement. web/src/lib/chatAttachments.ts preflights each upload against that live value and formats 1024-based sizes with IEC KiB/MiB/GiB labels. Commit 0288d1adc.

Codex compaction emits a reset-shaped `token_count` where all detailed `last_token_usage` counters are zero while positive `last_token_usage.total_tokens` reports current post-compaction context occupancy. Gobby stores that value in normalized context-usage snapshot fields and never adds it to cumulative input/output/cache accounting; later ordinary usage replaces the occupancy snapshot.

In useSessionDetail, an in-flight older-page fetch remains valid across live tail appends. prependOlderTranscriptPage merges the response into the current transcript window with ID deduplication, so loadMore uses session identity and detail-load version as stale boundaries while tail appends commute with the prepend.

Pipeline templates synced via reload_cache have source='template' in workflow_definitions DB. The loader's get_by_name excludes source='template' by default. To make a pipeline runnable, use create_pipeline with the YAML content to create an 'installed' copy (source='installed'). Just enabling a template record is insufficient.

gcode uses gcore RuntimeMode and daemon-served effective configuration in daemon mode. Environment values take precedence; daemon DSN resolution is environment > daemon-served > bootstrap and excludes gcore.yaml. Standalone mode uses environment > bootstrap > gcore.yaml. Operational AI source construction uses gcore ai_source_for_conn or ai_source_without_primary, and effective-config transport or non-2xx failures are hard errors.

Codex item normalization now lives in src/gobby/adapters/codex_impl/item_normalization.py as pure shared helpers (constants plus payload extraction, tool-item detection, lifecycle payload building, and MCP argument parsing). Future Codex adapter and web-chat changes should reuse this module instead of duplicating item/* parsing logic.

In gobby-wiki, individual raw source notes under `raw/src-*.md` are not part of the normal search surface; `indexer::document_kind` and BM25 filters search `raw/INDEX.md`, `knowledge/sources/*.md`, `knowledge/concepts/*.md`, `knowledge/topics/*.md`, and `code/*.md`. Ingest modalities that need searchable source content should write a derived note with `paths::derived_markdown_path(record)` under `knowledge/sources/{source_id}.md` while keeping immutable raw provenance under `raw/`.

Code-index BM25 recovery contract: Gobby verifies only public.code_symbols_search_bm25 and public.code_content_search_bm25 with pdb.verify_index. Startup and `gobby postgres repair-code-index` use a PostgreSQL advisory lock, run schema-qualified REINDEX INDEX only for indexes classified damaged, and reverify before success. Missing indexes require setup/migrations. If startup recovery fails, the daemon stays up but marks code_index_bm25 degraded and does not start code-index maintenance/sync workers. gcode BM25 query/count errors must propagate with the PostgreSQL message and repair guidance rather than returning empty results or zero.

LazyBool in src/gobby/workflows/safe_evaluator.py has boolean value semantics as of task #18312: equality evaluates and caches each LazyBool thunk, while hashing delegates to the cached bool hash. This preserves the equality/hash contract and makes list and set membership behave like the underlying boolean.

PostgreSQL support did not go public while the bundled Docker image moved from PostgreSQL 17 to PostgreSQL 18; that upgrade was local/internal only, so docs should not imply a public 17-to-18 upgrade path.

In gobby-cli codewiki, per-symbol prose at non-symbols --ai-depth is NOT plain structural text: structural_symbol_purpose (crates/gcode/src/commands/codewiki/text.rs) prefers symbol.summary from the PostgreSQL hub, which the Gobby daemon's enrichment populates with AI-generated summaries. So sections/files-depth runs get AI-quality, citation-grounded symbol purposes for free from the index, with no codewiki-time LLM calls. Fallback order: summary -> docstring -> 'Indexed {kind} {name} in {file}'.

In Gobby's web WikiTab, wiki/source hrefs are intentionally rendered only when they parse as absolute http:// or https:// URLs. Relative paths and other schemes are filtered out rather than shown as anchors; tests should use HTTPS fixtures for positive link assertions and separate invalid entries for filtering coverage.

Web-chat plans should use text artifacts so they render as markdown. ArtifactPanel owns editing and source/preview state and renders the header controls; ArtifactCodeView and ArtifactTextView receive state as props. Plan approval UI is supplied through ArtifactPanel approval props.

FilesPage file state intentionally separates terminal read/load errors (`OpenFile.error`) from recoverable write errors (`OpenFile.saveError`). A write failure must preserve `editing`, `dirty`, and `editContent`; the UI shows a dismissible inline alert while retaining Save/Cancel so the same draft can be retried.

Spawned tmux agents should not inherit a missing or unwritable uv cache. As of task #14352, TmuxSpawner sets UV_CACHE_DIR to a per-session directory under tempfile.gettempdir()/gobby/uv-cache/<sanitized GOBBY_SESSION_ID> unless UV_CACHE_DIR is explicitly provided.

Plan review parallel research is owned by provider-native internal subagents inside plan-adversary and plan-adversary-taskless; the parent remains the sole evidence/finding/manifest/coverage/verdict owner. Both definitions have a 2700-second top-level agent timeout enforced by the agent lifecycle. Native lane 15-minute deadlines are best-effort and are not Gobby-enforced. A terminal timeout is `inconclusive/timeout` with no partial reuse or checkpoint: expire the evidence, then retry the same display round from a fresh snapshot, inventory, and index token under a newly bound adversary run. Managed Claude strips the native Task facility, so a Claude provider override for either adversary emits an explicit warning. plan-review-researcher-taskless remains removed, and gobby-agents:spawn_agent remains agent-level blocked. Task #19084, commit a5cca4e29.

Daemon-stop resume consumption is recorded in resume_metadata_json keys daemon_stop_resume_consumed_at / daemon_stop_resume_consumed_by_run_id; the canonical consumed/unconsumed SQL predicates live in src/gobby/storage/daemon_resume_keys.py (daemon_resume_consumed_condition / daemon_resume_unconsumed_condition — non-empty string check, not key presence). Since the durable-session model (#18974/#18995), resume performs ZERO claim work: task claims, worktrees, and clones never leave the parked child session, so the old LocalWorktreeManager.claim_if_available re-claim step in the resume path no longer exists (claim_if_available itself still exists for other spawn paths). Deferred releases happen only on genuine completion or 24h orphan-reaper give-up.

Task #13842 implemented the stage manifest MCP tool surface in commit 54a5a57c0: read tools live in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_stage_read.py and register on gobby-tasks; mutating tools live in _stage_ops.py and register on gobby-tasks-ops; InternalTool metadata now supports optional outputSchema.

The session rendered-messages endpoint returns HTTP 413 when a transcript is too large to render. The raw transcript remains downloadable from /api/sessions/{session_id}/transcript, which streams the live JSONL or decompressed archive with attachment disposition.

Session titles default to `#<session_ref> <Provider>` with title_source="provisional". Each successful full-turn digest may replace and refresh any non-manual title. User renames use title_source="manual" and permanently take precedence. Do not persist prompt-derived heuristic titles or provider-native AI titles. Enforce title/title_source ownership atomically at every storage mutation boundary.

ChatInput provider/model/reasoning selection was previously split out of web/src/components/chat/ChatInput.tsx into useChatInputProviderSelection.ts and ChatInputModelControls.tsx during task #12258. Task #17239 further decomposed ChatInput.tsx: queued attachment upload/delete/retry lifecycle now lives in useChatInputAttachments.ts; queued attachment rendering in ChatInputQueuedFiles.tsx; command palette rendering in ChatCommandPalette.tsx; toolbar/meta controls in ChatInputToolbar.tsx; narrow-layout observation in useChatInputNarrow.ts; and send/stop/PTT primary button behavior/rendering in useChatInputPrimaryAction.ts plus ChatInputPrimaryButton.tsx. ChatInput.tsx remains the composer orchestration layer for input text, submit/key handling, provider selection wiring, model controls, observe overlay, and drag/drop file-path insertion.

The memory stats endpoint (GET /memories/stats) now includes `recent_count` - the number of memories created in the last 24 hours. This was added to `src/gobby/memory/services/maintenance.py` get_stats() and exposed in the MemoryStats TypeScript type. The frontend 24H chip in MemoryFilters uses this server-side count for accuracy.

The shared web ResizeHandle horizontal logic now supports explicit anchor semantics: right-anchored panes keep the original behavior (drag left / ArrowLeft expands), while left-anchored panes like FilesTab must pass horizontalAnchor='left' so drag right / ArrowRight expands the left pane. FilesTab desktop split regression coverage lives in ResizeHandle.test.tsx and FilesTab.test.tsx.

Telegram outbound parity contract (task #17897, commit bbf054180): BaseChannelAdapter exposes supports_typing/send_typing alongside supports_message_edit/edit_message. CommunicationsManager rate-limits both capabilities, and ChatSessionCommsBackend publishes Telegram typing presence at turn start with four-second refresh until completion. TelegramAdapter sends safe HTML for bold/italic/code/links, chunks by Telegram's 4096 visible-character limit while balancing tags, preserves overflow message IDs for later streaming edits, routes image/* attachments through sendPhoto and other files through sendDocument, and formats captions as Telegram HTML.

Codex 0.145 terminal `functions.exec` results may arrive as a `custom_tool_call_output.output` list whose first text item is the exact provider wrapper `Script completed|failed
Wall time <number> seconds
Output:
`, followed by command-output text items. Receipt normalization must trust only that exact first-item wrapper, map completed/failed to the structured boolean outcome, and concatenate only later items as output. A wrapper appearing later in command output must remain unknown to prevent spoofing. Fixed under task #18958.

gwiki research contract now includes the top-level `session_id` JSON output key emitted by `ResearchOutput`. Canonical gobby-cli surfaces were updated in commit ce1438a (`contract.rs`, `crates/gwiki/contract/gwiki.contract.json`, `docs/contracts/gwiki-research.md`), and the Gobby daemon vendored contract was refreshed in commit 1662d5cb3 (`tests/contracts/gwiki.contract.json`).

Claude transcript module boundary: src/gobby/sessions/transcripts/claude.py owns JSONL parsing, session boundaries, usage/model extraction, and parse-event orchestration. src/gobby/sessions/transcripts/claude_records.py owns construction and normalization of Claude message content blocks, including media, tool results, tool uses, thinking, fallback, and unknown blocks.

Grok watchdog transcripts are raw JSON-RPC update envelopes, not normalized transcript records. Classify on params.update.sessionUpdate for methods session/update, _x.ai/session/update, and _x.ai/session_notification. turn_completed is conclusive only with prompt_id, stop_reason, and a valid top-level epoch-seconds timestamp or params._meta.agentTimestampMs epoch-ms fallback; user_message_chunk supersedes obsolete completion. retry_state with type=retrying is diagnostic provider_error_kind=retry/reason=retrying and never a conclusive capacity error. A 2026-07-22 structural-only audit of 234 local updates.jsonl files found numeric top-level and meta timestamps on all observed recognized events, with 16 turn_completed and 4 retry_state records; the checked-in grok-0.1.216 ACP fixture also uses _x.ai/session_notification tool_call_delta_chunk records.

For Gobby 0.5.0 daemon auth, the install-scoped plaintext token lives at $GOBBY_HOME/local_cli_token (default ~/.gobby/local_cli_token) and only its SHA-256 hash is stored in config_store as auth.api_token_hash. The DB hash is authoritative on mismatch; hash-only and mismatch states warn without regenerating. A DB-unreachable `gobby install` writes the 0600 file only, and daemon startup adopts it into config_store immediately after SecretStore.ensure_ready. Implemented by task #17789 in commit 33d755c22.

Plan mode prompt and file handling fixes (session #1840): (1) Plan mode system prompt in chat_session_permissions.py now explicitly tells agent to call ExitPlanMode after writing plan file — previously said 'present a structured plan' without mentioning the approval trigger. (2) _PLAN_FILE_PATTERN regex updated from r'^.*[/\]\.' to r'^(?:.*[/\])?\.': now accepts relative paths like .gobby/plans/foo.md. (3) _read_plan_file() has fallback: if _plan_file_path wasn't tracked (user rejection + retry race), finds most recently modified .md in .gobby/plans/ or .claude/plans/. (4) _BASH_WRITE_PATTERNS regex: added negative lookbehind (?<![0-9&]) so 2>/dev/null and 2>&1 don't trigger write detection false positive.

In gobby-cli/gcode, crates/gcode/src/graph/code_graph/write.rs is close to or over the repo's <1000-line code-file rule. When adding new graph write/query planning logic (e.g. batch planners), extract graph write planning/query helpers to a submodule rather than growing this file further, so the <1000-line rule stays satisfied.

In Gobby's Codex web-chat path, the daemon launches the app-server as `codex app-server`, and sandboxing is applied per thread through the `thread/start` `sandbox` parameter via `CodexSandboxResolver.thread_sandbox_policy`, not through app-server startup flags.

In gobby-cli, gcode index walker code is split with `crates/gcode/src/index/walker.rs` as a thin public facade re-exporting discovery, classification, and type APIs. Child modules live under `crates/gcode/src/index/walker/`: `types.rs` defines `FileClassification` and `DiscoveryOptions`; `discovery.rs` handles `discover_files`, `discover_files_with_options`, walker setup, hidden allowlist discovery, and de-duplication; `classification.rs` handles `classify_file`, explicit-file visibility, content-language labeling, and safe text checks; `hidden.rs` handles `.gobby`/`.github` hidden metadata allowlists and generated wiki metadata filtering; `generated.rs` handles generated/minified JavaScript bundle filtering. Unit tests are split under `crates/gcode/src/index/walker/tests/` into `discovery.rs`, `classification.rs`, `hidden.rs`, and `generated.rs`, with shared helpers in `walker/tests.rs`. Add future walker logic or tests to the relevant child module instead of growing `walker.rs`.

In Gobby task artifacts, base_commit_sha requires an active isolation artifact family. When persisting a refreshed base SHA for a reused worktree, use set_artifacts_atomic with worktree_path and worktree_id (and clear clone_path/clone_id if switching families) so artifact constraints are satisfied atomically.

Gobby build cleanup defers dirty descendant worktrees by default and skips branch cleanup when artifacts are deferred. Deletion of dirty descendants requires explicit delete_dirty_worktrees=True; preserve local changes whenever the worktree HEAD differs from the task's integrated closed_commit_sha.

Session registration with project_id=None normalizes to PERSONAL_PROJECT_ID (_personal) in src/gobby/storage/sessions/_crud.py and _discovery.py. sessions.project_id is required/FK-backed, so projectless public inputs should not be stored as NULL or an empty string; sequence locking uses the normalized storage project id.

Test pattern for HTTP route tests requiring FK constraints: Use the global project_manager fixture from tests/conftest.py to create a test project, then pass project.id to task creation. The tests/servers/conftest.py provides create_http_server() helper. Patch get_project_context at its source module (gobby.utils.project_context.get_project_context) not at the import site.

ActivityPanel pipeline execution steps are rendered by PipelinesTab through web/src/components/shared/executions/execution-utils.tsx. StepDisplay owns card/timeline layouts, and StepStatusIcon is the centralized status glyph and accessible-label renderer; keep future pipeline step status accessibility changes in this shared path.

Transcript rendering is decomposed around stable public imports in `gobby.sessions.transcript_renderer`: dataclasses live in `transcript_render_models.py`, tool classification/result metadata in `transcript_tool_metadata.py`, protocol/context tag parsing in `transcript_protocol.py`, and ParsedMessage block assembly in `transcript_render_blocks.py`. Keep external callers importing public APIs from `transcript_renderer.py`; use the focused modules for internal maintenance.

Fire-and-forget hook coroutines scheduled on a running asyncio loop should use gobby.hooks.background_tasks.create_background_task. The helper strongly retains tasks until completion, removes completed tasks, ignores cancellation, and retrieves/logs unexpected task exceptions.

Auto-Task Workflow: Activate with session_task variable (not assigned_task_id): activate_workflow(name='auto-task', variables={session_task: '#1234'}). Meeseeks agent pattern is deprecated and no longer in use. The call_tool MCP proxy uses `arguments` parameter (not `args`).

Storage row factories in Gobby should preserve PostgreSQL JSONB fields that arrive already decoded as dict/list containers and only json.loads string values. MCP Tool.input_schema remains a dict contract: pre-decoded dict schemas are valid, but pre-decoded list schemas should be rejected as invalid tool schemas.

Epic #18705's receipt-centered task-close design was superseded before 0.5.0 by epic #19101. Current leaf closure is an ordered checklist: criteria and changes_summary; linked commits when task-attributed edits exist; no dirty task-attributed paths; category-aware clean validation derived at close time from the claiming and closing session transcripts; and one bounded LLM criteria-coherence verdict. Transcript validation becomes stale only when a later task-attributed file edit occurs; commits preserve it. preview=true is the conditional-close contract: blocked evaluation is read-only, while ready evaluation enters a mutation-only phase in the same call; that phase rechecks the lock, commits, and dirty paths without rerunning the LLM. Receipt storage/admission/projection, manual evidence tools, completion-readiness rules, and validation_epoch were deleted. Infrastructure failures fail closed with 15-120 second backoff and escalation at five. Do not restore pre-#18666 validation_tool_loop or validation_coverage machinery.

Session detail transcript now reuses chat page components (MessageItem, ToolCallCard) via a transcriptAdapter (web/src/components/sessions/transcriptAdapter.ts). The adapter's sessionMessagesToChatMessages() function transforms SessionMessage[] to ChatMessage[] by: (1) grouping tool-use messages into the preceding assistant message's toolCalls array, (2) skipping user-role tool_result protocol messages, (3) parsing assistant JSON tool_use arrays into ToolCall objects, (4) extracting server_name from double-underscore naming (mcp__gobby__X → gobby). Hook feedback messages ('Stop hook feedback:', 'PreToolUse hook', 'PostToolUse hook', 'UserPromptSubmit hook') must be classified with role: 'system' (not role: 'user') for correct transcript rendering—system shows grey System label, user incorrectly shows blue You label. An isHookFeedback() detector function identifies these messages. A `.h` routes to `objc` only with a sibling `.m`/`.mm` or Obj-C directives (`@interface`, `@protocol`, `@import`), routes to `cpp` on C++ header keywords (`class`, `namespace`, `template`), and otherwise defaults to `c`. `.mm` deliberately uses the Objective-C grammar because it inherits C/C++ constructs while exposing Objective-C `@interface`/`@implementation` and message sends. Incremental session processing snapshots parser state only for Codex and hydrates that snapshot after parse/filter or downstream batch failure, while other parsers avoid snapshot overhead.

Terminal Codex (0.144.x rollout JSONL) records a nested functions.exec outer call as response_item custom_tool_call/custom_tool_call_output and may emit the yielded-cell wrapper as a raw string. Correlation is definitive only when the wrapper's first nonblank line exactly matches `Script running with cell ID <id>`; appended wall-time and output lines are allowed. Subsequent functions.wait records use standard function_call/function_call_output envelopes with JSON in `arguments`. CodexTranscriptParser shares envelope classification across rendering and nested reconciliation, accepts input/arguments parity, persists call-id and cell-id correlation in parser snapshots, and emits exactly one synthetic Bash AFTER_TOOL per final structured result with identity `outer_call_id:result_index`, an explicit cmd/command, and an integer exit_code/exitCode. Yielded and repeated-wait chunks, prose, generic MCP lifecycle records, and outcome-free payloads remain unknown or history-only. Corrected in task #18663, commit 5a83630c78bf566af73a354ed31ed273fdf6e1f8.

`useTmuxSessions` models create, attach, and detach as one generation-scoped `PendingRequest` union. It suppresses concurrent sends, correlates result/error frames by request_id and connection generation, and gives each request a 10-second deadline that clears pending/loading state and surfaces an error. Uncorrelated session-list and kill-result frames must not clear loading while a request is pending. Socket close and unmount cancel the deadline. Creation exposes `createdSession` as `{session_name, socket}`; `TerminalTab` waits until the session-created list refresh contains that socket-qualified key, consumes it once, then selects it so the existing attach state machine attaches. Hardened through task #19000, commit 66c1afb54.

The bundled gobby SKILL.md is a thin router contract. Bare `/gobby` and `/gobby help` show dynamic help from discover_core_skills(); `/gobby <skill> [args]`, `/gobby skill <skill> [args]`, and legacy `/gobby:<skill> [args]` route through gobby-skills get_skill without inlining skill bodies. In Codex-facing examples, use `$gobby <skill> ...`. Router directives fetch only the skill; trailing command text remains in the prompt and must not be duplicated as `User arguments:`.

The admin restart endpoint in src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py follows this lifecycle: evaluate service-manager mode via asyncio.to_thread, persist the restart shutdown source, request runner shutdown or schedule process shutdown, then spawn the detached restart helper. The restart lock is released on failures before shutdown initiation and retained once shutdown begins to guard duplicate restart requests.

Agent-run completion must not treat `SESSION_END` alone as success when an inline agent step workflow still has an enabled instance whose current step has not satisfied its exit condition. Check this before session-end cleanup removes workflow-instance state, and fail the run with an incomplete-step diagnostic. Use the shared workflow-finished predicate for this decision.

Codex-managed agents are separate CLI/TUI processes in tmux. Graceful exit uses the native matcherless SessionEnd hook with `ghook --gobby-owned --cli=codex --type=SessionEnd --enqueue-only` and timeout 3; enqueue-only durably writes the inbox envelope and returns, while replay performs cleanup. Forced kills, crashes, timeouts, and `end_agent_run` use explicit terminal cleanup and never synthesize Stop or SessionEnd. Passive-wait detection must inspect both outer hook names and call_tool inner names, including Codex-normalized `collaborationwait_agent`. Lifecycle envelopes carry trusted terminal context and run identity; invalid managed terminal identities are acknowledged and discarded before terminal side effects.

Observability preference: remove Gobby-private trace persistence, API, WebSocket, and UI. OTLP export monitors the Gobby daemon only, configured through standard `OTEL_*` values in `~/.gobby/bootstrap.yaml`; Gobby does not ingest user-application spans, ship a shared application Collector setup, or add cross-service trace propagation. Metrics remain a Prometheus scrape surface backed by OpenTelemetry instruments, and the operator-managed OpenTelemetry Collector filelog pipeline remains the log-shipping path.

Bundled agent YAML must use current AgentDefinitionBody fields: put model-facing text in `instructions` rather than `prompt`, and represent `skills` as a dictionary of named lists (for example `skills.baseline` and `skills.tool_allowlist`), not a bare list. Deprecated agent tombstones such as conductor, developer, and pipeline-worker must retain non-empty instructions containing lifecycle semantic terms required by bundled-agent validation.

CodexAppServerTextGenerateAdapter enforces its configured generation deadline through _generate_with_deadline, wrapping the app-server turn in asyncio.wait_for. CodexAppServerClient.run_turn also treats active-turn terminal notifications as failures: it subscribes to turn/failed and matching thread/closed, yields the terminal event, then raises RuntimeError so text-generation callers can advance to fallback instead of hanging.

The expired-isolation reaper must execute every git worktree remove, worktree prune, and branch deletion with subprocess cwd set to the recorded project.repo_path. _run_git_command requires keyword-only cwd, and the outside-daemon-CWD integration test asserts all three invocations use that repository.

Task #18223 established reused-worktree cleanup ownership: explicit spawn reuse is persisted as initial_variables.reused_worktree in the agent run resume snapshot; post_terminal_cleanup forwards that worktree ID to build artifact cleanup, which defers it with cleanup_reason reused_worktree_preserved. Worktree lifecycle events now live in gobby.worktrees.events so both build cleanup and MCP worktree tools emit the same worktree_deleted event without a build↔MCP import cycle. Commit d86b8785a.

Gobby build coordination convention: `gobby build` is expected to run autonomously without a coordinator. A build coordinator should monitor agents and debug/fix build-system issues that prevent autonomy. Manual nudges such as resuming dispatch are acceptable only after identifying or fixing the issue that made the nudge necessary.

Genuine hook/transcript activity may revive an expired terminal session through `revive_expired_terminal_session`; that activity-specific reconciliation uses machine/tmux-socket/pane identity and immutable creation order to prevent delayed historical activity from reviving a superseded row. Passive liveness and tmux title repair use the separate foreground-process-group contract from task #19318 / commit dc27207bd: expired/deleted rows never become owners from tmux existence, and only an eligible row whose validated CLI process group matches the terminal foreground PGID can own or rename the pane.

Task #17659 / commit c08fa44bc established dispatch skill-composition validation. inspect_skill_composition resolves AgentDefinitionBody.step_variables.required_skills plus SpawnAgentAction.additional_skills through LocalSkillManager project/global precedence, blocks unknown or disabled skills before launcher-session creation and agent spawn, and reports a deterministic allowed_tools union. explain_dispatch uses the same report and failure reason.

As of task #18564 (commit 73d44dd70), generation routes use semantic names throughout current Rust source: `one_shot` for single completion and `tool_loop` for agentic generation. gcore module is `ai::generation::one_shot`; gwiki routing lives in `commands::generation_routes` with `resolve_tool_loop_generator` and `run_agentic_generation`; gcode uses `ToolLoopResult` and `FrontmatterToolLoop`. CodeWiki failure dumps now use `_meta/tool_loop/` and `GOBBY_CODEWIKI_TOOL_LOOP_DUMP_DIR` directly, with no legacy path or environment fallback.

web/src/lib/chatMessageMapping.ts pairs persisted tool results only with pending tool calls, searching newest-first so duplicate tool_use_id values cannot overwrite completed calls. An unmatched result is rendered as a system message and marks the latest pending call errored, preventing a permanent calling spinner without silently re-pairing the payload.

MCP action tool wrapping pattern: To expose workflow actions as MCP tools, create thin wrappers using @registry.tool() decorator in the relevant registry module. Pattern: (1) Import the workflow action function, (2) Create async wrapper that captures managers via closure, (3) Handle None manager with early error return, (4) Call action, check for errors, return {success: True, **result}. For new tool groups, create a register_*_tools() function in a separate _actions.py file and call it from the _factory.py. Wire new dependencies through registries.py setup_internal_registries(). See sessions/_actions.py and memory.py lines 606-678 for examples.

Gobby repo now documents daemon/web consumption of `gwiki --format json` in `docs/guides/gwiki-daemon-web.md`, including the `GwikiGateway`-only boundary, consumed command JSON fields, source lifecycle contracts, URL batch ingest, source refresh, timeout/error behavior, and operation classifications.

Terminal web placement contract after task #19155 / commit b4f176ba8: ActivityPanelTabs still registers `terminal` so stored actions and `gobby:show-activity-tab` recognize it, but useActivityPanel treats it as a bottom-dock command and never side-panel content. ChatPage renders TerminalDock below the chat when `terminalOpen`; the dock owns expand/collapse/close and embeds TerminalTab. TerminalTab/wterm remain lazy assets. The same commit fixed live PTY operation by forcing TERM=xterm-256color for attach clients, signaling SIGWINCH after TIOCSWINSZ, and owning container-to-grid fit when wterm's initial measurement is zero.

Onboarding implementation: `_personal` is backed by `~/.gobby/personal`, `/gobby intro` is bundled as `src/gobby/install/shared/skills/intro/SKILL.md`, fresh non-resume non-spawned sessions can inject `~/.gobby/personal/USER.md` via `user_profile_content`, and obsolete PostgreSQL install modes are rejected through the bootstrap/config validation path instead of normalized to docker.

`blocked` means unresolved dependencies and must not be used for dispatch-failure escalation. Dispatch recovery uses the first-class `Task.is_escalated` / `tasks.is_escalated` state with an escalation reason; state projections and transition guards must not infer escalation from legacy status or timestamps. Failure recovery remains status-aware, and close of an escalated task requires the current explicit override/validation path when applicable.

As of commit 93e7e3e3e (task #18999), gobby-core direct text-generation target resolution falls back to conventional environment API keys only when both the provider label and parsed api_base identify that provider's exact official HTTPS host: anthropic→api.anthropic.com/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, openai→api.openai.com/OPENAI_API_KEY, openrouter→openrouter.ai/OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and groq→api.groq.com/GROQ_API_KEY. Configured API keys remain authoritative. Missing/custom providers, missing or malformed bases, HTTP bases, and custom OpenAI-compatible hosts never receive ambient provider keys, preventing Bearer credential leakage.

Task #17881 established the editorial contract for Gobby's original 17 bundled language skills (c, cpp, csharp, dart, elixir, go, java, javascript, json, kotlin, php, python, ruby, rust, swift, typescript, yaml). Their SKILL.md indexes stay at or below 100 lines, route detail to existing references, use `## Concurrency` as the shared concurrency heading, keep short API Design guidance inline for Go/JavaScript/Python/Rust/TypeScript, and include one language-specific `Diagnostic hook:` warning against bypassing compiler/analyzer/schema feedback. Commit f6e1378ae reduced the family from 1,937 to 1,374 lines and added tests/skills/test_language_skill_editorial.py.

Codex web-chat stream_codex_turn now bounds notification polling with a 600-second monotonic deadline and checks CodexAppServerClient.is_connected each cycle, emitting an error and DoneEvent when the shared app-server disconnects or the deadline expires.

PostgreSQL is authoritative for tasks and memories. Pre-push/remote-push context writes deterministic atomic JSONL backups of current live scoped rows only; normal local daemon and build activity must not export them. Restore is explicit, validates the complete file, and only upserts backup rows that win by updated_at.

Managed helpers resolve ~/.gobby/bin before PATH. Install/status/updater logic first accepts an installed local binary at or above its managed version floor; GitHub releases are used only for missing or stale helpers. The daemon background updater uses GitHub release artifacts and leaves binaries untouched when release assets are unavailable or fail the version floor.

list_rules MCP tool supports brief=True parameter (added in #9074). When brief=True, returns only name/event/group/enabled per rule instead of the full summary (which includes id, description, effect, when, priority, source, tags). This reduces token output from ~20k to a fraction. Implementation: _rule_brief() helper in src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/workflows/_rules.py, wired through __init__.py registry.

The .claude/hooks/hook_dispatcher.py (and .gemini/hooks/hook_dispatcher.py) are symlinks to src/gobby/install/shared/hooks/hook_dispatcher.py. If these are broken, hooks fail and the agent can enter an unrecoverable deadlock where tool use is blocked. Always update/recreate the symlink BEFORE deleting old target files.

During #12761 PostgreSQL migration coordination, #14891 fixed a gobby build merge-worker contract bug: clean merge-worker prompts may include verification, and because merge-workers record merge results themselves, gobby-merge:verify_in_worktree must be allowed in the merge-worker merge step before record_merge_result. Commit 5cedc0361 updates merge-worker, merge-orchestrator, and merge-expert guidance plus regression tests so verification can run before a successful merge result is recorded.

RulesTabData.detailToDraft is the shared conversion boundary for rule form saves, YAML rendering, and rule duplication. Preserve fetched definition-only fields in RuleDraft.extra while filtering API metadata such as id, source, project_id, and has_template_update.

Credential-backed Codex Responses endpoints use an endpoint-specific CODEX_HOME at `<gobby_home>/codex-endpoints/<endpoint_name>`, exclude GOBBY_CODEX_ENDPOINT_API_KEY from spawned shells, and set features.shell_snapshot=false so endpoint credentials and provider configuration cannot leak across endpoints or persist in Codex shell state. Endpoint selectors remain UI-facing while canonical model IDs go on the wire; reasoning effort resolves through execution_provider=codex, including spawned-agent startup validation. Endpoint-specific app-server homes were enforced in task #19001 / commit 919289a3e.

Gobby's Rust migration plan lives at docs/plans/rust-migration-epic.md (refined 2026-07-10, commit f6f6b7318). Incremental strangler migration: Python remains the public daemon/front door on :60887/:60888; the gobby-daemon Rust sidecar (binary gobbyd, crate crates/gdaemon) runs on internal port 60890 (NOT 60889 — that is the dev web UI; 60891 is the managed Postgres hub). Contract fixtures live in tests/contracts/http/, with compare mode -> opt-in delegation -> route-scoped rollback gates. First wave (post-0.5.0-ship): M1-M9 milestones from sidecar shell + health/config reads through reduced GET /api/tasks. Second wave: external-MCP transport multiplexer behind Python's ToolProxyService front door; internal MCP servers port only after the Rust multiplexer exists. Phase 2 gcore foundation extraction is complete. The Rust workspace is crates/ in the gobby monorepo (gobby-cli repo retired, epics #17469/#17470 closed).

The Sessions activity running-agents poll is handled by useRunningAgents in SessionsTab.entries.ts. Its supported payload shapes are a bare array or an object with an agents array. Poll and payload failures preserve the last successful agent list, set fetchError, and SessionsEntryList displays that error above retained entries.

The gobby-agents skill documents agent lifecycle, querying, definition CRUD, messaging, and command tools. Refer to the current bundled skill under the shared workflows/skills installation tree rather than the retired direct `shared/skills` path; use MCP schema discovery for the authoritative current tool list.

Agent terminal lifecycle cleanup is coordinated by AgentCleanupHandler but owned by dedicated terminal delivery and terminal resource-cleanup modules. Managed tmux termination must use the centralized capture-and-kill path so terminal intent and scrollback are persisted before serialized tmux teardown and terminal-state updates.

Managed native binary freshness treats a floor-satisfied installed binary as status up_to_date when GitHub release resolution fails, while recording latest_version=None and last_error=str(exception). This distinguishes operational safety from a successfully verified latest release. Implemented for task #16780 in commit e605f40f9.

Gobby build plan expansion contract: approved implementation-plan expansion must emit only development-forward leaf categories (`code`, `config`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`). `research`, `planning`, and `manual` remain valid for direct task creation but are rejected from Plan-Coverage Contract manifests and compiled expansion specs to avoid dispatching discovery-stage agents from approved plans. Successful merge cleanup should delete inactive merged worktrees immediately; active-agent-owned worktrees are still deferred.

In gobby-cli gwiki, ask synthesis normalizes model output at `record_synthesis` before citation checking or rendering. `strip_leading_model_narration` removes leading first-person process/status sentences (e.g. patterns like 'I'm checking ... I've got ...'), but preserves the original text if stripping would leave no answer. `synthesis_system` also asks for answer-only output with no process/search/retrieval narration. Regression coverage lives in `commands::ask::tests::synthesis_strips_leading_model_narration_before_recording`, `synthesis_system_requests_answer_only_output`, and the integration test `crates/gwiki/tests/cli_output.rs::ask_llm_text_output_strips_model_narration`, which runs the actual `gwiki ask --llm --require-ai --ai direct --format text` binary path against an isolated topic plus a one-shot OpenAI-compatible loopback server returning the narration prefix.

Project convention clarification for Gobby: the 1,000-line monolith principle applies to code files. Oversized code files may still be touched when needed for the current task, but the agent must ensure a suitable refactor task exists rather than forcing that refactor into the current bug. Test, docs, and content files should not block work solely for exceeding 1,000 lines.

CodexAppServerClient is now a public facade in src/gobby/adapters/codex_impl/client.py. Implementation logic lives in focused helper modules: client_lifecycle.py for app-server subprocess start/stop, client_rpc.py for JSON-RPC send/read/incoming request dispatch, client_api.py for thread/model/turn/auth/account methods, and client_notifications.py for notification handlers and enrichment. Keep the CodexAppServerClient import path and facade private methods stable for tests and callers.

RuleEngine active-rule filtering now resolves the current `_agent_type` agent definition at evaluation time and checks each rule row with `rule_matches_agent`; `_active_rule_names` is compatibility/debug metadata only when the agent definition cannot be resolved. Session activation reconciliation refreshes `_active_rule_names` opportunistically. `auto-compact-after-task-close` now queues background `gobby-sessions:compact_self` for terminal sessions too and de-dupes repeated close-task after-tool events using `_auto_compact_after_task_close_queued_for`.

Deferred hook memory recall is owned by src/gobby/hooks/memory_recall_dispatcher.py. MemoryRecallDispatcher owns configuration/session-variable checks, per-turn scheduling and deduplication, payload delivery, background futures, cancellation, and five-second sync/async draining; HookManager only schedules it at BEFORE_AGENT and delegates shutdown.

Storage contract: LocalPlanManager.create_plan validates root_task_ref before inserting and generates an implementation plan's coverage manifest inside the same database transaction. If manifest evaluation or writing raises, the plan registry insert/update must roll back so the database never advertises a plan without its required manifest.

Durable project constraints: task descriptions and validation criteria must commit to one implementation approach and must not offer A-or-B alternatives or delegate key decisions to the executing agent. PostgreSQL, Qdrant, and FalkorDB are required Gobby services; PostgreSQL is authoritative for tasks and memories. Legacy SQLite code, dialect branches, fallbacks, and DDL should be removed rather than maintained.

Generated Git hooks keep code indexing and codewiki refresh behavior aligned. The daemon coalesces refreshes per project root, honors wiki.codewiki_on_commit, generates codewiki output in the project gobby-wiki vault by default, and indexes changed documentation once.

Implementation plan parsing now treats missing or literal `unknown` Plan IDs as draft-mode warnings and expansion/strict-mode errors for `PlanKind.implementation`; `PlanKind.strategy` remains unaffected. Validation payloads expose `warnings`, and missing/unknown identity returns the same message in `errors` and `warnings` to block planner/adversary spawn before `covers:unknown:*` manifests can validate.

Current Gobby session status counts intentionally reuse `_build_session_filters(project_id, None, None)`, so `SessionManager.count_by_status()` excludes deleted sessions by default just like normal session list/count queries. Do not bypass shared session filters for default status aggregates; query deleted rows explicitly when a deleted-inclusive audit is required.

Web chat stream finalization uses ChatStreamEventState.completed to distinguish a fully handled DoneEvent from cancellation, backend errors, client disconnects, and generators that end without DoneEvent. ChatStreamingMixin._stream_chat_response persists accumulated AssistantContentBlocks and sets the DB session status to paused for every incomplete exit; DoneEvent already performs both operations and sets completed only after its persistence finishes.

Python test-quality SLEEP_IN_TEST detection in src/gobby/test_quality/_analyzer_python.py is import-aware: canonical time.sleep and asyncio.sleep calls plus aliases imported from time/asyncio are recognized. Module aliases apply across tests, function-local aliases stay scoped to that test, and arbitrary object.sleep methods or unimported bare sleep calls are ignored.

Gobby build merge/autonomy fix: reused agent worktrees must be clean and rebased onto the current local base branch before respawn/review. The fix is in src/gobby/agents/worktree_reuse.py and is called from WorktreeIsolationHandler and spawn_agent worktree_id reuse. Also, gobby-merge predict_conflicts now defaults omitted target_branch to each worktree.base_branch instead of main, and merge-orchestrator prompt instructs using base_branch as target unless explicit. This prevents PostgreSQL epic task worktrees based on 0.4.7 from being surveyed/merged against main.
